No other service joins it, no service uses `network_mode: service:<a member>` or `pid: service:<a member>` (the companion included), and no service of a template with an `identity_headers` companion (either kind) uses `network_mode: host` (it would send from the host's addresses, the trust network's gateway included) or `pid: host`. The caller secret's variable (`caller_secret.env`) may be interpolated (`${VAR…}`, `$VAR`, nested defaults included) only in the companion's own service. Since the Hub refuses foreign network names (§3), nothing outside the project can join it either, so the app may trust identity headers from that network's addresses: no IP or subnet is pinned, the app reads the prefix from its own interface at start and refuses to start when it is ambiguous — the default route must be on portcullis-proxy and the trust interface must carry only its connected prefix (Grafana: `grafana/portcullis/trust.sh` adds that prefix without its own address — a data source pointing at the app itself —, the bridge gateway — the host's side, which host processes and host-network containers come from; Docker's builtin IPAM's first address — and the network and broadcast addresses to `GF_AUTH_PROXY_WHITELIST`, next to Traefik's). The companion reaches the app by a name ending in `-internal` on the trust network (an exactly `{internal: true}` network, §3): on `portcullis-proxy` the app's service name is shared by every instance.
- **`ai-providers.json`** (the AI page's data file, Hub → template). For an `ai.chat` instance the Hub writes `<appfiles>/<instance-id>/ai-providers/ai-providers.json` (mode 0640, directory 0750, atomic, like the data files of §13.7; delivery unit `file:ai-providers`) and bind-mounts its directory read-only at `ai.chat.file.mount` in `ai.chat.file.service`:

    ```json
    {
      "version": 1,
      "instance": "ai-chat",
      "providers": [
        {
          "name": "ollama-gpu",
          "label": "Ollama on the office GPU",
          "kind": "openai_compatible",
          "base_url": "http://gpu.lan:11434/v1",
          "region": "",
          "instance_name": "",
          "api_version": "",
          "deployments": {},
          "models": {"fetch": false, "list": ["llama3.3:70b", "qwen3:32b"]},
          "credentials": "admin",
          "env": {"key": "PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_OLLAMA_GPU_KEY"}
        }
      ]
    }
    ```

    - one entry per provider the instance selected (§15.12), sorted by `name`; every field always present (`""`, `{}` or `[]` when the kind has no such field); `deployments` maps an Azure deployment to its model; `models.fetch` only where the kind allows it (`litellm`, `openai_compatible`, `openai`);
    - `credentials` is `admin` or `per_person` (each person enters their own key in the chat app; the Hub stores none);
    - `env` maps each of the kind's secret fields whose value is set to the **name** of the variable that holds it (`PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_<NAME>_<FIELD>`, §15.12); `{}` for `per_person`. The file **never** holds a secret value. The template renders its own configuration from it (the `ai-chat` template's `config` init service writes `librechat.yaml` with env references such as `apiKey: "${PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_OLLAMA_GPU_KEY}"`), so no secret is written into a file either.

Example (`gitea`, abridged; hooks in §13.8):

```yaml
# manifest.yaml (excerpt)
ai:
  mcp:
    - name: gitea
      label: Gitea
      kind: companion
      service: gitea-mcp
      port: 8080
      router: gitea                 # https://<gitea host>/mcp
      upstream: official
      source: https://gitea.com/gitea/gitea-mcp
      protocol: ["2026-07-28", "2025-11-25"]
      modes: [read_only, read_write]
      default_mode: read_write
      identity:
        mode: app_token
        format: "token {credential}"
        mint: mcp-mint
        revoke: mcp-revoke
        scopes:
          read_only:  [read:repository, read:issue, read:user]
          read_write: [write:repository, write:issue, read:user]
      tools:
        writes:  ["*_write", "create_*", "update_*", "merge_*", "delete_*"]
        confirm: ["delete_*", "repo_write:delete"]
        never:   []
```

```yaml
# compose.yml (excerpt)
services:
  gitea-mcp:                         # no Traefik labels, not on portcullis-proxy
    image: docker.gitea.com/gitea-mcp-server:<tag>@sha256:<digest>
    environment:
      GITEA_READONLY: ${PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_GITEA:-true}
    networks: [default]
```

### 3.3 VPN-only access: the `vpn:` block — NEW (VPN)

A template that is a VPN app (a mesh, a WireGuard server) may declare a `vpn:` block. The block lets the admin wire an instance of it as a **VPN provider** (§11.7, §16): a path through which people's devices reach VPN-only apps. Installing such a template doesn't make it a provider; the admin turns that on per instance. The templates repo's schema, `tests/validate.py` and the Hub's `ValidateVPN` implement exactly the rules below, with the same refusal texts in the same order. The Hub skips a template that fails them.

- **Optional.** A template without a `vpn:` block can't be a provider. Any template's instance can still be made VPN-only (§11.7).
- **Fields** (unknown keys refused; `control_routers` and `identity.refresh` are optional):
    - **`label`** (string): a single line, 1–64 characters. Shown on Settings → VPN, the instance and the device lists.
    - **`ranges`** (array): 1–8 IPv4 prefixes the app hands to its clients, each between /8 and /30, with no overlaps among them. Each entry is a literal prefix or exactly `{{setting:<key>}}`, where `<key>` is a string option of the template with `format: cidr` (§13.2). The Hub resolves each `{{setting:…}}` to the instance's value; an unset or invalid value, or ranges that overlap after resolving, refuse the wiring (§11.7).
    - **`ingress`** (object): how the provider's traffic reaches the edge (§16).
        - **`service`**: a service of `compose.yml` with no `network_mode`, not a job (§3), not a `kind: companion` AI service (§3.2), and with no Traefik router and no `traefik.*` label: the gateway is reached only over `portcullis-vpn`, never through Traefik.
        - **`proxy_protocol`**: exactly `v2`, the only value.
    - **`identity`** (object): how the provider's device map is built (§16).
        - **`source: hook`**: **`hook`** names a hook of the template with exactly `when: [vpn]` (§13.8), and **`owner`** is `oidc_sub` (the hook's owners are Keycloak user ids) or `username` (LLDAP usernames).
        - **`source: static`**: no `hook` and no `owner`. The admin assigns addresses to people on the instance's VPN tab (§11.7). The map never goes stale, but the device's existence isn't proven (doctor `vpn_static_mapping`, §14.5).
        - **`refresh`**: how often the Hub runs the identity hook, `15s`–`10m`, default `60s`.
    - **`dns`** (object): exactly one of:
        - **`hook`**: a hook of the template with exactly `when: [vpn]` that receives the A records to apply (§13.8 `op: dns`);
        - **`manual: true`**: the instance's VPN tab shows the A records to configure by hand; doctor `vpn_dns_manual` (Info) stays until the admin acknowledges it (§11.7).
    - **`control_routers`** (array, optional, default `[]`): host routers (§3.1) of the template that the provider's clients need to connect (coordination, signal, relay); each router's rule is `Host(…)` alone or `Host(…) && PathPrefix(…)`. A router of an admin UI the template marks (`auth.admin_paths`, or any router of a `group_admin` template) is refused. The Hub renders these on `websecure,vpnsecure` whatever the reach or mode, so clients can always reach the control plane (§5).
- **The ingress namespace.** The services with `network_mode: service:<ingress.service>` (chains of `service:` followed) share the ingress service's network namespace. Besides the ingress service itself, the only service allowed in it is one running core's forwarder image `ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-forwarder`, pinned by digest (§16).
    - **The same checks apply to every service in it**: not a job, not an AI companion, no Traefik router and no `traefik.*` label, no published `ports`.
    - **Host namespaces.** With a `vpn:` block, no service of the template uses `pid: host`. `network_mode: host` is allowed only on a service outside the ingress namespace that has no Traefik router and no `traefik.*` label; the ingress service, the services sharing its namespace and every routed service never use it.
    - **The gateway's own privileges.** The ingress service and every service in its namespace: not `privileged`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `cap_add` only `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, no `devices` and no `device_cgroup_rules` (the gateway runs userspace), and no `pid`, `ipc` or `volumes_from` key at all. No other service joins a member's `pid` or `ipc` namespace (`service:<member>`) or names a member in `volumes_from`.
    - **The gateway's mounts.** A member binds only the template's own files under `./templates/<id>/`, read-only. Its volumes are the template's own: declared, with no `external`, `name`, `driver` or `driver_opts`. A volume (or bind) a member mounts read-write is the gateway's alone, mounted by no other service; a volume all members mount read-only may be shared with other services as a hand-over.
- **Mounts and volumes of every service (VPN templates).** With a `vpn:` block, on every service of the template:
    - bind sources start with `./`, have no `..` segment and no backslash, and never resolve outside `templates/<id>/` through a symlink;
    - a short-syntax volume source is a `./` bind or a declared volume;
    - no read-write bind of `.`, `./templates` or the template's own files (the template's files are read-only for every service);
    - no volume name of a single letter (it would read as a Windows drive);
    - no top-level volume sets `name`, `external`, `driver` or `driver_opts`: every volume is a plain `<project>_<key>` volume.
- **Compose shape (VPN templates).** `compose.yml` uses no YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys, and a service answers to an `-internal` name (service name, hostname, container name or alias) on the project's `default` network only.
- **Providers keep the client's address.** A provider must hand the edge each client's own tunnel address (in PROXY v2, from its own node or through the forwarder): the device ↔ person binding is built on it. A VPN app whose gateway can't preserve the client's source address can't be a provider, which is why NetBird and plain WireGuard aren't supported today.
- **The `vpn` hook trigger.** A hook with `when: [vpn]` must be named by `identity.hook` or `dns.hook`, and `vpn` can't be combined with another trigger (like `ai`, §13.8). A `vpn` hook is never a `reload.hook` or an option's `delivery.hook`, and the settings engine never runs it.
- **Validation refusals** (these exact texts, shared by the Hub and `tests/validate.py` through the vectors file `vpn_vectors.json`; `<n>` in the ingress texts is the ingress service or a service in its namespace, `<m>` such a member, `<s>` any service of the template):
    - `vpn.label: a single line of 1–64 characters`
    - `vpn.ranges: 1–8 IPv4 prefixes`
    - `vpn.ranges[<i>]: <v> is not an IPv4 prefix between /8 and /30`
    - `vpn.ranges: <a> overlaps <b>`
    - `vpn.ranges[<i>]: {{setting:<k>}} must name a cidr setting`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> is not a service of compose.yml`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> has network_mode`
    - `vpn: service <n> uses network_mode: host`
    - `vpn: service <n> uses pid: host`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> shares <s>'s network namespace: only the pinned ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-forwarder image may`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> is a job`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> is an AI companion`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> has a Traefik router`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> publishes ports`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> is privileged`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> must set cap_drop: [ALL]`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> adds <cap>: a VPN gateway may add only NET_BIND_SERVICE`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> has <key>: a VPN gateway runs userspace (no devices)` (`<key>` is `devices` or `device_cgroup_rules`)
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> sets <pid|ipc>: a VPN gateway keeps its own pid and ipc namespaces`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <n> uses volumes_from: a VPN gateway mounts no other service's volumes`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <m> mounts <entry>: unresolvable (a VPN gateway's mounts are literal)`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <m> mounts <entry>: a VPN gateway binds only the template's own files (./templates/<id>/…), read-only`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: a VPN template's binds start with ./ and have no .. segment`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: a VPN template's volume names are longer than one letter`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <m> mounts volume <v>: a VPN gateway's volumes are the template's own (declared, with no external, name, driver or driver_opts)`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> shares the <pid|ipc> namespace of <m>`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> volumes_from <entry>: the mode must be ro or rw`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts the volumes of <m> (volumes_from)`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: unresolvable (a VPN template's mounts are literal)`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: a VPN template's short-syntax sources are ./ binds or declared volumes`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: in a VPN template the template's files are read-only for every service`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts volume <v>, which <m> mounts read-write`
    - `vpn.ingress.service: <s> mounts <entry>: it resolves outside templates/<id>/ (a symlink)`
    - `vpn: service <s> answers to <name> on network <net>: a VPN template's -internal aliases are on the default network only`
    - `vpn: volume <v>: a VPN template's volume names are longer than one letter`
    - `vpn: volume <v> sets <key>: a VPN template's volumes are plain <project>_<key> volumes`
    - `compose.yml: a VPN template uses no YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys`
    - `vpn.ingress.proxy_protocol: only v2`
    - `vpn.identity.hook: <h> is not a hook with exactly when: [vpn]`
    - `vpn.identity.owner: oidc_sub or username`
    - `vpn.identity: source static takes no hook or owner`
    - `vpn.identity.source: hook or static`
    - `vpn.identity.refresh: between 15s and 10m`
    - `vpn.dns: exactly one of hook and manual: true`
    - `vpn.dns.hook: <h> is not a hook with exactly when: [vpn]`
    - `vpn.control_routers: <r> is not a host router of the template`
    - `vpn.control_routers: <r> serves an admin UI`
    - `hooks[<n>]: when: [vpn] needs a vpn: block that names it`
    - `hooks[<n>]: vpn can't be combined with other triggers`
    - `router <r>: entrypoints must be 'websecure'` (every template router, with or without a `vpn:` block: the Hub adds `vpnsecure` per reach, §5)
- **Devices hook stdout (`identity.source: hook`).** One JSON document, at most 4 MiB and at most 10 000 devices, strict (unknown keys refused), `version` exactly 1:

    ```json
    {
      "version": 1,
      "gateway": "100.64.0.1",
      "devices": [
        {"id": "12", "name": "laptop", "address": "100.64.0.7", "owner": "<sub or username>",
         "online": true, "last_seen": "2026-11-12T10:00:00Z", "expires": null}
      ]
    }
    ```

    - **`gateway`** (required): the gateway node's IPv4 tunnel address, inside the ranges. It is the DNS target (§13.8 `op: dns`) and never a device.
    - **Each device** has exactly `id` (the app's own node id), `name`, `address`, `owner` (the Keycloak user id for `owner: oidc_sub`, the LLDAP username for `owner: username`), `online` (boolean), `last_seen` and `expires` (RFC 3339 UTC or `null`).
    - **The whole document is refused** in these cases, and the Hub keeps the last good map until it is stale:
        - over 4 MiB or over 10 000 devices;
        - `version` ≠ 1, or an unknown key;
        - `gateway` missing or outside the ranges.
    - **Single devices are dropped**, each shown with its reason on the instance's VPN tab:
        - an IPv6 `address` (`ipv6`);
        - an address outside the ranges (`outside_ranges`);
        - the gateway's own address (`gateway`);
        - `expires` in the past (`expired`);
        - an address two devices share: every device with it (`duplicate`; doctor `vpn_provider_invalid`, Problem);
        - an owner that doesn't resolve to an enabled person in the VPN users group (`not a Portcullis person`).

        `oidc_sub` resolves through Keycloak's LDAP-federated user id to the LLDAP username, never through an email. `username` is an exact lowercase match.

    - **Stale.** A map is stale `max(3 × refresh, 3 min)` after its last good run (`stale_after`, §4), which is never more than 30 min (3 × the 10 min refresh maximum). A hook failure, a timeout or a refused document keeps the last good map until then. The edge and group-gate deny a stale map's addresses, and the next good run recovers it.
    - **Address reuse.** A mesh may hand a removed node's address to another person's node within one refresh. The binding then fails (the owner isn't the signed-in person) until the next run: it fails closed, never open.
- **Several providers.** Provider ranges never overlap. The Hub refuses to wire a provider (`409`, §11.7) whose ranges overlap the built-in subnet, the reserved link subnet, a **reserved range**, a Docker network or another wired provider, and refuses to publish one; every reader refuses a `vpn.json` with overlapping ranges or with a range that overlaps a reserved range (§4).
    - **Reserved ranges** are the configured core subnets (`portcullis-proxy`, `portcullis-auth`, the domains and MCP networks, `portcullis-vpn`, `portcullis-vpn-edge`, **NEW (multiple servers)** `portcullis-link`, `portcullis-link-data`), the link subnet `10.214.0.0/24` (fixed, §17.2), plus `172.16.0.0/12` and `192.168.0.0/16`: Docker's default address pools allocate app-instance networks from both, so a provider there could claim an app's own container addresses. With rootless Podman, the operator's `containers.conf` pins `default_subnet_pools = [{"base" = "10.89.0.0/16", "size" = 24}]`, and the reserved ranges also include `10.88.0.0/16` and `10.89.0.0/16` (Podman's default network and that pool). Core checks the pool at rootless host preparation: a mismatch is a warning while the `wg` profile is off and a refusal with it on. Core passes them to the Hub as `PORTCULLIS_VPN_RESERVED_RANGES` in `core.env` (space-separated prefixes).

    So an address belongs to at most one provider. An overlap with Local networks is allowed (doctor `vpn_range_overlap`, Warning, §14.7).

- **DNS hook (`dns.hook`).** The hook receives the records on stdin (`op: dns`, §13.8) and applies them its own way (Headscale: `dns.extra_records_path`). It exits 0 when they are applied; its stdout is ignored.
    - **The records.** One `{"name": "<fqdn>", "type": "A", "value": "<gateway>"}` per core host and per enabled instance host that the DNS plan serves from this server (explicit names, no wildcard). `value` is the `gateway` of the last good devices run.
    - **When.** After a devices run that changes `gateway`, and after any change of Portcullis hostnames (instance hosts, an enable, an added domain), always with every record.
    - **Failure.** A failed run is doctor `vpn_dns_failed` (Problem), never a map failure: the names then resolve publicly, and VPN-only apps show `/vpn-required` (§5).
    - **The built-in resolver** (§16) is a separate thing: it serves built-in clients only.
- **Gateway attachment (the Hub's override, for a wired provider).**
    - **Networks.** The ingress service keeps its own networks (the template's `networks`, or `default` when it declares none, aliases kept) and gains `portcullis-vpn: {ipv4_address: <gateway>}`, the provider's slot address (§16). The override declares `networks: {portcullis-vpn: {external: true}}`.
    - **The edge address.** The override sets `environment: {PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE: "<wg ip>:<9001 + slot>"}` on the ingress service **and** on every service with `network_mode: service:<ingress.service>`. Templates read it only as `$$PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE` in a container shell.
- **Control routers (§5).** Each router in `control_routers` keeps `entrypoints: websecure,vpnsecure` and no allowlist, whatever the instance's reach and the server mode, so the provider's clients can still reach its control plane when the rest of the app, its admin UI included, is VPN-only. Its rule, middlewares, TLS tier and service are unchanged.
- **Primary only.** A wired provider's instance runs on the primary server, because its gateway joins `portcullis-vpn`.

Example (`headscale`; hooks in §13.8). Its `gateway` (userspace `tailscale/tailscale`) reaches headscale's control and DERP server over https at its public hostname, through Traefik's published port on the host (`extra_hosts: <host>:host-gateway`), trusting the Hub's CA bundle that `headscale-init` hands over through the read-only `gateway-ca` volume. After wiring, the gateway restarts once, which is expected: its first TLS connection predates the headscale router, so Traefik answers it with `421`, and containerboot's 60 s boot deadline exits it; the restart reconnects:

```yaml
# manifest.yaml (excerpt)
vpn:
  label: Headscale tailnet
  ranges: ["100.64.0.0/10"]
  ingress: {service: gateway, proxy_protocol: v2}
  identity: {source: hook, hook: vpn-devices, owner: oidc_sub, refresh: 60s}
  dns: {hook: vpn-dns}
  control_routers: [headscale]
```

### 3.4 Compose on Kubernetes — NEW (Kubernetes)

Under `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes` (§6) the Hub doesn't run `docker compose`. It loads each instance's project exactly as above (the template's `compose.yml`, the Hub's override and the custom override, interpolated from the same env file, setup profiles applied), runs every check of this section on that compose model, and then translates it into Kubernetes objects in the apps namespace (`PORTCULLIS_APPS_NAMESPACE`, default `portcullis-apps`). Templates don't change and ship no Kubernetes manifests. The instance's runtime compatibility (§11.10) is judged first: a `refused` template is never translated, and the translator refuses exactly what the compatibility rules refuse, so the two can't disagree.

**Refused on Kubernetes.** These reasons are exact (shared byte for byte with the templates validator, §11.10); `<s>` is the compose service:

- `service <s>: its name isn't a DNS label without "--" (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s>: the name is reserved on Kubernetes (the instance's pod DNS)` (a service named `pods`: `<instance>--pods` is the instance's headless Service)
- `service <s> uses network_mode: host (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> shares the network of <x>, which isn't a service`, `service <s> shares the network of <x>, which shares another's` (`network_mode: service:<x>`)
- `service <s> passes host devices (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> is privileged (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> shares the host's <pid|ipc> namespace (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> adds <CAP>, outside the Kubernetes baseline` (`<CAP>` is `a capability` when it isn't a Linux capability name)
- `service <s> binds a host path outside the shared-folder roots (not on Kubernetes)`
- **host paths** (a pod with a `hostPath` runs non-root with a group other than 0, §6): `service <s> binds a host path but has no numeric user`; `service <s> binds a host path but its group isn't set or is 0: set user "<uid>:<gid>" with a gid other than 0`; and the same for a service that shares a pod (`network_mode: service:<x>`) with a host path: `service <s> shares a pod with a host path but its group isn't set or is 0: set user "<uid>:<gid>" with a gid other than 0`
- `service <s> publishes <port> on a specific address (not on Kubernetes)` (`<port>` is `a port` when it isn't a number)
- `service <s> runs as a non-numeric user: Kubernetes needs a numeric uid`
- `service <s> adds a non-numeric group: Kubernetes needs a numeric gid` (`group_add`)
- `service <s> exposes something other than a single port (not on Kubernetes)` (`expose`)
- `service <s> mounts a <type> volume (not on Kubernetes)` (a long-syntax volume other than `bind`, `volume` or `tmpfs`; `<type>` is `an unknown` when it isn't a compose type)
- `service <s> mounts a volume but has no numeric user` (a named volume's owner on Kubernetes is the service's uid)
- `service <s> runs as root (user 0)` (a long-running service)
- `service <s> runs as root (user 0): only a one-shot job (restart no or on-failure) with cap_drop [ALL], cap_add within CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, no ports and no routes may`
- `service <s> runs as root with group 0: set user "0:<gid>" with a gid other than 0`
- `service <s> runs as root with a host bind` (a root job may bind only the template's own files, `./templates/…`, which become the instance's ConfigMap)
- `service <s> runs as root and mounts a volume no non-root service mounts (its owner on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> sets replicas above 1 (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> sets extra_hosts (not on Kubernetes)`
- `service <s> publishes port <p>, a core port`
- `service <s> uses TUN/NET_ADMIN (not on Kubernetes; prefer a userspace mode)`
- **aliases** (a `container_name` or a network alias becomes an alias Service and `hostAliases`): `service <s> answers to alias <a>, not a DNS label without "--" (not on Kubernetes)`, `service <s> answers to alias <a>, also a compose service name`, `service <s> answers to alias <a>, reserved on Kubernetes (the instance's pod DNS)`, `alias <a> names two services (<s1>, <s2>)`, `service <s> answers to alias <a> but serves no declared port (expose it)` and `more than 16 network aliases (not on Kubernetes)`
- **Traefik labels** (the template's own labels, with their defaults only, judged by the same code that converts them, §5 "Traefik on Kubernetes"): for example `router <r>: its name isn't one DNS label once _ and . become - (no --, no trailing -; not on Kubernetes)` (the same for a middleware; only the template's part of a name is judged, not the Hub's `portcullis-mcp-<instance>--` prefix of a companion router), `router <r>: its rule isn't Host(…) with an optional && Path/PathPrefix over lowercase hostnames (not on Kubernetes)`, `router <r>: priority <p> is above 1000 (not on Kubernetes)`, `router <r>: its tls.options isn't one of the tiers`, `middleware <m> is a forwardAuth (not allowed for apps)`, `middleware <m> sets <header> (an X-Portcullis-* header)`, `middleware <m>: type <t> is not on Kubernetes` and `middleware <m> is not on Kubernetes (not the instance's own, not a core name apps may use)`

Reasons quote only names the template or core supplies, never an instance value: a value that isn't of the expected kind is replaced by a placeholder (`a capability`, `a port`, `an unknown`).

The **Kubernetes baseline** capabilities are `AUDIT_WRITE`, `CHOWN`, `DAC_OVERRIDE`, `FOWNER`, `FSETID`, `KILL`, `MKNOD`, `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, `SETFCAP`, `SETGID`, `SETPCAP`, `SETUID` and `SYS_CHROOT`; any other `cap_add` is refused. The shared-folder roots are the bind roots (`HUB_OVERRIDE_BIND_ROOTS`). The core ports are the admission policy's list (§6 "On Kubernetes"): 80, 443, the VPN port, 8000, 8081, 8443 and 8444. Compose `scale: 0` and `scale: 1` are allowed (replicas 0 and 1); `deploy` is refused on every runtime (§3). A device slot follows the rootless rule: an empty slot (a `/dev/null` source) is degraded, a real device refused (`/dev/net/tun` with the TUN reason). **Degraded:** `service <s> has device slots: host devices can't be passed on Kubernetes`, and `the Avahi services directory binds a host path outside the shared-folder roots: leave it empty and connect by address` (Time Machine with `avahi_services_dir` set).

**Translation.** Every name and label below is set by the translator only (§11.2 "On Kubernetes" for the names):

| Compose | Kubernetes |
|---|---|
| service | Deployment, replicas 1 (0 while the service's compose `scale` is 0: a companion switched off, §3.2), strategy `Recreate`; pod labels `portcullis.io/instance`, `portcullis.io/service`, one `portcullis.io/net-<network>: "true"` per compose network and `portcullis.io/egress` for a non-internal network (§5). Compose labels become annotations, never pod labels |
| one-off job (§3) | Job, `backoffLimit: 0` |
| `depends_on` (`service_healthy` / `service_completed_successfully`) | ordered apply: the Hub waits for readiness or completion before the next step |
| `healthcheck` | exec probes: `CMD-SHELL x` → `["sh", "-c", x]`, `CMD a b` → `["a", "b"]`. `interval` / `timeout` / `retries` → `periodSeconds` / `timeoutSeconds` / `failureThreshold` of the readiness probe; the liveness probe has `failureThreshold` × 2; `start_period` → a `startupProbe` (the same exec, `periodSeconds` = interval, `failureThreshold` = ceil(start_period / interval) + retries). No probe has `initialDelaySeconds` |
| `user`, `group_add`, `cap_add` / `cap_drop`, `read_only`, `security_opt: no-new-privileges` | `runAsUser` / `runAsGroup` (numeric only), `supplementalGroups` (numeric only), capabilities (`cap_drop` carried, `ALL` first), `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`. Always `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault` and `automountServiceAccountToken: false` (the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount) |
| `tmpfs: <path>:size=N,mode=M`, `shm_size` | `emptyDir {medium: Memory, sizeLimit: N}` per container; the mode isn't carried. `/dev/shm` the same |
| `mem_limit` | `resources.limits.memory` = `resources.requests.memory` |
| `pids_limit` | not carried: the kubelet's per-pod limit (1024) applies |
| `environment`, the env file | the Secret `<instance>--env`, read through `envFrom`: no value ever appears in a pod spec |
| `image` | resolved by the Hub to `name@sha256:…` (anonymous registry lookup, fully qualified references only) and deployed by that digest; an image that doesn't resolve refuses the deploy. A resolved digest is kept only after a successful deploy. Docker's image-label merge doesn't exist here, so the image-label check (§3) has nothing to check |
| named volume | PVC (StorageClass `portcullis-apps`, §11.2) plus two init containers (below) |
| bind `./templates/<id>/…` | the instance's own ConfigMap `<instance>--tpl-<hash10>` (`<hash10>` = the first 10 hex digits of the sha256 of the files; at most 1 MiB, nested paths through `items`), mounted read-only; never shared between instances |
| data files `./appfiles/<id>/<name>` (§13.7) | the ConfigMap `<instance>--<name>` (the data file) and the Secret `<instance>--<name>-secrets` (the secrets file), mounted read-only at the file's `mount` with the modes of §13.7 "On Kubernetes" |
| the per-person secrets mount (§6) | the Secret `<instance>--<key>-pw` (§6 "On Kubernetes") |
| bind under the bind roots (shared folders) | `hostPath`, type `Directory`, only under the bind roots |
| `ports:` (manifest ports) | Service `LoadBalancer` with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` and `allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false` (no node port bypasses the source ranges; core's e2e checks that none is allocated); `lan_only` → `loadBalancerSourceRanges` = the Local networks' IPv4 entries, and no Service at all when there are none (§13.15) |
| Traefik labels | IngressRoutes and Middlewares in the edge namespace `portcullis-edge` (§5 "Traefik on Kubernetes") |
| `network_mode: service:<x>` | an extra container in `<x>`'s pod |
| `stop_grace_period`, `stop_signal` | `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, a `preStop` exec `kill -s <sig> 1` |
| `extra_hosts` | refused (above) |

**Middleware and service names.** The Hub renders an instance's Traefik labels exactly as on Docker (§5); the translator maps the core names they use from `…@docker` to `…@file` (§5 "Traefik on Kubernetes" has the list), and refuses every other `@docker` name that isn't the instance's own.

**Volume seeding.** Docker copies an image's content into a new named volume; a PVC starts empty. So for every named volume of a service the translator adds two init containers:

- **`portcullis-bin`**: the Hub's own image by digest (`HUB_SELF_IMAGE`, §6); it copies the static binary `/usr/local/bin/hub` into an `emptyDir` mounted at `/portcullis-bin`;
- **`portcullis-seed`**: the service's own image and user, with the PVC mounted at `/portcullis-seed`; it runs `/portcullis-bin/hub seed <target> /portcullis-seed`, where `<target>` is the volume's mount target in the service. `hub seed` copies the image's directory into the PVC only when the PVC has no entries but `lost+found`, keeps modes and symlinks, and writes `.portcullis-seeded` last; when that file exists it does nothing.

No shell is needed in the app image, and the files are owned by the service's uid. `portcullis-bin` is also added to every pod that mounts a ConfigMap or Secret delivery, for the `.rev` check (§13.7).

**Nothing is applied for an instance whose translation can't be represented:** a refused feature, two compose names that give the same object name (refused naming both), or an object over the API's 1 MiB limit (`template files for <id> exceed 1 MiB`; also a data file or a `*-pw` Secret).

**A wired VPN provider** (§3.3, §16.1): its ingress pod gets the label `portcullis.io/vpn-slot: "<slot>"`, and `PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE` is in its `<instance>--env` Secret. There is no `portcullis-vpn` network.

### 3.5 Mail providers: the `mail:` block — NEW (mail provider)

A template that is a mail server may declare a top-level `mail:` block. As with `vpn:` (§3.3), the block alone grants nothing: an admin wires one instance of it into the mail slot (§19.9), and only the **wired** instance gets the slot's powers (§19.1). The templates repo's schema, `tests/validate.py` and the Hub's `templates.ValidateMail` implement exactly the rules below, with the same refusal texts in the same order. They share the vectors file `tests/mail_vectors.json` / `internal/templates/testdata/mail_vectors.json`, byte copies checked in CI the way `vpn_vectors.json` is. The Hub skips a template that fails them, and the Marketplace shows a template that passes with a "Mail server" badge (`mail_provider: true`).

```yaml
# manifest.yaml (excerpt, template stalwart)
instances: single
mail:
  label: Stalwart
  api_version: 1
  api:       {service: adapter, port: 8080}
  listeners: {service: stalwart, smtp: 10025, submissions: 10465, submission: 10587, imaps: 10993}
  wellknown: {service: adapter, port: 8081}
  metrics:   {service: adapter, port: 9100}
  server_metrics: {service: stalwart, port: 9180, path: /metrics/prometheus}   # optional
  tls:       [stalwart, adapter]        # services that get the mail certificate, read-only
  gated:     [stalwart, adapter]        # services that get the gate files and must honour them
  sessions:  {restart: stalwart}        # restarted after every removal and revoke
  export:    {service: adapter, argv: ["mailctl", "export", "--former", "{former_id}"]}   # optional
```

- **Fields** (unknown keys refused; only `server_metrics` and `export` are optional):
    - **`label`**: one line, 1–64 characters. Shown on Settings → Mail and the instance's Mail tab.
    - **`api_version`**: exactly `1`, the provider API of §19.5. The Hub refuses a version it doesn't speak (`409` at wiring, doctor `mail_provider_refused`).
    - **`api`**, **`wellknown`**, **`metrics`**, **`server_metrics`**: a compose service of the template (`service`) and a container port, 1024–65535 (`port`); `server_metrics` also has `path`, an absolute URL path. The Hub dials `api` on `portcullis-mail-api`, routes `wellknown` (§19.7) and scrapes `metrics` and `server_metrics` (§19.8).
    - **`listeners`**: exactly the keys `service`, `smtp`, `submissions`, `submission` and `imaps`: the four container ports, 1024–65535 each, all on one service. The Hub publishes host ports 25, 465, 587 and 993 onto them (§19.2).
    - **`tls`**, **`gated`**: lists of services. Every service in `listeners` and `api` must be in both. A service that serves mail or holds credentials must be `gated`: it gets the gate files and must honour them (§19.4).
    - **`sessions.restart`**: one service, normally the listener service. **Required**: the Hub restarts it after every removal and every revoked mail password, whatever the server claims about sessions (§19.6).
    - **`export`** (optional): `service` and `argv`, a literal argv with exactly one `{former_id}` element, run by `./portcullis mail export` as an exec in that service; stdout is the mbox (§19.11).
- **The services the block names** (`api`, `listeners`, `wellknown`, `metrics`, `server_metrics`, `sessions.restart` and `export`) are each a compose service of the template that is not a job (§3), not an AI companion (§3.2) and has no `network_mode`. `tls` and `gated` entries are compose services of the template.
- **Stricter rules for every service of a mail template.** These are the VPN gateway's rules (§3.3), applied to the whole template, because a mail provider holds everyone's mailbox:
    - no `ports:` on any service, and no `ports` list in the manifest: the Hub publishes a mail provider's ports (§19.1);
    - no Traefik router and no `traefik.*` label on any service: the provider's only router is the Hub's well-known router (§19.1);
    - not `privileged`; `cap_drop: [ALL]`, and `cap_add` only `NET_BIND_SERVICE`;
    - no `devices` or `device_cgroup_rules`;
    - no `pid`, `ipc` or `volumes_from` key, and no `network_mode: host`;
    - binds only the template's own files (`./templates/<id>/…`), read-only, with the VPN template's bind and volume rules (§3.3 "Mounts and volumes of every service");
    - plain `<project>_<key>` volumes: no top-level volume sets `name`, `external`, `driver` or `driver_opts`;
    - no YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys in `compose.yml`;
    - no `enable_ipv6` on any network (mail over IPv6 is refused, §19.2);
    - no `person_secret` or `person_id` options (§13.2): mail passwords go only through the provider API (§19.6);
    - `instances: single` (the host ports and the one slot).
- **`auth`** is `method: custom` with no routers and `group_access: false`. The mailbox population is the Hub's `mail_users` group (§19.6), never the template's.
- **Validation refusals** (these exact texts; `<field>` is the block key, e.g. `api`, `listeners`, `sessions.restart`; `<s>` a service, `<k>` a key's path inside the block, e.g. `api.host`). **Order:** unknown keys first; then each field in the order of the Fields list (`label`, `api_version`, `api`, `listeners`, `wellknown`, `metrics`, `server_metrics`, `tls`, `gated`, `sessions.restart`, `export`), each with its checks in list order (required; the field's own texts; for a service field: not a service of the template, the port, a job, an AI companion, `network_mode`); then the manifest (`instances`, `auth`, `ports`, the options); then service by service in compose order (each with its texts in list order, mounts in mount order); then the volumes, the networks and the YAML shape. The first refusal is the answer:
    - `mail: unknown key <k>`
    - `mail.<field>: required` (a missing required field, e.g. `mail.sessions.restart: required`)
    - `mail.label: 1–64 characters, one line`
    - `mail.api_version: only 1`
    - `mail.<field>: service <s> is not a service of this template`
    - `mail.<field>: port must be 1024–65535`
    - `mail.<field>: <s> is a job`
    - `mail.<field>: <s> is an AI companion`
    - `mail.<field>: <s> has network_mode`
    - `mail.listeners: exactly smtp, submissions, submission and imaps, on one service`
    - `mail.server_metrics.path: an absolute URL path`
    - `mail.tls: <s> serves mail and must be listed`
    - `mail.gated: <s> serves mail and must be listed`
    - `mail.export.argv: exactly one {former_id}`
    - `mail: instances must be single`
    - `mail: auth must be method custom with no routers and group_access false`
    - `mail: manifest ports are not allowed`
    - `mail: person_secret options are not allowed: mail passwords go through the provider API` (also for a `person_id` option)
    - `mail: service <s> publishes ports: the Hub publishes a mail provider's ports`
    - `mail: service <s> has a Traefik router: a mail provider's only router is the Hub's well-known router` (any `traefik.*` label)
    - `mail: <s> is privileged`
    - `mail: <s> must set cap_drop: [ALL]`
    - `mail: <s> adds <cap>: a mail provider may add only NET_BIND_SERVICE`
    - `mail: <s> has <key>: a mail provider has no devices` (`<key>` is `devices` or `device_cgroup_rules`)
    - `mail: <s> sets <pid|ipc>: a mail provider keeps its own pid and ipc namespaces`
    - `mail: service <s> uses network_mode: host`
    - `mail: <s> uses volumes_from: a mail provider mounts no other service's volumes`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: unresolvable (a mail template's mounts are literal)`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: a mail template's binds start with ./ and have no .. segment`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: a mail template's volume names are longer than one letter`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: a mail template's short-syntax sources are ./ binds or declared volumes`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: a mail provider binds only the template's own files (./templates/<id>/…), read-only`
    - `mail: <s> mounts <entry>: it resolves outside templates/<id>/ (a symlink)`
    - `mail: volume <v>: a mail template's volume names are longer than one letter`
    - `mail: volume <v> sets <key>: a mail template's volumes are plain <project>_<key> volumes`
    - `mail: network <n> enables IPv6`
    - `mail: network <n> sets <key>: a mail template's networks are plain project networks (internal, ipam subnets and IP ranges, enable_ipv6: false)` — `<key>` is the top-level key, `ipam.<k>` for an ipam key other than `config`, `ipam.config.<k>` for a config key other than `subnet` / `ip_range`
    - `mail: network <n> is one of core's networks: a mail template declares only its own` — every core network key and name, case-folded (the Hub adds the core networks a wired provider joins)
    - `mail: service <s> joins network <n>: a mail template's services join only networks it declares at the top level`
    - `mail: service <s> sets <key> on network <n>: a mail template's fixed addresses are IPv4 inside that network's own declared subnet` — `ipv4_address` only inside the declared ipam subnet of a network the template declares; `ipv6_address` and `link_local_ips` always refused; on core / external networks every address and alias is the Hub's
    - `compose.yml: a mail template uses no YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys`
    - `mail: <service> image must be a literal reference: a mail template's images are hashed (no ${…})`

    The mount texts are the VPN template's (§3.3) with the prefix `mail:` and "mail template" for "VPN template".

- **Variables.** A mail template never interpolates `${PORTCULLIS_MAIL_*}` (§2): the override sets the provider's environment (§19.4), which its programs read at run time.
- **Primary only.** The wired provider runs on the primary server: it joins core networks and mounts core volumes.

## 4. Policy file (Hub → group-gate)

The Hub writes `group-gate-policy.json` atomically (temp file + rename) to the `hub_data` volume. group-gate mounts that volume read-only and re-reads the file on every request.

**NEW (sign-in): policy file v6.** **NEW (VPN): policy file v7.** The file is `version: 7`. Every per-app map is keyed by **full hostname** (as since v5), and the access rule is a **sign-in template** (§8.1) instead of a factor list: `methods`, `templates`, `default`, `hosts`, `core`, `people` and `add_stronger` replace v5's `default` / `policies`. **NEW (VPN):** v7 adds the required top-level key `vpn` (VPN settings and the binding). Format:

```json
{
  "version": 7,
  "vpn": {
    "hosts": {"<app hostname>": {"via": ["*"], "public_links": false}},
    "server_mode": false,
    "admin_only": false,
    "public_enrol": true,
    "devices_file": "vpn.json"
  },
  "methods": ["<switched-on method id>"],
  "templates": {"<template id>": {"op": "any|all", "items": ["<method id>", {"op": "any|all", "items": ["..."]}]}},
  "default": "<template id>",
  "hosts": {"<app hostname>": "<template id>"},
  "core": {"<core hostname>": "<template id>"},
  "people": {"<lowercase username>": ["<switched-on method id they have set up>"]},
  "add_stronger": false,
  "extra_domains": ["<added domain>"],
  "groups":   {"<hostname>": "<required LLDAP group>"},
  "path_groups": {
    "<hostname>": [{"prefix": "/admin", "group": "<LLDAP group>"}]
  },
  "public_paths": {
    "<hostname>": {
      "paths": [{"path": "/s/{token}", "match": "prefix"}, {"path": "/dist", "match": "static"}],
      "token_pattern": "^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$",
      "static_extensions": ["css", "js", "..."],
      "credential_headers": ["Authorization", "Proxy-Authorization"],
      "credential_cookies": ["nc_token"],
      "credential_query": []
    }
  },
  "expiring": [
    {"user": "jsmith", "group": "contractors", "at": "2027-03-31T23:59:59Z"}
  ]
}
```

Example: main domain `portcullis.example.com`, two Grafana instances (`grafana-team-a` on the main domain, on the default template; `grafana-team-b` on the added domain `team-b.example.org`, its hostname edited to `grafana.team-b.example.org`, picked onto Strong) and the default instance of Vaultwarden. The methods are the four switched on at the start (password, browser certificate and authenticator app off), the enabled templates the built-in Standard and Strong (Basic, YubiKey + certificate and Password + authenticator code start disabled, §8.1), and the core pages are on their starting picks (`hub` and `people` on Strong, the rest on the default). The groups of core hosts (`portcullis.example.com`, `hub.portcullis.example.com`, `people.portcullis.example.com`, …) are **not** in the file: they come from `group-gate-map.conf`.

```json
{
  "version": 7,
  "vpn": {
    "hosts": {},
    "server_mode": false,
    "admin_only": false,
    "public_enrol": true,
    "devices_file": "vpn.json"
  },
  "methods": ["passkey_device", "passkey_synced", "security_key", "yubikey_cert"],
  "templates": {
    "standard": {"op": "any", "items": [
      {"op": "any", "items": ["passkey_synced", "passkey_device", "security_key"]},
      {"op": "any", "items": ["yubikey_cert"]}
    ]},
    "strong": {"op": "any", "items": ["security_key", "yubikey_cert"]}
  },
  "default": "standard",
  "hosts": {"grafana.team-b.example.org": "strong"},
  "core": {
    "directory.portcullis.example.com": "standard",
    "hub.portcullis.example.com": "strong",
    "metrics.portcullis.example.com": "standard",
    "people.portcullis.example.com": "strong",
    "portcullis.example.com": "standard",
    "traefik.portcullis.example.com": "standard"
  },
  "people": {
    "alice": ["passkey_synced", "security_key"],
    "bob": ["passkey_synced"]
  },
  "add_stronger": false,
  "extra_domains": ["team-b.example.org"],
  "groups": {
    "grafana-team-a.portcullis.example.com": "users_grafana-team-a",
    "grafana.team-b.example.org": "users_grafana-team-b",
    "passwords.portcullis.example.com": "users_vaultwarden"
  },
  "path_groups": {
    "passwords.portcullis.example.com": [{"prefix": "/admin", "group": "admin_vaultwarden"}]
  },
  "public_paths": {
    "grafana-team-a.portcullis.example.com": {
      "paths": [
        {"path": "/public-dashboards/{token}", "match": "prefix"},
        {"path": "/api/public/dashboards/{token}", "match": "prefix"},
        {"path": "/public/build", "match": "static"}
      ],
      "token_pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{32}$",
      "static_extensions": ["css", "js", "svg", "woff2"],
      "credential_headers": ["Authorization", "Proxy-Authorization", "X-Access-Token", "X-Grafana-Id"],
      "credential_cookies": ["grafana_session", "renderKey"],
      "credential_query": ["auth_token"]
    }
  },
  "expiring": []
}
```

- **`methods`** (**NEW**, v6): the switched-on sign-in method ids (§8.1 table), sorted, no duplicates. A method that is off is not listed and is never accepted, whatever the session's `amr` says.
- **`templates`** (**NEW**, v6): template id → **compiled** rule (§8.1 "Rules"), for every **enabled** template (plus the synthetic collision templates, below). Ids match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, or `^collision\.[1-9][0-9]*$` for a collision template. A compiled rule is an object with exactly the keys `op` (`all` or `any`) and `items` (1–8 entries); each item is a method id listed in `methods` or a nested group of the same shape; groups nest at most **4** levels (the top group is level 1), with at most **48** leaves (method ids) in one rule. A compiled rule never holds a family (`family:*`): the Hub expands families before publishing. **NEW (authenticator codes):** a compiled rule with an alternative that is `{totp}` alone (§8.1 "Rules": an authenticator code is never a way in alone) is refused like any other invalid rule (group-gate's `validate_rule`: "an authenticator code alone is a way in").
- **`default`** (**NEW**, v6): the Portcullis-wide default template, a key of `templates`.
- **`hosts`** (**NEW**, v6): app hostname → template id, only for hostnames of enabled instances that picked their own template (instances on the default publish nothing; group-gate falls back to `default`). An instance can pick a template only when its app has a Portcullis sign-in: an app with `auth.method` `custom` (without Portcullis sign-in) or `public` takes none (the Hub answers `400`), and an `auth.method: mtls` app takes none either (its certificate at the TLS handshake is its authentication, §5 "TLS tier per host").
- **`core`** (**NEW**, v6): core hostname → template id, for **every** core host group-gate gates: the main domain (the portal, key `portal` in the Hub) and `hub`, `people`, `directory`, `metrics` and `traefik` under it (§8.1 "Core pages"). It holds **only** those hosts: any other key (`enroll.<d>`, `auth.<d>`, `mcp.<d>`, an app host) makes the file invalid and group-gate denies every request. **NEW (sign-in part 2):** `enroll` is not a gated core host and is never listed: `enroll.<main domain>` serves only setup links (`/invite/*`, no forward-auth, §5), so the Hub has no `enroll` core page. `auth` and `mcp` are never listed: `mcp` never reaches group-gate (mcp-gate authorizes it), and `auth.<main domain>` — the Keycloak admin console's router (`/admin`, `/realms/master`), the one `auth` route behind group-gate — takes the Hub's template, `core["hub.<main domain>"]` (missing = deny): the console is as powerful as the Hub.
- **`people`** (**NEW**, v6): lowercase username → the ids of the switched-on methods that person has set up, sorted (the Hub's inventory, §8.1). **Page text only, never an access decision**: group-gate uses it to word its step-up and needs-stronger pages (§5). A person absent from `people` means "not known" (the Hub couldn't read their methods); `[]` means none set up.
- **`add_stronger`** (**NEW**, v6): the Settings switch "add a stronger method from a weaker sign-in" (§8.1). Page text only: "Set up …" when on, "ask your admin" when off and the method is stronger than the session.
- **`vpn`** (**NEW**, v7): the VPN-only hosts and the server mode (§16). A required object with exactly these keys:
    - **`hosts`** (object): hostname → `{"via": […], "public_links": true|false}`, one entry for every host of every VPN-only instance (§11.7). Keys are valid hostnames ("Keys are full hostnames" below). `via` is `["*"]` (every wired provider), `[]` (no provider: the host is unreachable and step 1 below always denies) or 1–8 provider ids, each `builtin` or an instance id; anything else makes the file invalid. Only an explicit `["*"]` means any provider. `public_links` (required boolean) is the instance's *public links stay on the internet* opt-in (§11.7): on `websecure`, `/public-guard` admits the host's published public paths only when it is true. A `via` naming only providers that are no longer wired stays as written, so step 1 denies. A host missing from `hosts` is reachable from the internet. Core hosts are never keys of `hosts`.
    - **`server_mode`** (boolean): true exactly when core's `PORTCULLIS_VPN_MODE` is `server` (§16).
    - **`admin_only`** (boolean): true exactly when it is `admin`.
    - **`public_enrol`** (boolean): core's `PORTCULLIS_VPN_PUBLIC_ENROL`: whether the `/vpn/` paths on `people.<main domain>` stay reachable from the internet in server mode (§5.1).
    - **`devices_file`** (string): exactly `"vpn.json"`. Any other value makes the file invalid.

    The Hub copies `server_mode`, `admin_only` and `public_enrol` from `core.env`; it never sets them on its own (§11.7). **group-gate takes the VPN mode from its own environment**, which core sets from `.env` (`PORTCULLIS_VPN_MODE`): that value is authoritative. The policy's `server_mode` / `admin_only` are ignored for the decision, and a mismatch with group-gate's own mode is logged. So `./portcullis vpn mode apps` works as the break-glass even with the Hub down (§16).

- **The MCP endpoints (VPN).** In the `admin` and `server` modes, `mcp`, `hub-mcp` and `people-mcp` answer only over the VPN (`vpnsecure`, §5), but they never reach group-gate, so they aren't bound to the device's owner. The MCP OAuth token is still required (§15).
- **The client address (VPN).** It is the **last** entry of `X-Forwarded-For`, which Traefik appends from the connection's remote address (on `vpnsecure`, the PROXY v2 source, §5). group-gate splits on `,`, trims spaces, takes the last entry and parses it as IPv4. An IPv6 or malformed value means "no VPN address" (step 1 denies). Client-sent copies are discarded on both entrypoints.
- **The binding steps (VPN).** For a VPN-only host with `via` = `<providers>`, and `a` = the client address:
    1. **The provider.** `p` is the one provider whose `ranges` contain `a`; ranges are disjoint across the file, so there is at most one. Deny when:
        - there is no such `p`, or `vpn.json` is missing or invalid (the `/vpn-required` text, §5);
        - `via` doesn't accept `p` (the `/vpn-required` text; `*` accepts every provider);
        - `p` is stale: `stale: true`, or a hook provider `p` at or past its `stale_after` by group-gate's own clock (reason "your VPN's device list is out of date; try again in a minute").
    2. **A device of that provider.** The device with `ip` = `a` **and** `provider` = `p.id`, not past its `expires`; for `builtin`, also with its matching unexpired peer. A device of another provider never counts. None → deny (the `/vpn-required` text).
    3. **The owner.** The device's `user` equals the session's `preferred_username`, lowercased. Otherwise deny with "this device isn't yours; sign in on your own device". The owner's name is never shown.

    Any failure is a `403` with that step's page (§5). group-gate's reasons (metric labels and log values) are `vpn_not_vpn`, `vpn_stale`, `vpn_via`, `vpn_unknown_device`, `vpn_expired`, `vpn_other_owner` and `vpn_no_doc`. The binding runs after the identity checks and **before** the membership checks; a request through a VPN to an internet host needs no binding.

- **The binding counts only on the VPN paths (VPN).** A VPN-only decision is bound to the entrypoint by the forward-auth address, which no client chooses. group-gate evaluates the binding only on its three VPN paths: `/auth/vpn` (middleware `portcullis-groups-vpn@docker`), `/public-guard/vpn` (`portcullis-public-guard-vpn@docker`) and `/portal/vpn` (`portal-vpn-path@docker`). These middlewares are attached only to `vpnsecure`-only routers. On its normal paths (`/auth`, `/public-guard`, `/portal`) group-gate denies every VPN-only host (a `vpn.hosts` key, or a core class the mode makes VPN-only) with the `/vpn-required` page before it looks at the address, so a websecure request with a LAN, Docker or CGNAT address can never satisfy a binding.

- **Why the address names the provider (the trusted ingress signal, VPN).** group-gate sees only the address. That is enough, because the provider a connection belongs to is fixed by where it entered, never by anything a client or a gateway sends:
    - **The edge, marketplace providers (§16).** Each wired provider has its own TCP port on the edge (`9001 + slot`). The edge takes the provider from the port the connection arrived on, and admits it only when its TCP peer address (never a header) is that provider's `gateway_ip` and the PROXY v2 source lies in **that** provider's ranges and is a fresh device of **that** provider.
    - **The built-in provider.** Its connections never use an edge port: the people tunnel hands them to the edge in-process as provider `builtin`, and the source address is fixed by WireGuard's cryptokey routing.
    - **Traefik.** `vpnsecure` listens only on `portcullis-vpn-edge`, whose members are exactly `wg` and Traefik, and honours PROXY v2 only from `wg`'s address there (§5). Gateways are on `portcullis-vpn`, which Traefik isn't on.
    - **The ranges** are disjoint across the file, and readers refuse a file where they overlap.

    So an address in `p`'s ranges reached `vpnsecure` only through `p`. Every reader looks devices up by provider first, `(provider, ip, now)`. A gateway that claims another provider's address is closed at the edge (`outside_ranges`).

- **Core-host classes (VPN).** group-gate holds a fixed table of core hosts (`group-gate-map.conf` is unchanged):
    - **`admin`**: `traefik.`, `hub.`, `directory.`, `metrics.` and `auth.` (the Keycloak console paths) under the main domain;
    - **`core`**: the main domain itself (the portal) and `people.`;
    - **`enrol`**: the paths under `/vpn/` on `people.<main domain>`.

    The mode decides which classes are VPN-only, and a VPN-only core host needs the full binding (steps 1–3, `via` = `*`):

    | | `admin` | `core` | `enrol` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `admin_only` | VPN-only | open | open |
    | `server_mode` | VPN-only | VPN-only | open with `public_enrol`, else VPN-only |

    - **The portal.** The portal (a group-gate backend, not forward-auth) checks class `core` too, on `/portal/vpn` behind the `portal-vpn` router.
    - **The `mcp` routers.** `mcp`, `hub-mcp` and `people-mcp` never reach group-gate: in the `admin` and `server` modes only their entrypoint protects them (`vpnsecure` only, §5).
    - **The public guard (§5).** On a VPN-only app host, `/public-guard/vpn` enforces steps 1 and 2 only, since there is no signed-in person. On `websecure`, a VPN-only host's published public paths (its public router, kept there by `public_links`, in server mode too) are admitted by `/public-guard` without a VPN check only when the host's `public_links` is true; every other path on the host needs the VPN.
- **The opened log (VPN).** A line for a request that passed the binding gains `via` (`"vpn"`), `provider` and `device` (the device id).
- **`vpn.json` version 2 (Hub → `wg`, group-gate, VPN).** The Hub writes `vpn.json` atomically (temp file + rename), mode 0640, group 10007, to the dedicated core volume **`vpn_doc`** (never `hub_data`, §6), which it mounts read-write at `/vpn-doc` (`HUB_VPN_DOC_DIR=/vpn-doc`, `HUB_VPN_DOC_GID=10007`). It holds public data only. `wg` and group-gate mount `vpn_doc` read-only at `/vpn-doc` and read the file (group-gate as `GATE_VPN_FILE=/vpn-doc/vpn.json`), re-reading it on a change of device, inode, size or mtime. The Hub rewrites it on every map change, at least once per `refresh` of each live provider, and at least every 10 min (`valid_until`, below).

    ```json
    {"version": 2, "valid_until": "2026-11-13T15:23:01Z",
     "builtin": {"subnet": "10.213.0.0/22", "server_public_key": "<base64 public key>",
                 "domains": ["portcullis.example.com"],
                 "peers": [{"ip": "10.213.0.5", "public_key": "<base64 public key>",
                            "device_id": "<16 hex>", "expires": "2027-11-13T14:30:00Z"}]},
     "providers": [{"id": "builtin", "source": "builtin", "ranges": ["10.213.0.0/22"], "edge_port": 0, "gateway_ip": "", "stale": false},
                   {"id": "headscale", "source": "hook", "label": "Headscale tailnet", "ranges": ["100.64.0.0/10"],
                    "edge_port": 9001, "gateway_ip": "172.31.254.16",
                    "refreshed_at": "2026-11-13T14:23:01Z", "stale_after": "2026-11-13T14:26:01Z", "stale": false}],
     "devices": [{"ip": "10.213.0.5", "provider": "builtin", "user": "alice",
                  "device_id": "<16 hex>", "name": "laptop", "expires": "2027-11-13T14:30:00Z"},
                 {"ip": "100.64.0.7", "provider": "headscale", "user": "alice",
                  "device_id": "headscale:12", "name": "phone", "expires": null}]}
    ```

    - **`version`**: exactly 2. Readers serve only 2.
    - **`valid_until`** (required, RFC 3339 UTC): the Hub sets it to the write time + 1 h and republishes the file at least every 10 min. A missing `valid_until`, one in the past by the reader's own clock, or one more than 1 h 5 min ahead of it makes the file invalid: every VPN request is denied and the edge closes every spliced connection. So a Hub that stopped publishing ends every VPN access within the hour.
    - **`builtin`**: present exactly when there is a `builtin` provider: the people role's `subnet`, its `server_public_key`, the `domains` its resolver rewrites (the main domain and the added ones, §16) and its `peers`. Each peer has `ip` (in `subnet`, unique), `public_key` (32 bytes of base64, unique), `device_id` (non-empty) and `expires` (RFC 3339 UTC or `null`). Every reader checks `expires` against its own clock: `wg` removes a peer past it and group-gate denies it, with no new file needed.
    - **`providers`**: at most 48 (the built-in plus 47 slots). Each `id` is `builtin` or an instance id, and ids are unique.
        - **`source`** (required): `builtin` (exactly the provider with id `builtin`), `hook` (`identity.source: hook`) or `static` (`identity.source: static`). A missing `source`, or any other value, makes the whole file invalid. The freshness rules below key off it.
        - **The built-in provider:** `ranges` exactly `[builtin.subnet]`, `edge_port` 0, `gateway_ip` `""`, no `refreshed_at` / `stale_after`.
        - **Every other provider:** `edge_port` 9001–9047, unique; `gateway_ip` its IPv4 address on `portcullis-vpn`; `label` (the template's `vpn.label`).
        - **Freshness fields.** A provider with `source: hook` carries `refreshed_at` (its last good run) and `stale_after` = `refreshed_at + max(3 × refresh, 3 min)`; `stale_after` must be after `refreshed_at` and at most 30 min after it (3 × the 10 min refresh maximum), and a `refreshed_at` more than 2 min ahead of the reader's own clock makes the file invalid. A `hook` provider without either field, or with a span outside that, makes the whole file invalid, and every VPN request is denied by the edge and group-gate; a reader never treats a missing `stale_after` as fresh. Providers with `source: static` (an admin's map) or `source: builtin` carry neither field: either one on them makes the file invalid. Built-in devices end at their own `expires`.
        - **Before the first good run.** Until a hook provider's first successful hook run, the Hub leaves it out of the file: its addresses match no provider and are denied, and nothing else is affected. **`stale: true`** denies a listed provider's addresses whatever `stale_after` says.
        - **`ranges`**: 1–8 IPv4 prefixes, /8–/30, disjoint across the **whole file**, none overlapping a reserved range (§3.3; the readers take the core subnets from compose, `GATE_CORE_SUBNETS` / `WG_CORE_SUBNETS`).
    - **`devices`**:
        - `ip`: IPv4, unique across the whole file, inside its provider's ranges;
        - `provider`: an id of the file;
        - `user`: the lowercase LLDAP username, non-empty;
        - `device_id`: non-empty;
        - `name`: the device's name;
        - `expires`: RFC 3339 UTC or `null`; readers drop a device past it by their own clock.

        A `builtin` device counts only with a `builtin.peers` entry that has the same `ip` and `device_id` and hasn't expired.

    - **Fail closed.** Every VPN request is denied by the edge and group-gate when the file:
        - is missing (while anything needs it), unreadable or not one JSON document;
        - has an unknown key or version, a malformed timestamp, a `valid_until` that is missing, past or more than 1 h 5 min ahead, or a `refreshed_at` more than 2 min ahead;
        - breaks any rule above (overlapping ranges, a duplicate or out-of-range address, a missing or unknown `source`, a `hook` provider without `stale_after`, a `static` or `builtin` provider with it, and so on).

        A provider past its `stale_after`, or with `stale: true`, denies its own addresses only. Readers compare with their own clock, so a stopped Hub ends in deny. The Hub never writes a file its own reader refuses. The edge's and group-gate's readers and the Hub's reference reader run the same vectors file, `vpn_json_vectors.json` (the Hub's `internal/vpn/testdata/`, byte-copied to core's `tests/`).

- **How group-gate decides.** The VPN binding runs first, after the identity checks (above). Then come the membership checks (the reserved deny group, the host's group, `path_groups`, `expiring`): a signed-in person outside the app's groups gets the plain group `403`, never a step-up or needs-stronger page naming the app or its rule. Then the template check: for a request it picks the template from the normalised host: `core[host]` for a gated core host, `core["hub.<main domain>"]` for `auth.<main domain>`, else `hosts[host]`, else `default`. It takes the session's methods from the token's `amr`: each value mapped through the §8.1 table (`pwd` → `password`, `otp` → `totp` (**NEW, authenticator codes**), `spk` → `passkey_synced`, `file` → `browser_cert`, `dpk` → `passkey_device`, `hwk` → `security_key`, `mtls` → `yubikey_cert`; anything else, `inv` included, maps to nothing), kept only while the method is in `methods`. **NEW (authenticator codes):** group-gate's table has `AMR_TO_METHOD["otp"] = "totp"`, `METHOD_TENTHS["totp"] = 15`, `METHOD_WORDS["totp"] = "code from an authenticator app"` and `totp` second in `METHOD_IDS`; `STEPUP_METHODS` follows `METHOD_IDS`, so a step-up may ask for `pc_method=totp`. `totp` has no certificate binding (it isn't a certificate). A certificate method counts only when the **current request** presents a non-revoked certificate of its own kind whose CN is the session's user (the certificate binding below, [Sign-in methods → Certificate binding](../operations/auth-policies.md#certificate-binding)). An `all` group is met when every item is met, an `any` group when at least one is; a method item is met when the session has it. A met template lets the request through; an unmet one gets the present-certificate, step-up or needs-stronger page (§5). group-gate's `group_gate_requests_total` counts them with `result` `present_certificate`, `stepup` and `needs_stronger`.
- **Sign-in paths (NEW, sign-in part 2).** On `people.<main domain>` only, the rule is `{"op":"any","items":[every id in methods]}` instead of the `people` template (no methods → deny) when:
    - `normalize_path_candidates(raw)` doesn't raise, and
    - every candidate it returns is exactly `/signin` or exactly `/api/me/signin` (group-gate's `SIGNIN_EXACT`), under `/api/me/signin/` or under `/static/`, or (**NEW, sign-in part 3**), **only on a live impersonation** ("Impersonated requests" below), exactly `/impersonation/stop`, exactly `/api/me/impersonation` or exactly `/api/me/impersonation/stop` (`SIGNIN_IMPERSONATION_EXACT`), so Stop is always reachable. For any other session those three are ordinary `people.<main domain>` paths under the `people` template.

    Anything else, including an encoded `/` or `\`, gets the `people` template. Membership checks still run first (`people=*`). The same paths on `hub.<main domain>`, on any other core host or on an app host get that host's template. **Why the exception is safe:** anything on `/api/me/signin*` that adds a method needs a fresh sign-in under the `people` template (§8.1 "Fresh auth for adding a certificate") or the presented YubiKey certificate; everything else only reads or removes the caller's own data. The three impersonation paths only show the caller's own impersonation or end it (§5.1), and they skip the `people` template only for a request group-gate has already found live, so they give a weak session nothing it doesn't already have. Pinned by group-gate's `test_signin_paths_exact_after_normalising` and `test_imp_signin_paths`, and core's e2e `signin_page_reachable_weak` (which sends the raw, unnormalised path).

- **Certificate binding (NEW, sign-in part 2).** group-gate tells the two certificate kinds apart from the presented **leaf itself**, never from the Info text (Traefik doesn't escape `"`, `;` or `,` there, so a crafted CN could fake an issuer): every gated router passes the PEM (`client-headers@file` and `client-cert-pem@file` both set `passTLSClientCert` `pem: true`). group-gate parses the first certificate of `X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert` and verifies its signature against `GATE_YUBIKEY_CA_FILE` (`/etc/group-gate/ca/yubikey-ca.crt`, core's `certs/yubikey-ca.crt`: `pki_int`'s certificate) and `GATE_BROWSER_CA_FILE` (`/etc/group-gate/ca/browser-ca.crt`, core's `certs/browser-ca.crt`: `pki_file`'s), both read with Python `cryptography` and cached by (inode, mtime, size). The CA whose subject is the leaf's issuer and whose key verifies the leaf (`verify_directly_issued_by`) is its kind, and the user is its one subject CN (LLDAP grammar, exact: nothing stripped or folded). Equal subjects or CNs, a leaf both CAs verify, or a missing or unreadable file, means no certificate counts (fail closed).
    - `yubikey_cert` counts only when `mtls` ∈ amr and a non-revoked `pki_int` leaf with CN = the user is presented on this request.
    - `browser_cert` counts the same way, with `file` and a `pki_file` leaf.
    - A leaf of one kind never binds the other kind's method: a session with amr `mtls` presenting a `pki_file` leaf never has `yubikey_cert` (`test_browser_leaf_never_binds_yubikey`).
- **Revocation lists (NEW, sign-in part 2).** group-gate reads `GATE_CRL_URLS` and `GATE_DELTA_CRL_URLS`, each space-separated: core sets `http://vault:8200/v1/pki_int/crl http://vault:8200/v1/pki_file/crl` and `http://vault:8200/v1/pki_int/crl/delta http://vault:8200/v1/pki_file/crl/delta`. They are re-fetched every `GATE_CRL_REFRESH_SECONDS` (default 60). Its revoked set is the union of every CRL and the serial file (`GATE_REVOKED_FILE`, written by `./portcullis cert revoke|sync`, the union of both mounts' revoked serials). A request presenting a revoked certificate of either kind is denied on every host. A revocation made on the web rotates that mount's full CRL (§9.4), so it is enforced within 60 s. `GATE_CRL_URL` / `GATE_DELTA_CRL_URL` don't exist.
- **Opened log (NEW, sign-in part 2).** The first allowed request per `(session, host)` that a group-gate process sees appends one line to `group_gate_data/opened/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl` (UTC day; in group-gate `GATE_OPENED_DIR=/data/opened`). The line is `{"time","user","session","host","app","methods":[…],"ip","ua","act"}`:
    - `time` RFC 3339 UTC; `user` the lowercase username; `host` the normalised host; `app` the app's name from `portal-apps.json` by host, else the host; `methods` the session's method ids as group-gate counted them for this request (above), in the §8.1 table's order;
    - `session` is the token's `sid`, else `<user>@<auth_time>`;
    - `ip` is `X-Real-Ip`, and `ua` is the User-Agent, ≤ 256 characters;
    - `act` (**NEW, sign-in part 3**) is the administrator's username on an impersonated request ("Impersonated requests" below), else `""`.

    Remembered sessions sit in an in-memory LRU of 10 000: a restart may log one more line, and readers dedupe on `(session, host, day)`. A write failure never denies a request: it is logged and counted (`group_gate_opened_log_failures_total`). Ownership: the volume `group_gate_data` is owned `10003:10001`; group-gate runs as 10003 with `group_add: ["10001"]`; the `opened/` directory is mode 2770 with group 10001, and files are 0640. The Hub reads it and prunes it (§8.2).

- **Impersonated requests (NEW, sign-in part 3).** An administrator signed in as someone else (§8.1 "Impersonation") reaches group-gate with the person's forward-auth session, whose token carries the claims `act` = `{"sub": "<admin username>"}` and `pc_imp` = `{"id": "<32 lowercase hex>", "until": <epoch seconds>}`.
    - **The file.** group-gate reads `GATE_IMPERSONATION_FILE` (core sets `/hub-data/impersonation.json`, the Hub's file, §8.1 "The published file") with the stdlib `json`, cached by (inode, mtime, size). A missing, unreadable or invalid file, a `version` other than 1, or a file whose `written` is more than **300 s** old counts as unreadable: `allowed` false and nothing live. So a Hub that stopped writing ends every impersonation at group-gate within 5 minutes. A failure is logged once per change.
    - **The claims.** group-gate reads `act` and `pc_imp` only from the payload of `X-Forwarded-Access-Token`, never from `Authorization`. Neither claim present means not impersonated. Anything else that isn't exactly the shape above is malformed: one claim without the other, `act` not an object, `act.sub` not a username (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`), an `id` not `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`, an `until` that isn't a number. Client-sent `X-Forwarded-Impersonator` / `X-Forwarded-Impersonation` headers never count (Traefik deletes them, §5).
    - **Live.** An impersonation is live only when all of these hold: the file's `allowed` is true; its `sessions` has a record with the claim's `id`; that record's `ended` is `null` (it must be `null` or an RFC 3339 string; any other value makes the whole file invalid); its `admin` equals `act.sub`; its `target` equals the forward-auth username; and now is before both the claim's `until` and the record's `until`.
    - **Order.** The check runs on every request (the forward-auth path and `/portal`), after the username checks and before membership:
        1. malformed claims, claims that aren't live, or a token whose `preferred_username` isn't the forward-auth username → the **ended page** (`403`, on every host): "Your session as &lt;person&gt; has ended." with a link to sign out, `https://auth.<main domain>/oauth2/sign_out?rd=https%3A%2F%2F<main domain>%2F`; logged `DENIED … reason=impersonation_ended`;
        2. membership as today, for the person;
        3. the template (call 5): the session's methods come from `amr` as always, and they are the administrator's (§8.1). A certificate method counts only with a non-revoked leaf of its kind whose CN is the **administrator's** username (`bound_cert_method(leaf, act.sub)`): a certificate of the person's never counts. There is **never a step-up** and no present-certificate page: the person's session can't gain the administrator's methods. An unmet template gets the needs page in its impersonation form (`render_needs_page(…, impersonated=rec)`): "&lt;App&gt; needs &lt;methods&gt;. &lt;admin&gt;'s sign-in didn't use them, and a session as &lt;person&gt; can't add one: Stop, sign in with them, and start again.", with a Stop link, no "Set up" links and no `X-Stepup-URL`;
        4. on allow, group-gate adds `X-Forwarded-Impersonator: <admin>` and `X-Forwarded-Impersonation: <id>` (§5), and the opened log line has `act` = the administrator.

        Every page group-gate renders for a live impersonation carries the banner (§5 "The impersonation banner").

- **Unknown values fail closed.** A missing key, an unknown method id, a rule of another shape (an unknown `op`, an empty or over-long `items`, a family, a leaf not in `methods`, more than 4 levels, more than 48 leaves), a template id that `default`, `hosts` or `core` names but `templates` lacks, a gated core host missing from `core`, a `core` key that isn't a gated core host, **NEW (VPN):** a malformed `vpn` (a missing or unknown key, a host key that isn't a valid hostname, a `via` that isn't `["*"]`, `[]` or 1–8 provider ids, `devices_file` not `"vpn.json"`), any other key shape, a file that exists but can't be parsed, or a `version` other than 7 makes group-gate deny the request.
- **Version 7** (**NEW**, VPN; the Hub always writes 7). group-gate serves **only** version 7 and denies every request on a file of any other version, and the Hub has no version 6 writer. **The Hub and core must be upgraded together:** a group-gate from before this change serves only version 6, so it denies every gated request on the Hub's version 7 file, and every app and gated core page stays denied until core is upgraded. The same holds for `vpn.json` version 2.
- **`expiring`** is unchanged from version 4:
    - an array of `{"user": "<lowercase username>", "group": "<LLDAP group>", "at": "<RFC 3339 UTC timestamp>"}` entries for temporary group memberships. group-gate treats the membership as **absent** once `now >= at`, regardless of what the user's token says. Usernames are lowercase; timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC (e.g., `2027-03-31T23:59:59Z`).
    - The Hub writes **at most one entry** per `(user, group)` pair: the **earliest** `at` when multiple expiries exist for the same membership.
    - The Hub writes every pending expiry into this array so that expiry enforcement is strict even while the Hub is down. The Hub keeps publishing an expired entry until the membership is actually removed from LLDAP, plus a 10-minute grace period afterwards (cleared on regrant). One exception: the end of an "added" exception of a rule group is not written while the user is a current member, the group's rule matches them and the evaluator keeps them (they stay by rule after the end). Manual expiries and grace entries are always written.
    - **Which removals revoke Keycloak sessions.** The Hub signs the user out of Keycloak (`POST …/users/{id}/logout`) after: every membership the evaluator removes (rule, exception or expiry), an admin's member removal, a group deletion (every former member), and a password change; a user deletion removes the Keycloak copy. OIDC apps then lose access at their next token refresh, forward-auth sessions within about a minute (oauth2-proxy cookie refresh). Core runs Keycloak's LDAP federation with `cachePolicy: NO_CACHE`, so that refresh reads the user's current groups and attributes from LLDAP instead of a cached copy.
    - When group-gate strips an expired membership for a request, it also withholds `Authorization` and `X-Forwarded-Access-Token`. The `portcullis-groups` middleware lists both in `authResponseHeaders` and echoes them to the backend only when the request is allowed.
- **Keys are full hostnames** (**NEW**, policy v5). `hosts`, `groups`, `path_groups` and `public_paths` (**NEW (sign-in):** and `core`, for core hosts) are keyed by the lowercase hostnames that **enabled** instances route, e.g. `grafana.team-b.example.org` — never by template or instance id. A key is a **valid hostname**: at most 253 characters and matching `^([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` (lowercase, at least two labels, no port, no trailing dot, no wildcard). This page uses "valid hostname" in exactly this sense. Any other key shape makes group-gate deny.
- **`extra_domains`** (**NEW**, policy v5): every added domain (§12) the Hub knows, sorted, each a valid hostname. A host equal to or under one of them is an **extra-domain host** (§5); group-gate uses this to build the step-up URL.
