Refusals, in this order: `404` (as the page); `409` `{"state": "<state>"}` when it isn't pending (approved, declined, consumed or expired); `409` "type <check> to confirm" when the typed check doesn't match (nothing recorded); `403` with the fixed text "a fresh sign-in is required" when the proof fails (a method the confirmation's governing template doesn't accept included, §8), or when its `auth_time` is earlier than 60 s before the confirmation was created (a sign-in from before the request never approves it); `503` when the Hub can't verify proofs (as for credentials). A decline needs neither the typed check nor a proof. Refused approvals count toward the refused-save limit below (`429`)
  - **Fresh auth** (people.html): the page opens `authorize_url` in a popup with `response_type=code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope=openid`, a random `state` and `nonce`, `code_challenge` (S256) of a random verifier, `prompt=login` and `max_age=0` (**NEW, sign-in:** no `acr_values`; which methods count as fresh is the proof's rule, §8: a method the governing template accepts, a password included). **NEW (authenticator codes):** `freshauth.js` `start(fa, h)` adds `pc_method=totp` only when the view's `pc_method` (`fresh_auth.pc_method`, or an app's `fresh_pc_method`) is `"totp"` and only on a proof flow, never together with a `kc_action`; any other value is never sent. For the Sign-in page's authenticator actions it adds `kc_action` = `h.kcAction`, which must match `^(CONFIGURE_TOTP(:[0-9a-f-]{36})?|delete_credential:[0-9a-f-]{36})$` (else nothing is opened); `freshauth-callback.js` forwards Keycloak's `kc_action_status` to the opener (`msg.kc_action_status`, `""` when absent) and also accepts a callback that carries only `kc_action_status`. The popup lands on `https://people.<domain>/signin` (**NEW, sign-in part 2**; My apps and the Sign-in page use the same redirect URI, and `mysignin.html` loads `freshauth-callback.js` first in its `<head>`); the page there acts only when `window.opener` is same-origin, drops `code` / `state` from the URL at once (`history.replaceState`), posts them to the opener with `targetOrigin = location.origin` and closes; without an opener it ignores the parameters. Every page of the people listener is served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, so the `code` / `state` in the callback URL never reach a `Referer` header. The opener accepts only a message with `event.origin === location.origin` and its stored `state`, deletes its `sessionStorage` entries and posts `{code, code_verifier, nonce}`. The Hub exchanges the code itself (server-side, PKCE) and verifies the ID token (§8). **NEW (AI support):** the confirmation page uses exactly this popup flow on both listeners: on the Hub listener the popup lands on `https://hub.<domain>/`, where `index.html` runs the same callback handler, and every Hub-listener answer is served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` too. Each listener has its own verifier, whose redirect URI is `https://people.<domain>/signin` on the people listener and `https://hub.<domain>/` on the Hub listener (§8)
  - Common rules: no `X-Forwarded-User` is 401; a body over 4 KiB (credentials, confirmations and the Sign-in page's bodies: 8 KiB) is 413; unknown fields or trailing data are 400 with a fixed usage text; 4xx answers carry the Hub's text (never another person's name or value), 5xx a generic message. After **10 refused saves in a minute** (any 4xx, 404 included; 5xx never count) every save of that caller is `429` until the minute ends (in memory, per caller; refusals past the limit are not audited one by one). Admins on the Hub listener are never limited, except for refused confirmation approvals (§15.6), which count there too
  
  These are the **only** app-related routes on the people listener. They are read-only or self-service only (the caller's own data) and CSRF-guarded. The people listener's MCP endpoint (`people.<domain>/mcp`) is not one of its routes: core routes it to `mcp-gate` (§5), which forwards to the Hub's MCP listener (§15.7).

- **Sign-in page (NEW, sign-in part 2).** Every person's one place for their sign-in methods.
    - **The page.** `GET /signin` on the people listener, served as its own HTML (`web/mysignin.html` + `web/mysignin.js`, both in `web/web.go`'s `//go:embed` list; `mysignin.js` is in `peopleStatic`). It calls only the `/api/me/signin*` routes below, so it works for a session the `people` template wouldn't admit: group-gate applies "any switched-on method" to exactly these paths (§4 "Sign-in paths"). The people SPA's top nav has "Sign-in" (→ `/signin`), and the portal's "Sign-in methods" link (§10), group-gate's needs-stronger page (§5) and the extension's page (§8.1) all point at `https://people.<domain>/signin`.
    - **Routes.** People listener only, caller only (`X-Forwarded-User`, lowercased; no route takes a username), CSRF-guarded, under the common rules and refusal limit below. JSON names are snake_case.
        - `GET /api/me/signin` → `200` with the caller's view (`MySignIn`):

            ```json
            {
              "user": "alice",
              "methods": [
                {"id": "password", "label": "Password", "on": false, "state": "off"},
                {"id": "totp", "label": "Authenticator app", "on": true, "state": "set",
                 "authenticators": [{"id": "3e5a7c9b-1d2f-4a6b-8c0e-2f4a6b8c0d1e", "label": "Authenticator 2026-11-14 10:21:07", "created_at": "2026-11-14T10:21:07Z"}],
                 "remove_impact": ["Nextcloud"]},
                {"id": "passkey_synced", "label": "Synced passkey", "on": true, "state": "set",
                 "passkeys": [{"id": "6f1c2a9e-3b4d-4e5f-8a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b", "label": "iPhone", "kind": "passkey_synced", "model": "iCloud Keychain", "created_at": "2026-11-02T09:12:00Z"}]},
                {"id": "browser_cert", "label": "Browser certificate", "on": true, "state": "set"},
                {"id": "passkey_device", "label": "Device-bound passkey", "on": true, "state": "none"},
                {"id": "security_key", "label": "Security key", "on": true, "state": "set",
                 "passkeys": [{"id": "0b9d8c7a-6e5f-4a3b-9c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d", "label": "YubiKey 5C", "kind": "security_key", "model": "YubiKey 5 Series with NFC", "created_at": "2026-10-20T14:03:00Z"}]},
                {"id": "yubikey_cert", "label": "YubiKey certificate", "on": true, "state": "unknown"}
              ],
              "certificates": [
                {"serial": "1a:2b:3c", "kind": "browser", "status": "valid", "not_before": "2026-11-10T08:00:00Z", "not_after": "2026-12-10T08:00:00Z"}
              ],
              "apps": [
                {"kind": "instance", "id": "gitea", "name": "Gitea", "template": "standard", "template_name": "Standard", "score": {"tenths": 25, "reason": "…"}, "ok": true},
                {"kind": "core", "id": "people", "name": "People", "template": "strong", "template_name": "Strong", "score": {"tenths": 35, "reason": "…"}, "ok": true}
              ],
              "limits": {"limits": {"browser_cert_days": 30, "browser_cert_max_active": 3, "history_days": 365}, "ceiling_days": 30,
                         "effective": {"browser_cert_days": 30, "browser_cert_max_active": 3, "history_days": 365}},
              "active_browser_certs": 1,
              "max_authenticators": 3,
              "add_stronger": false,
              "fresh_auth": {"authorize_url": "https://auth.<domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/openid-connect/auth", "client_id": "portcullis-fresh-auth", "redirect_uri": "https://people.<domain>/signin"},
              "account_url": "https://auth.<domain>/realms/portcullis/account/account-security/signing-in",
              "cert_fresh": ["passkey_device", "security_key", "yubikey_cert"],
              "cert_fresh_refusal": "creating a certificate needs a passkey or YubiKey sign-in that people.<domain> accepts"
            }
            ```

            - `methods`: all seven methods in the §8.1 table's order. `state` is `set`, `none`, `unknown` (the inventory couldn't read that source, §8.1 "Inventory") or `off` (switched off: the page shows "off on this server"). `passkeys` (passkey kinds only, omitted when empty) and `password_set_at` (the Hub's record, omitted when none) are the caller's own. `label` is the method's name (§8.1 "Methods"). **NEW (polish 1):** each passkey is `{"id", "label", "kind", "model", "created_at"}`: `id` the Keycloak credential id, `label` its name (Keycloak's credential `userLabel`), and `model` the FIDO MDS v3 `description` for the credential's AAGUID. `model` is shown only, never stored, and is `""` when the AAGUID is zero, missing or not in the list (or the `credentialData` can't be read); the page then shows "unknown model".
            - **NEW (authenticator codes):** the `totp` row carries `authenticators` (omitted when empty, like `passkeys`): each `{"id", "label", "created_at"}` (`AuthenticatorRow`: the Keycloak credential id, its `userLabel` and `createdDate`), sorted by `created_at`; never a secret or `credentialData`. Its `state` is `unknown` while Keycloak can't be read, `set` with one or more authenticators, else `none` (`off` while `totp` is off; `none` for `admin`, `portcullis-hub` and every `portcullis-*` name, whose `otp` credentials the inventory drops). `remove_impact` (omitted when empty) is present when the caller has exactly one authenticator: the names of the caller's apps (`apps`) whose `ok` turns false without `totp`; the page lists them before it opens `delete_credential`. `max_authenticators` is `hub.MaxAuthenticators` (3): the page hides "+ Add authenticator app" at 3 (the extension enforces it, §8.1 "Authenticator-app codes"). `fresh_auth` carries `pc_method` and `refusal`, chosen for the caller under the `people` core template by the per-person rule of §8.1 "Fresh auth" (each omitted when empty).
            - `certificates`: the caller's YubiKey and browser certificates from enroll (§9.4), revoked ones included. `kind` is `yubikey` or `browser`; `status` is `valid`, `expiring` (fewer than `CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS` days left, default 7; the Hub reads `HUB_CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS`, which core passes through as `${CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS:-7}`, with core's grammar exactly, as `certs.sh` `cert_warn_seconds`: a value matching `^[0-9]+$` is used, `0` included; anything else, or unset, means 7; the Hub never refuses to start over it), `expired` or `revoked`.
            - `apps`: every enabled instance whose population includes the caller, plus the core pages `people` (everyone) and `hub` (administrators), each with the template that governs it, its score and `ok` = whether the caller has a set-up method that meets it (`null` while the inventory doesn't know the person).
            - `limits`: the limits view of §8.1 "Limits". `active_browser_certs` counts the caller's unexpired, unrevoked browser certificates. `fresh_auth` is the people listener's fresh-auth `{authorize_url, client_id, redirect_uri}` (§8).
            - `account_url`: the account console's signing-in page (`https://auth.<d>/realms/portcullis/account/account-security/signing-in`), where passkeys and security keys are added (`""` = no link); `cert_fresh`: the methods a fresh sign-in may use to create a certificate (`certFreshAllowed`, D26; `[]` when none); `cert_fresh_refusal`: the D26 `409` text (always present), which the page shows instead of opening the popup when `cert_fresh` is empty.

        - **NEW (authenticator codes):** `GET /api/me/signin?refresh=1` also marks the caller's inventory stale (`MarkInventoryStale`), at most once per 10 s per caller (a per-user timestamp in the Hub, `RefreshMySignIn`), bypassing the 30 s throttle once; more often, `refresh` is ignored, never an error. The page sends it after a fresh-auth popup ends. Being a `GET`, it also works while impersonated (read-only).
        - `GET /api/me/signin/history?before=<cursor: a page's next>&limit=<1–100, default 50>` → `200` `HistoryPage` (§8.2). A malformed `before` or a `limit` out of range is `400`.
        - `POST /api/me/signin/browser-certificates` `{"days", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` (≤ 8 KiB) → `200` `{"p12": "<std base64>", "password": "XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX", "filename": "<user>-browser-certificate-<YYYYMMDD>.p12", "certificate": <the new CertRow>}` (its `not_before` is the Hub's clock at the answer, not Vault's) with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. This answer is the only place the `.p12` and its password reach the browser; neither is logged, cached, audited or stored, and the private key can't be downloaded again (§9.4). Refusals, in this order: `409` "browser certificates are off on this server" when `browser_cert` is off (enroll isn't called); `400` when `days` isn't 1 to the effective `browser_cert_days`; `409` "creating a certificate needs a passkey or YubiKey sign-in that people.<domain> accepts" when no method may approve it (D26, below; checked before the proof, so it isn't spent); `403` "a fresh sign-in is required" for a refused proof (the reason audited only); `503` when the Hub can't verify proofs (§8); then enroll's answer: `409` "you already have <n> browser certificates, the most allowed: revoke one first", `404`, `400` passed through with enroll's text. One create at a time per person (a per-user lock); the Hub passes `days`, `max_days` = the effective `browser_cert_days` and `max_active` = the effective `browser_cert_max_active` to enroll. Audited `cert.create`, detail `browser <serial> until <date>`.
        - `DELETE /api/me/signin/certificates/{serial}` → `204`. The caller's own browser certificates only: a YubiKey certificate's serial or someone else's is `404`. No fresh auth: it only removes access. Audited `cert.revoke`. A revoked certificate stops working within 60 s (§4 "Revocation lists").
        - `POST /api/me/signin/yubikey-certificate/renew` `{"csr": "<PEM>"}` → `200` `{"certificate": "<PEM>", "serial", "not_after"}`. The people router passes the presented certificate (`client-cert-pem@file`) in `X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert`: base64 DER without BEGIN/END lines, possibly URL-escaped, comma-separated, leaf first. The Hub (`presentedCertPEM`) takes the first entry, decodes it to DER, checks that it parses as X.509, and sends real PEM to enroll (§9.4). **Only a YubiKey (`pki_int`) leaf renews:** the Hub also checks that the leaf's serial is one of the caller's unexpired, unrevoked `kind: yubikey` records in enroll's `GET /internal/certificates`, and enroll checks the issuer again (§9.4). A missing or unparsable header, or a leaf that isn't the caller's YubiKey certificate (a browser certificate included), is `403` "present your current YubiKey certificate"; enroll's `403` / `400` texts are passed through. `409` "YubiKey certificates are off on this server" while `yubikey_cert` is off; the protected-name `409` (below) comes before anything else; more than one `X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert` value is `403` "present your current YubiKey certificate". No fresh auth: the TLS session and the CSR's signature both prove possession of the key. Audited `cert.renew`.
        - `PUT /api/me/signin/password` `{"password", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` (≤ 8 KiB) → `204`. Refused (`409`) while the password method is off; `400` with `CheckPassword`'s text (12–128 characters, not the username, not a common password, §8.1 "Passwords"); the proof is under `FreshAccepted(peopleRule)` and its method is on the D26 allowlist (below): a strong method always, `password` or (**NEW, authenticator codes**) `totp` only when the person already has a password under their current account, anything else never. The Hub records `sign_in.passwords.<user>` with `set_by` = the caller.
        - `DELETE /api/me/signin/password` → `204`. LLDAP can't clear a password, so this sets a random 32-byte one nobody sees and drops the Hub's record. No fresh auth.
        - **NEW (polish 1):** `PUT /api/me/signin/passkeys/{credentialId}/label` `{"label": "…"}` (≤ 8 KiB) → `204`. Renames one of the caller's own passkeys. No fresh auth: it only changes a name.
            - The label is trimmed, then must be 1–64 runes, valid UTF-8, with no control or bidi character; otherwise `400` "a passkey name is 1–64 characters on one line".
            - Only the caller's own passkey, by Keycloak credential id. Anything else (another person's credential, a credential that isn't a passkey, an id that isn't a UUID) is `404` "no such passkey".
            - The label must be unique among the caller's **other** credentials, case-insensitively (recasing a passkey's own name is not a duplicate); otherwise `409` "you already have a sign-in method named “&lt;label&gt;”". This is because Keycloak refuses duplicate labels.
            - The Hub calls Keycloak's `PUT /admin/realms/portcullis/users/{id}/credentials/{credentialId}/userLabel` (`text/plain`, the label as the body) and marks the person's inventory stale, so the next view shows the new name.
            - It is refused while impersonated (`RefuseWhileImpersonated`, "Read-only while impersonated" below), counts toward the refusal limit, and is audited `signin.passkey.label`: detail `<old> → <new>` when it succeeds, `credential <id>` when it is refused.
        - **NEW (authenticator codes):** `PUT /api/me/signin/authenticators/{credentialId}/label` `{"label": "…"}` (≤ 8 KiB) → `204`. Renames one of the caller's own authenticator apps, with the passkey rename's rules (above), its own texts and its own audit action. No fresh auth: it only changes a name.
            - `400` "an authenticator name is 1–64 characters on one line";
            - only the caller's own `otp` credential: anything else (a passkey's id, another person's credential, an id that isn't a UUID) is `404` "no such authenticator app" (`keycloak.ErrAuthenticatorNotFound`; `SetAuthenticatorLabel` refuses a non-`otp` id, as `SetPasskeyLabel` refuses an `otp` one);
            - `409` "you already have a sign-in method named “&lt;label&gt;”" for a duplicate among the caller's other credentials, case-insensitively;
            - refused while impersonated, counts toward the refusal limit, audited `signin.authenticator.label` (detail `<old> → <new>`, or `credential <id>` when refused).
        - **NEW (authenticator codes): adding, replacing and removing an authenticator app** never go through a Hub route. The page opens Keycloak's application-initiated actions in the fresh-auth popup (above): **+ Add authenticator app** `kc_action=CONFIGURE_TOTP`, **Replace** `kc_action=CONFIGURE_TOTP:<credential id>`, **Remove** the stock `kc_action=delete_credential:<credential id>` (Keycloak's own confirmation and re-authentication, `max_auth_age` 300 s). The `CONFIGURE_TOTP` override (§8.1 "Authenticator-app codes") is the only gate: the switch, the reserved accounts, impersonation, the add-stronger cap, the limit of 3 and the replace id. "+ Add" is hidden at `max_authenticators` and when `totp` is off ("off on this server"); with `add_stronger` off and no set-up method of at least 1.5 it shows "ask your admin for a setup link" instead, the same copy as for passkeys. After the first add, the page recommends a second app. The account console's own "Authenticator application" section runs through the same override and `delete_credential`.

        Administrators may create and revoke their **own** browser certificates and renew their own YubiKey certificate here like anyone else; `admin`, `portcullis-hub` and every `portcullis-*` name can't (`409` "this account's certificates are managed from the server: ./portcullis cert revoke <serial>"). The people listener registers **only** these D25 routes under `/api/me/signin/` (**NEW, polish 1:** `PUT /api/me/signin/passkeys/{credentialId}/label` included; **NEW, authenticator codes:** `PUT /api/me/signin/authenticators/{credentialId}/label` included); any route added there later that adds a method must need a fresh-auth proof under D26 (below), because group-gate lets any switched-on method reach these paths (§4 "Sign-in paths").

        Own password changes and removals sign the person out of Keycloak, like every password change (§4). Both are refused for `admin` and `portcullis-hub` (`409` "Password sign-in isn't available for this account"). Audit actions: `cert.create`, `cert.revoke`, `cert.renew`, `signin.password` (detail `self set` / `self removed`), `signin.passkey.label` (**NEW, polish 1**, above), `signin.authenticator.label` (**NEW, authenticator codes**, above). No audit entry ever holds the `.p12`, its password, a CSR, a certificate or a proof.

    - **Fresh auth for adding a certificate (D26).** Creating a browser certificate (the caller) and issuing a YubiKey certificate (an administrator, §9.7) need a fresh-auth proof (§8) under the `people` core template (`freshGov` for the people listener):
        - `pc_fresh` must be in `signin.FreshAccepted(peopleRule)` **and** (**NEW, authenticator codes:** an allowlist) be one of `passkey_synced`, `passkey_device`, `security_key`, `yubikey_cert` (`strongFreshMethods`, `certFreshAllowed`): a password, a copied certificate file, a phishable code or any method added later never mints a new certificate (`cert_fresh` never lists `password`, `browser_cert` or `totp`);
        - when that set is empty, the answer is `409` "creating a certificate needs a passkey or YubiKey sign-in that people.<domain> accepts";
        - a refused proof is the standard `403` "a fresh sign-in is required", with the reason audited only;
        - setting your own password needs a proof under `FreshAccepted(peopleRule)` whose method is on an allowlist (**NEW, authenticator codes**; `passwordFreshAllowed`): a strong method (`strongFreshMethods`: `passkey_synced`, `passkey_device`, `security_key`, `yubikey_cert`) sets one; `password` or `totp` (`passwordChangeFreshMethods`) only changes one the person already has under their current account, never adds the first (audited reason "pc_fresh names <method>, but there is no password yet: …"); anything else (`browser_cert`, a copied certificate file, or any method added later) is refused (`403` "a fresh sign-in is required", the reason audited only);
        - add-stronger (§8.1) doesn't apply separately: the fresh method is already at least as strong as a browser certificate.

- **VPN page — NEW (VPN).** A person's VPN devices from every provider, and their built-in devices (§16).
    - **The page.** `GET /vpn/` on the people listener serves its own HTML (`web/vpn.html` + `web/vpn.js`). Core routes `` PathPrefix(`/vpn/`) `` on `people.<main domain>` through the **`people-vpn-enrol`** router:
        - priority above `people`;
        - the `people` router's full chain, forward-auth and group-gate included: every `/vpn/` route needs a signed-in person;
        - service `hub-people`;
        - on `${PORTCULLIS_WEB_ENROL:-websecure}`, with its twin `people-vpn-enrol-vpn` on `vpnsecure` (§5).

        In `server` mode, with `PORTCULLIS_VPN_PUBLIC_ENROL=true` the router stays on `websecure` (reachable from the internet, still behind sign-in); with `false` it is parked and only the twin answers. Public enrolment never means unauthenticated. Everything the page needs is under this prefix.

    - **VPN assets.** `GET /vpn/assets/{file}` serves the page's own files, from an allowlist (`vpnAssets`) that includes its own copies of the fresh-auth scripts (`freshauth.js`, `freshauth-callback.js`). In server mode `/static/` is VPN-only, so internet enrolment needs these copies. Any other `{file}` is `404`.
    - **Fresh auth.** The page signs in again through the fresh-auth client with the redirect URI `https://people.<domain>/vpn/` (§8), and sends the proof as `code`, `code_verifier` and `nonce` (as the Sign-in page does, above). The proof's sign-in must be at most **5 min** old and be the caller's; otherwise `403`.
    - **Keys stay in the browser.** The page generates the X25519 key pair with WebCrypto, POSTs only the public key, assembles the WireGuard config text and its QR code in the page, shows them once, and drops the private key from memory. It never stores the key (no `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` or `indexedDB`), and the Hub never returns config text.
    - **Routes.** People listener only, caller only (`X-Forwarded-User`, lowercased), CSRF-guarded, under the common rules above. JSON names are snake_case.
        - `GET /vpn/api/devices` → `200` with the caller's devices from **every** provider, static assignments included, each a `VPNDeviceView`:

            ```json
            {"id": "<16 hex>", "provider": "builtin", "provider_label": "<label>", "name": "laptop",
             "address": "10.213.0.5", "last_seen": "2026-11-13T09:23:00Z", "expires": "2027-11-13T14:30:00Z",
             "online": true, "managed": true}
            ```

            `managed` is true for built-in devices, the only ones that can be renamed, removed or renewed; the others are managed in their app. `last_seen` and `expires` are RFC 3339 UTC or `null`. The Sign-in page's "VPN devices" card reads the same route.

        - `POST /vpn/api/devices` `{"name", "public_key", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` → `201` `VPNDeviceConfig`:

            ```json
            {"address": "10.213.0.5", "server_public_key": "<base64 public key>", "endpoint": "portcullis.example.com:51820",
             "allowed_ips": "10.213.0.1/32", "dns": "10.213.0.1", "mtu": 1280}
            ```

            `endpoint` is `<main domain>:<people port>` (the apex). The Hub allocates the next free address of the built-in subnet (§16) and publishes `vpn.json` (§4); `wg` picks up the peer on its next read. The device expires after the Settings expiry (§11.7). Refusals:

            - `403` without a valid fresh-auth proof (above);
            - `409` while the built-in provider is off;
            - `403` for a person outside the VPN users group;
            - `400` for a `public_key` that isn't 32 bytes of base64;
            - `409` for a `public_key` any device already uses;
            - `409` "at most <n> devices" at the devices-per-person limit.

            Audited `vpn.device_added`, never with key material.

        - `PUT /vpn/api/devices/{id}` `{"name"}` → renames one of the caller's built-in devices. Audited `vpn.device_renamed`.
        - `DELETE /vpn/api/devices/{id}` → removes one of the caller's built-in devices. Its address is quarantined for 7 days (§16). Audited `vpn.device_removed`.
        - `POST /vpn/api/devices/{id}/renew` `{"public_key", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` → `200` `VPNDeviceConfig`. Renewal **re-keys**: the same id and address with a new public key, behind a fresh-auth proof. Audited `vpn.device_added`.

        `id` is a device id the caller owns; another person's is `404`. The people listener registers exactly these seven routes under `/vpn/`.

- **Mail passwords — NEW (mail; §19.6).** A section "Mail passwords" of the Sign-in page (`mysignin.html` / `mysignin.js`), shown only when `GET /api/me/mail` answers `200`. People listener only, caller only (`X-Forwarded-User`, lowercased; no route takes a username), CSRF-guarded, under the common rules, the refusal limit and "Read-only while impersonated" (below). Bodies ≤ 8 KiB. For anyone not in `mail_users` every route answers the same `404`.
    - `GET /api/me/mail` → `200`:

        ```json
        {"addresses": ["alice@example.com", "alice@team-b.example.org"], "server": "mail.example.com",
         "imaps": 993, "submissions": 465, "submission": 587, "username": "alice@example.com",
         "passwords": [{"id": "m3f9a0c1d2e4b5a67", "label": "iPhone", "created_at": "2026-11-15T09:00:00Z", "expires_at": null, "last_used": null, "status": "active"}]}
        ```

        `server` is `MAIL_HOSTNAME`, `username` the primary address (the login), `passwords` the caller's `MailPasswordView`s (§19.9): active ones and those reset by a restore (`voided`: "reset by a restore"), never a secret. `404` (the shared answer) also while `PORTCULLIS_MAIL=off`. It needs no fresh auth; the page's `fresh_auth` (`GET /api/me/signin`) covers the popup.

    - `POST /api/me/mail/passwords` `{"label": "…", "expiry": "none"|"90d"|"1y", "code": "…", "code_verifier": "…", "nonce": "…"}` (the fresh-auth proof flat, as every Sign-in page route) → `201` `{"id", "password", "mobileconfig_b64"}` (`id` the Hub's row id, §13.16) with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. This answer is the only place the password ever appears. `mobileconfig_b64` is an unsigned Apple configuration profile (`com.apple.mail.managed`, IMAP `MAIL_HOSTNAME`:993 SSL, SMTP `MAIL_HOSTNAME`:465 SSL, username the primary address, the password for both), base64, built in memory and never stored. Checks, in this order (the proof is consumed only at step 7):

        1. the caller's refusal limit (`429`);
        2. `PORTCULLIS_MAIL=on`, a wired mail provider reachable with `bootstrap: true`, no void owed and no hold (§19.9); else `503` "mail isn't running right now";
        3. the caller in `mail_users`; else the shared `404`;
        4. `label` 1–64 characters on one line and a known `expiry`; else `400`;
        5. fewer than 5 active mail passwords; else `409` "at most 5 mail passwords: revoke one first";
        6. the caller's LLDAP uuid read; else `503`;
        7. the fresh-auth proof under the **`people` core template** (`govCore("people")`, the governing template of every Sign-in page action, so the popup's `pc_method` and the check agree; §8 "Fresh auth"); else `403` "a fresh sign-in is required" (the reason audited only), `503` when the Hub can't verify proofs;
        8. the provider's `POST /v1/credentials` (§19.5);
        9. the metadata row (§13.16), then the audit `mail_credential.create` (the id and the label's length, never the secret), then the answer. The Hub zeroes the password and the profile once the answer is written.
    - `DELETE /api/me/mail/passwords/{id}` → `204`: revokes one of the caller's own mail passwords (reason `revoked`, `revoked_by` the caller), also when it was already gone. No fresh auth: it only removes access. Another person's id is `404`. Audited `mail_credential.revoke`.
    - **Fresh auth** uses the Sign-in page's popup and redirect URI `https://people.<domain>/signin` unchanged.

- **Signing in as someone else (NEW, sign-in part 3).** The impersonating browser's routes (§8.1 "Impersonation"; the start and the administrators' stop are directory routes, §9.7):
    - **Read-only while impersonated.** Both listeners wrap their handlers as `ProxySecret(RefuseWhileImpersonated(CSRF(…)))`. While `X-Forwarded-Impersonation` is present (any value, empty included; only group-gate sets it, §5) or the `X-Forwarded-Access-Token` payload has an `act` or `pc_imp` claim (any value), every request that isn't `GET` or `HEAD` is refused with `403` "not while you are signed in as someone else: Stop first", except `POST /api/me/impersonation/stop`. That covers My apps values, file-share passwords, AI connections, passwords, certificates, confirmations and every delegated directory action. Reads work.
    - **`GET /api/me/impersonation`** → `200` `{"active": null}`, or, only when `X-Forwarded-Impersonation` names the running impersonation whose person is the caller, `{"active": {"person", "admin", "reason", "until", "stop_url"}}` (`until` RFC 3339 UTC; `stop_url` = `https://people.<domain>/impersonation/stop`). Another id, another person's, an ended one, one past its `until`, or any while the switch is off answers `null`.
    - **`POST /api/me/impersonation/stop`** (CSRF) → `200` `{"sign_out": "https://auth.<domain>/oauth2/sign_out?rd=https%3A%2F%2F<domain>%2F"}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. It ends the impersonation the header names, when its person is the caller (`how` `stopped`, by the administrator; a Stop from the impersonating browser is audited with actor = the record's `admin`); otherwise `404`. The page then goes to `sign_out`: oauth2-proxy deletes the session's ticket and cookie, and the backend logout runs.
    - **The Sign-in page while impersonated (NEW, polish 1).** While the browser is signed in as you, the Sign-in page offers no action and says "Changes are off while &lt;admin&gt; is signed in as you."
    - **`GET /impersonation/stop`**: the Stop page (`web/impersonation-stop.html`), with a "Stop signing in as &lt;person&gt;" button that does the POST above, or "Nothing to stop" when the browser isn't impersonating.

    The three paths are Sign-in paths (§4), so Stop is reachable whatever the `people` template needs.

## 6. Engine access

Neither Traefik nor the Hub mounts the engine socket (`PORTCULLIS_ENGINE_SOCKET`) directly. Each gets its own socket proxy, on its own internal network:

| Client | Proxy endpoint | Allowed |
|--------|----------------|---------|
| Traefik | `tcp://socket-proxy-traefik:2375` | read-only (`POST=0`): containers, networks, events, version, ping |
| Hub | `tcp://socket-proxy-hub:2375` | containers, images, networks, volumes, exec, events, info, version, ping, logs, plus POST/PUT/DELETE. No build, commit, swarm, nodes, services, tasks, plugins, secrets, configs, system (df/prune), auth, distribution or session |

The Hub reads `DOCKER_HOST` for both the `docker compose` CLI (only `up`/`down`) and its own Engine API calls (status, logs, exec, events, and for instance backups (§11.5): volume list / inspect / create / remove, image pull of the fully qualified helper image, container create / remove and the archive endpoints `GET`/`PUT /containers/{id}/archive`). `CONTAINERS`, `IMAGES`, `VOLUMES` and `POST=1` above cover it, plus `ALLOW_ARCHIVE=1`: the proxy denies `/containers/{id}/archive` without it (the Hub's exec rights already reach any container's files, so it adds no new kind of access). Core CI checks that only the two proxies mount the socket and that each proxy network has exactly its two members. See [Security & Hardening](../operations/hardening.md#docker-socket-proxies).

**The engine socket — NEW (rootless).** Core runs on rootful Docker or on rootless Podman, chosen once by `./portcullis init` and kept in core's `.env` as `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=docker|podman`. "The engine socket" is the host path in core's `.env` key `PORTCULLIS_ENGINE_SOCKET`: `/var/run/docker.sock` under Docker (the default), the operator's `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock` under Podman.

- **Mount.** Each proxy mounts exactly `${PORTCULLIS_ENGINE_SOCKET:-/var/run/docker.sock}:/var/run/docker.sock:ro`, read-only, and no other service mounts it. Core CI matches that exact source string. The Podman socket speaks the Docker-compatible API, so the proxies, their images, their environment and their allowlists are the same on both runtimes.
- **libpod is always denied.** `/libpod/…` and `/v*/libpod/…` (Podman's own API, which includes `play kube`, `generate` and `machine`) never match an allowed section, so both proxies answer `403`. So does `/build` (`BUILD` stays off): under Podman the CLI builds core's local images itself before `up`. Core CI checks these denials on both proxies.
- **The Hub's runtime.** Core's compose sets the Hub env `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` from `CONTAINER_RUNTIME` (`${CONTAINER_RUNTIME:?…}`, so a missing value stops compose). The Hub requires it: a value other than `docker`, `podman` or (**NEW, Kubernetes**) `kubernetes`, or none, refuses the start (`kubernetes`: "On Kubernetes", below). At start the Hub asks the engine's `/version` and compares the names in `Components[]`: `Podman Engine` means podman, `Engine` (without a `Podman Engine` entry) means docker. It keeps asking until it gets an answer.
    - Until the answer agrees with `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME`, and permanently once it contradicts it, every engine operation and every compose run answers **`503`** `the container engine is not verified: <why>` (for example `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=docker but the engine is Podman Engine`). Only `/_ping` and `/version` pass meanwhile, and the compose plugin's own version check, which never reaches the engine.
    - A contradiction is fixed only by restarting the Hub against the right engine. The doctor reports it as `runtime_mismatch` (§14.5).
    - `GET /api/runtime` (§11.10) shows the state.

**Compose's environment — NEW (apps).** The Hub runs `docker compose` with only an allowlisted environment, never its own: `HOME` and `PATH` from the Hub's environment (the docker CLI's config directory and credential helpers), plus `DOCKER_HOST` (the Hub's, as above) and `COMPOSE_IGNORE_ORPHANS=true`, which the Hub sets. Nothing else of the Hub's environment (its secrets, `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `HUB_PROXY_SECRET`, …) reaches compose, so a template's `${NAME}` can't read it. Every instance variable comes only from the instance's `--env-file` (§11.9), and the Hub interpolates the project for its checks from exactly the same environment and env file. `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, the TLS variables, `DOCKER_API_VERSION` and the HTTP proxy variables are not passed: compose reaches the same daemon as the Hub's Engine API calls, through `DOCKER_HOST` only.

**Helper containers.** The Hub uses two kinds, both labelled `io.portcullis.hub.helper` and both removed at Hub start if one was left behind (§11.5 Leftovers):

- **Volume helper** (§11.5), **created but never started.** The daemon itself reads and writes the one volume it mounts, through the archive endpoints. Unchanged.
- **Folder fixer** (§14), **started.** Docker's archive endpoints can't change group owners recursively, set modes in place or write ACLs, so shared folders need a process. It is the only helper that runs:
    - **Image:** the Hub's own image, by **image ID** (`sha256:…`), found by inspecting the Hub's own container by its **full container ID**, read from `/proc/self/mountinfo` (the `…/docker/containers/<64 hex>/` root of the `/etc/hostname`, `/etc/hosts` or `/etc/resolv.conf` mount; **NEW (rootless):** under `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman` instead the `…/overlay-containers/<64 hex>/userdata/<file>` root of those mounts, in the graph root or in the run root; every such mount must name the same ID). The answer's ID must equal it and carry core's compose labels `com.docker.compose.project=portcullis` and `com.docker.compose.service=hub`; any failure is the `503` below, with no fallback to the hostname (a name or short-ID prefix another container could shadow). No new image to trust or pull. `HUB_FIXER_IMAGE` (must contain `@sha256:`) replaces it for development only: it is honoured only with `HUB_DEV=1` and refused otherwise (an env-selected, root-capable image would be a privilege pivot). Image not found: every folder disk operation answers `503` "the Hub can't find its own image".
    - **Command:** `Entrypoint` is the full argv `["/usr/local/bin/hub", "folderfix", <mode>, <flags>…]`, built from a Go struct, never a shell; `Cmd` is empty. Modes `probe`, `scan`, `snapshot`, `apply`, `restore`, `restore --dry-run` (§14.2–14.4) and **`childfix`** (**NEW**, file sharing: `childfix --rel <tree> --child <name>:<uid> --expect-uid <uid> --expect-dev/--expect-ino/--expect-mount-root <the child's>`, exactly one child; every component opened `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` and its fd's device/inode compared with the lstat, the owner and mode changed through that fd; refused — exit 2, nothing changed — when the child is a symlink, not a directory, another mount (its own dataset/subvolume: "fix it on the host"), another device/inode/mount root than expected, or owned by another uid than `--expect-uid`; caps `CHOWN`, `FOWNER` only (the tree's path must be searchable by others); §14.6 `person_tree_owner`). `scan --top-only` reads a per-person tree's first level only. Paths aren't secrets, and no secret is ever passed.
    - **Isolation:** `User "0:0"`, `NetworkMode "none"`, `no-new-privileges`, read-only rootfs, `CapDrop: ALL`, `Privileged false`, no devices, no port bindings, pids 16, memory 256 MiB, `Healthcheck {Test: ["NONE"]}` (the Hub image's own `HEALTHCHECK` would run `wget`), `LogConfig {Type: "json-file"}` (the report is read from the logs), no `Tty` / `OpenStdin`, `AutoRemove false` (the Hub removes it), label value `folder:<id>` for a folder's runs.
    - **Mounts:** one bind mount (`Type: bind`, never the `Binds` string form), at `/folder`: the folder (or a hand-typed path the doctor scans), read-only for `scan` and `snapshot`. `probe` binds the folder's **bind root** at `/broot` instead (read-only; read-write only for `probe --create`). Anonymous scratch volumes `/out` (`snapshot`) and `/in` (`restore`) only where the mode needs them; removing the container removes them. Docker's `CreateMountpoint` is never used: it would create a missing host path following host symlinks in its ancestors. Missing directories are created by `probe --create` (`mkdirat` under an `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` fd of `/broot`, with no capability beyond `DAC_READ_SEARCH`; any failure is a `409`) and by `apply --mkdir` inside the folder.
    - **Capabilities by mode** (each the measured minimum; the Hub's `docker`-tagged CI test drops each in turn): `probe`, `scan`, `snapshot`, `restore --dry-run` and (**NEW, usage**) `usage` → `DAC_READ_SEARCH`; `apply`, `restore` → `CHOWN`, `FOWNER`, `FSETID`, `DAC_READ_SEARCH`, plus `DAC_OVERRIDE` for an `apply` with `--mkdir` only; `childfix` → `CHOWN`, `FOWNER`. **`childfix`** (a per-person tree's top-level directory, §13.17): its preview is a read-only probe that records the child's device, inode and mount root (the folder path rules and the Docker-root rule apply, as for doctor scans), and the plan hash covers them; the apply probes again, opens the child `O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` relative to the tree, refuses a symlink, a non-directory or another mount (exit `2`), then `fchown <uid>:<uid>` and `fchmod 0700` through that fd. Not recursive: nothing inside the child changes. `DAC_READ_SEARCH`: read and search entries uid 0 doesn't own (a `0750` directory of uid 1000). `CHOWN`: the new group (and owner under `must_own`). `FOWNER`: `fchmod` and the `system.posix_acl_*` xattrs of entries uid 0 doesn't own. `FSETID`: the fixer runs as uid 0, which isn't in the folder's group, so without it the kernel clears setgid when it sets a directory's mode or access ACL. `DAC_OVERRIDE`: `mkdirat` in a directory uid 0 has no write bit on; every other change goes through an open fd, which no write permission check applies to. `SETFCAP` is never given (it guards `security.capability`, which the fixer never writes). A `chown` clears setuid/setgid bits whatever the capabilities, so the fixer sets the mode again after changing the owner (order in §14.2).
    - **Run:** create → copy `/in` (restore) → start → wait for not-running (called after start; a timeout kills it and fails the run) → logs (demuxed) → copy `/out` (snapshot) → remove, always, also on failure. Exit `0` = done, `2` = refused (`409` with the report's first error; nothing changed), `1` = failed (`500`). The report is the last non-empty stdout line, one JSON document (≤ 256 KiB, decoded strictly; stderr ≤ 16 KiB, crashes only).
    - **Refusals before any run:** a daemon whose `Info` reports `userns` in `SecurityOptions`, or `rootless` unless `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman` (ids inside the helper are translated: owners would read as 65534 and ACL entries would be written for the wrong ids) → `503`, explain-only. **NEW (rootless):** under Podman the fixer itself also refuses (exit `2`, nothing changed) any `/proc/self/uid_map` or `gid_map` that is neither the identity nor the **consistent shape**: exactly two ranges, container `0` → the operator (one id, not host root) and container `1` → one subordinate range of at least 65536 ids. Every container then shares that one mapping, so the ids the fixer writes, ACL entries included, are the ids the apps see (§14.2 for the report and unmapped owners). Every run on a **defined** folder (after its create) passes the folder root's stored device and inode (`--expect-dev`, `--expect-ino`) and its stored mount root (the root field of `/folder`'s line in `/proc/self/mountinfo`, recorded at create and at every path change, §14.1); the fixer exits `2` with nothing changed when `/folder` isn't that directory or its mount root isn't **exactly** the stored one (a symlink Docker resolved on the host). Check path, the create-time probe and scans of hand-typed paths have nothing stored yet and run unchecked.
- **Proxy flags.** `CONTAINERS` and `POST` (plus the existing `ALLOW_LOGS`, `ALLOW_ARCHIVE` and `INFO`) already cover create, start, wait, kill, logs, archive and info. **No flag of `socket-proxy-hub` changes.** The compose `up` path already starts containers through the same proxy.

**Resource usage (NEW, usage; §11.11).** The Hub's usage sampler and storage measurer read the engine through `socket-proxy-hub` with **no flag change**. `SYSTEM` (`/system/df`), `ALLOW_TOP` (`/containers/{id}/top`) and every `LIBPOD_*` stay off, and core CI asserts that they still answer `403` through the proxy on both runtimes. No new socket mount, no third proxy, no cAdvisor and no host collector.

- **`CONTAINERS`:**
    - `GET /containers/json?all=1` (the existing list), every 15 s.
    - `GET /containers/{id}/stats?stream=false&one-shot=true`, one sample per running in-scope container (§11.11 "Scope") every 15 s, at most 4 at once, 5 s each, 12 s per sweep, at most 256 containers. The body is capped at 1 MiB and decoded into the Hub's own struct, so an absent field stays absent (`null`) and is never read as `0`. Only `read`, `cpu_stats.cpu_usage.total_usage`, `memory_stats.usage`, `memory_stats.stats.inactive_file` (cgroup v2) or `total_inactive_file` (v1), `pids_stats.current`, the `networks{}` byte counters and `blkio_stats.io_service_bytes_recursive` (ops `read` / `write`, case-insensitive) are kept. `precpu_stats` is never used: CPU is the Hub's own Δ`total_usage` / Δ`read` between two samples.
    - `GET /containers/{id}/json` (inspect) on first sight and every 5 min. Copied **field by field**: `HostConfig.Memory`, `NanoCpus`, `CpuQuota`, `CpuPeriod`, `PidsLimit`, `NetworkMode`, `State.OOMKilled`, `State.StartedAt`, `RestartCount`, and `Mounts[]` type, name, source, destination and RW. Everything else, `Config.Env` included, is dropped at once and never logged, stored or returned.
    - `GET /containers/{id}/json?size=true` (`SizeRw`, the writable layer), once per storage run per container, 10 s each.
- **`IMAGES`:** `GET /images/{id}/json` (`Size`), once per storage run per image.
- **`INFO`:** `GET /info` (`NCPU`, `MemTotal`) at start and hourly.
- **Errors.** An engine error is logged without its body; the API says `stats unavailable` for that container. On a guard refusal (above) the sampler records the guard's message and keeps the last numbers with their age.

**The fixer's `usage` mode (NEW, usage).** `hub folderfix usage --root=/vol --max-entries=2000000 --max-time=2m0s` measures one volume or one hand-typed bind for the storage measurer (§11.11). It is the folder fixer above with these differences:

- **Mount:** exactly one, at **`/vol`**, read-only: a named volume (`Type: volume`, `VolumeOptions.NoCopy: true`, never a copy-up) or a bind (`Type: bind`, never the `Binds` string form, never `CreateMountpoint`). A started helper with a writable volume mount is refused before it is created. A bind source at or under an engine root dir (the Docker-root rule, §14.1) is refused, and so is a hand-typed path inside a shared folder (the folder's own scan measures it).
- **Capabilities:** `DAC_READ_SEARCH` only. Label value `usage:<target>` (the volume name or path, clipped to 200 characters). Helper wall timeout `max-time + 30 s`.
- **Walk:** the fixer's walk (`O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` directory fds, symlinks never followed, mount points counted and not crossed), `fstatat` and `getdents` only: no file is ever opened for reading. The helper sets its own IO priority to the idle class (`ioprio_set(IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, 0, IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE)`), best effort.
- **Report:** the scan report's shape with `mode: "usage"` (the folder fields at their zero values):

    ```json
    {"version":1,"mode":"usage","root":"/vol","fs_type":"ext4","alloc_bytes":0,"apparent_bytes":0,
     "entries":0,"dirs":0,"files":0,"hard_links":{"n":0},"mount_points":{"n":0},"failed":{"n":0},
     "free_bytes":0,"total_bytes":0,"dev":0,"io_idle":true,"partial":false,"partial_reason":""}
    ```

    `alloc_bytes` = Σ `st_blocks × 512` (what `du -s --block-size=1 -x` reports); an inode with `nlink > 1` is counted once, through a `(dev, ino)` set of at most 1,000,000 entries, past which the report is `partial` with `partial_reason` `hard_links`. `apparent_bytes` = Σ `st_size`. `io_idle` (usage only, omitted otherwise) says whether the idle IO class was set. `partial_reason` is also `entries` or `time` (a cap hit) or `failed` (entries that couldn't be read, counted in `failed.n`).

- **`scan` gains** `alloc_bytes` and `apparent_bytes` (no version bump; an older cached scan without them reads as "not measured yet").
- **Exit codes:** `usage` exits `0` when entries couldn't be read (`partial: true`, `partial_reason: "failed"`), `2` on a refusal, `1` on a crash. `scan` keeps exiting `1` on failed entries.

**Exec with stdin (§13.8).** The Hub runs `POST /containers/{id}/exec` with `AttachStdin: true` and hijacks the connection to send JSON on stdin to the process. Used for hooks that receive the full desired state.

**Split output for AI hooks (NEW, AI support; §15.5).** `ai` hooks run through the same exec endpoint with `Tty: false`, and the Hub demultiplexes stdout and stderr into two separate capped buffers (stdout ≤ 64 KiB, more is a failure; stderr the first 16 KiB), never one merged stream: a credential printed on stdout can't reach the stderr text that a failure records. No proxy flag changes.

**Container kill (§13.8).** The Hub sends signals with `POST /containers/{id}/kill?signal=<HUP|USR1|USR2>` for reload actions. No change to `socket-proxy-hub` (already `CONTAINERS` + `POST`).

**Restarting the mail provider's sessions (NEW, mail provider; §19.6).** The Hub restarts no core container. A mail server may check a session's credential only at AUTH, so an IMAP IDLE session and an authenticated SMTP session can survive a destroyed mail password and a disabled account. The provider has no engine access, so the Hub ends those sessions within the 8 s budget by restarting the wired provider's `sessions.restart` service (§3.5) after **every** removal and every revoked mail password: once the removal's document is applied (`applied_generation` reached, at most 4 s), or when that wait times out. This is required, not a fallback. Several removals within one restart's time share one restart.

- **Target.** `RestartService(project, service)`: exactly the one non-one-off container whose labels are `com.docker.compose.project=portcullis-<wired instance>` and `com.docker.compose.service=<sessions.restart>`, listed through the guarded engine client; zero or more than one match is an error and nothing is restarted. The Hub calls it for that one project and service only, never for another instance or a core service.
- **Call.** `POST /containers/{id}/restart?t=2` through `socket-proxy-hub` (`CONTAINERS` + `POST`: no proxy flag changes), as the runtime's `Restart(ctx, id, timeout)` verb, bounded at 30 s. Never under `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes` (the verb answers unsupported; mail isn't available there, §19.12).
- **Failure.** Logged, op record `mail_restart`, and doctor `mail_rate_held` with the line "mail sessions may still be open" (§14.5).

**Per-person secrets volume (NEW, file sharing; §13.16).** File-share password hashes live on their own volume, never on `hub_data`:

- **Core** declares the volume `hub_secrets` (`name: portcullis_hub_secrets`), mounts it into the Hub at `/secrets` and sets `HUB_SECRETS_DIR=/secrets` and `HUB_SECRETS_VOLUME=portcullis_hub_secrets` (the defaults). `./portcullis init`, `upgrade` and `restore` make sure the volume root is owned by `10001:10001` with mode `0700` (through the fully qualified helper image, as restore already does for volume roots). Core's backup never copies it and core's restore empties it (§11.5, §11.6). Before any destructive step the restore takes down (`compose down`, volumes kept) every app project with a container mounting the volume — any failure, or a container left, aborts with nothing restored — and lists them afterwards: they are started again from the Hub (drift shows them not running), never by the restore, since their credentials were just voided.
- **The Hub** checks at start that `HUB_SECRETS_DIR` is owned by its own uid and is mode `0700`. Otherwise it fails closed: the credential routes (§5.1, §13.16) answer `503` and every instance with a `person_secret` option refuses to enable or start, naming the reason. It keeps one directory per (instance, option) on the volume: `<secrets>/<instance>/<key>/` (`0700`) holding one `<username>.nt` per active credential (`0600`, 32 uppercase hex characters and `\n`), all owned by uid 10001, plus `<secrets>/.epoch` (§11.6). The directory exists before every `up` of the instance.
- **The Hub's override** mounts it into the option's `mount.service` only, read-only, as a subpath of the external volume:

    ```yaml
    volumes:
      portcullis-hub-secrets:            # reserved key (§3)
        external: true
        name: portcullis_hub_secrets     # HUB_SECRETS_VOLUME
    services:
      <mount.service>:
        volumes:
          - type: volume
            source: portcullis-hub-secrets
            target: <mount.path>
            read_only: true
            volume: {subpath: <instance>/<key>}
    ```

    So a container sees only its own instance's and option's hash files, never another instance's. Before every `up` the Hub checks the rendered project (template, Hub override and custom override merged): every top-level volume whose resolved name is `HUB_SECRETS_VOLUME`, under **any** key, is mounted only by `mount.service`, with exactly that subpath, read-only, and only through the key `portcullis-hub-secrets`; anything else refuses the `up` (`409`). Templates and custom overrides can't name the key, and can't declare a volume with that name (§3: templates may not name an external volume `portcullis*`; the custom override may not set `external` or `name` on any volume).

- **Requirements:** Docker Engine API **≥ 1.45** (Docker Engine 26.0, the first with volume subpath mounts) and `docker compose` **≥ 2.26.0** (the first release that passes `volume.subpath` to the Engine; **NEW (apps):** the Hub's own compose ≥ 2.27.2, the first that reads `COMPOSE_PROFILES` from the env file, §13.18). The Hub refuses to start with an older compose (its startup version check), and before every `up` of an instance that mounts the secrets volume it checks the daemon's API version (an older daemon would ignore the subpath and mount the whole volume: refused). Under rootless Podman per-person passwords are refused (`409` "per-person passwords need Docker for now"): Podman's compat API ignores compose volume subpaths.
- **Proxy flags:** none change (volume mounts are part of the container create the Hub already does through compose).

**VPN networks and the `vpn_doc` volume (NEW, VPN; §16).** None of these goes through the engine: `wg` never touches the engine socket.

- **`portcullis-vpn`** (internal, `${PORTCULLIS_VPN_NET:-172.31.254.0/26}`): `wg` (`.3`) and the wired providers' gateways only. `wg`'s edge listens there; Traefik is **not** on it.
- **`portcullis-vpn-edge`** (internal, `${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_SUBNET:-172.31.254.64/28}`, dynamic range `${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_IP_RANGE:-172.31.254.72/29}`): exactly Traefik (`${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_TRAEFIK_IP:-172.31.254.66}`) and `wg` (`${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_WG_IP:-172.31.254.67}`). Traefik's `vpnsecure` listens on `.66:8443` and trusts PROXY v2 only from `.67`.
- **`portcullis-metrics-wg`** (internal): `wg` (alias `wg-metrics`, metrics on `wg-metrics:9100`) and Prometheus only.
- **`vpn_doc`** (a core volume, owned `10001:10007`, setgid, mode 2750; the file 0640): holds `vpn.json` (§4). The Hub mounts it read-write at `/vpn-doc` (`HUB_VPN_DOC_DIR`, `HUB_VPN_DOC_GID=10007`); `wg` and group-gate mount it read-only and are in group 10007. `wg` has no `hub_data` mount and no group 10001.

**Workers — NEW (multiple servers; §17).** On a worker the socket rule holds for **`socket-proxy-agent`**; the agent API (§17.4) is the only remote access to an engine; no Engine API on any network.

- **Mount.** On a worker `${PORTCULLIS_ENGINE_SOCKET:-/var/run/docker.sock}:/var/run/docker.sock:ro` is mounted only into `socket-proxy-agent` (the same image, environment, allowlist and limits as `socket-proxy-hub`, the libpod and `/build` denials included), on its own internal network `socket-proxy-agent` whose only other member is the agent (`AGENT_ENGINE=tcp://socket-proxy-agent:2375`). Core CI counts the literal: twice in `docker-compose.yml`, once in `docker-compose.worker.yml`.
- **The agent** is the only client of that proxy. It runs `docker compose -p portcullis-<id>` from its bundles with the same allowlisted environment as the Hub (above), and nothing the primary sends is executed outside the routes and scopes of §17.4.
- **Helpers on a worker.** The volume helper is the pinned helper image, as on the primary (§11.5). The folder fixer is the **agent's own image** by image ID (found as the Hub finds its own, from the agent's container, which carries `com.docker.compose.project=portcullis-worker` and `com.docker.compose.service=agent`), with `Entrypoint` `["/usr/local/bin/portcullis-agent", "fixer", <mode>, <flags>…]` and otherwise the isolation, capabilities, mounts and run of the fixer above; the Hub sends no image reference. Binds are only under the worker's folder roots.
- **The engine's Info.** The doctor's and the fixer's refusals (`userns`, `rootless`) use the worker's own `/v1/info` (§17.4), with the worker's `CONTAINER_RUNTIME`.

**Link networks and the `link_doc` volume (NEW, multiple servers; §17.2).** None of these goes through the engine either. **`portcullis-link`** (internal, `${PORTCULLIS_LINK_NET:-172.31.254.80/29}`): exactly the Hub (`.82`) and `wg` (`.83`, link's control CONNECT listener on `:3128`). **`portcullis-link-data`** (internal, `${PORTCULLIS_LINK_DATA_NET:-172.31.254.128/26}`, dynamic range `172.31.254.160/27`): `wg` (`.130`, the data CONNECT listener on `:3129`) and the relays only. **`link_doc`** (a core volume, owned `10001:10009`, setgid, mode 2750; the file 0640): holds `link.json`; the Hub mounts it read-write at `/link-doc` (`HUB_LINK_DOC_DIR`, `HUB_LINK_DOC_GID=10009`), `wg` read-only in group 10009. The link's UDP port is published on `wg-egress`.

**On Kubernetes — NEW (Kubernetes).** Under `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes` there is no engine socket and there are no socket proxies. The Hub talks to the Kubernetes API with its in-cluster ServiceAccount (core's chart sets `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes`, `HUB_SELF_IMAGE` and `HUB_APPS_NAMESPACE`), and reads its own inputs (`core.env`, the LLDAP, invite, domains and `mcp-gate` secrets) from mounted Secrets, as on Docker.

- **Traefik's ServiceAccount** has one read-only Role, in the **edge namespace only**: `get`, `list` and `watch` on `services`, `secrets`, `endpointslices` and the `traefik.io` objects. The edge namespace holds no Secret (TLS comes from the file and HTTP providers and ACME), and Traefik has nothing in the core namespace or the apps namespace. Nothing cluster-scoped, and no `nodes` (the features that read nodes, the Ingress and Gateway providers, are off). No app object may reference a Secret: the templates validator and the translator never write one into a Traefik object, and the admission policy refuses it (`traefik`, below).
- **The Hub's Roles** are the Kubernetes form of `socket-proxy-hub`: the Role `portcullis-hub` in the apps namespace, and a second Role `portcullis-hub` in the edge namespace with only `create`, `update`, `patch`, `delete`, `get`, `list` and `watch` on `traefik.io` `ingressroutes` and `middlewares` and on core `services` (the apps' routes and their pinned ExternalName Services, §5). There is **nothing in the core namespace** and nothing cluster-scoped. The apps-namespace Role:

    | Resources | Verbs |
    |---|---|
    | `deployments`, `jobs`, `services`, `persistentvolumeclaims`, `configmaps`, `secrets`, `networkpolicies` | `create`, `update`, `patch`, `delete`, `get`, `list`, `watch` |
    | `pods` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `watch`, `delete` (never `patch` or `update`: a pod is restarted through its Deployment's pod template, §13.8) |
    | `pods/log` | `get` |
    | `pods/exec` | `create` only, **never `get`** (`create` is enough for every client and transport; `get` alone opens a WebSocket exec, as it does on every supported Kubernetes release) |
    | `events` | `list`, `watch` |
    | `metrics.k8s.io` `pods` (**NEW, usage**) | `get`, `list` (read-only pod metrics for the Usage page, §11.11; never `nodes`, `nodes/stats` or `nodes/proxy`) |

    Each Role object must equal these rules exactly: the Hub keeps them as `internal/runtime/kube/testdata/role.yaml` and `role-edge.yaml`, core's chart keeps byte copies (`charts/portcullis/files/hub-role.yaml`, `hub-role-edge.yaml`), and core CI compares them. RBAC can't limit what the Hub puts in a pod spec: the admission policies below do.

- **The cluster guard.** `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes` uses the in-cluster configuration, and `HUB_SELF_IMAGE` (the Hub's own image by digest, which the CLI resolves from the running Hub pod) is required: without it the Hub refuses to start. The Hub runs these checks, in this order, at start, every 60 s and **before every deploy** (create, enable, restart, restore, a Stop's undo; the deploy waits for the run):
    1. the in-cluster configuration loads, and the cluster check (below) passed and is at most 24 h old;
    2. its `SelfSubjectRulesReview` in the apps namespace holds every rule of the apps Role above, and in the edge namespace every rule of the edge Role, and in each nothing outside those rules plus the rules every authenticated user has: `create` on `selfsubjectaccessreviews`, `selfsubjectrulesreviews` (`authorization.k8s.io`) and `selfsubjectreviews` (`authentication.k8s.io`), and `get` on the discovery and health `nonResourceURLs` (`/api`, `/api/*`, `/apis`, `/apis/*`, `/openapi`, `/openapi/*`, `/version`, `/version/`, `/healthz`, `/livez`, `/readyz`). `get` on `pods/exec` is an extra verb. In the core namespace it holds only those defaults;
    3. the admission self-test (below);
    4. its own NetworkPolicy probe (below).

    Until all four hold, every runtime operation answers **`503`** `the cluster is not verified: <why>`, and a failed run before a deploy refuses that deploy the same way.

- **The cluster check.** The Hub never reads cluster-scoped objects. At every `./portcullis up` and `upgrade`, and at every `./portcullis kube check`, the CLI, with the operator's kubeconfig, verifies that the apps namespace `HUB_APPS_NAMESPACE` exists with its PSA labels (below) and that the six bindings below are live (each as a binding labelled `portcullis.io/binding: <name>`), and writes the result to the ConfigMap **`portcullis-cluster-check`** in the core namespace: `checked_at` (RFC 3339 UTC), `ok` (`true` or `false`) and `why` (empty when `ok`). The chart mounts it read-only into the Hub pod at **`/run/portcullis/cluster-check/`** (one file per key: `checked_at`, `ok`, `why`); it is a ConfigMap of the pod's own namespace, so the Hub's Role needs nothing in the core namespace. The Hub refuses every deploy while it is missing, says `ok: false`, or is older than 24 h, and while its own admission self-test fails.

    **Refresh.** `init` on Kubernetes installs the system units **`portcullis-kube-check.service`** (a oneshot running `./portcullis kube check` as the operator, `After=network-online.target` and, when this host runs k3s, `After=` / `Requires=k3s.service`) and **`portcullis-kube-check.timer`** (`OnCalendar=*-*-* 00/6:00:00`, `RandomizedDelaySec=10min`, `Persistent=true`), so the check is rewritten every 6 h. Without systemd, or when the install fails, `init` warns and prints the manual steps (run `./portcullis kube check` at least every 20 h). `./portcullis kube check` exits 1 when the check fails, and records the reason for the Hub. `./portcullis status` warns once the check is 20 h old, and counts it missing, failed or 24 h old as a problem.

- **The admission policies.** Core is the **only editor** of `kube/admission/` (`policies.yaml`, `bindings.yaml`, `params.yaml`, the vectors' params, and `params.tmpl.yaml`, the key list); the Hub keeps byte copies of the first three in `internal/runtime/kube/testdata/admission/` for its envtest vectors, and core CI compares them. `./portcullis init` and `upgrade` install six `ValidatingAdmissionPolicies`, each with its own binding (a binding binds exactly one policy): `portcullis-apps-{pods,workloads,services,traefik,netpol}`, bound by **`portcullis-apps-guard-<policy>`** to the apps namespace, and `portcullis-edge-routes`, bound by **`portcullis-edge-guard-routes`** to the edge namespace `portcullis-edge`. The CLI sets each binding's `namespaceSelector` from `PORTCULLIS_APPS_NAMESPACE` and the edge namespace, so an apps namespace other than the default is bound too. Every binding has `paramRef` → the params ConfigMap in the core namespace with `parameterNotFoundAction: Deny`, `validationActions: [Deny]`, `failurePolicy: Fail`.

    **Params generations.** The params' **generation** is the first 16 hex digits of the sha256 of every other `key=value` line, sorted. The CLI never rewrites live params: it creates the ConfigMap `portcullis-admission-params-<generation>` in the core namespace, then each binding as `<name>-<generation>` on it (labels `portcullis.io/binding: <name>`, `portcullis.io/params-generation: <generation>`), and probes them live (below). Only once the probe passes are the other generations' bindings deleted; their params ConfigMaps go after a 300 s grace. Until then the older bindings judge too (stricter, never weaker). A probe that fails within 60 s refuses the setup and keeps the older bindings. After a new generation the CLI re-judges every `owner: hub` object of the edge namespace through the live policies and deletes, naming it, one they now refuse.

    **The probe.** As the Hub's ServiceAccount, server dry-run: one object per binding annotated `portcullis.io/params-generation: <generation>` must be refused by `<binding>-<generation>` with `admission probe: params generation <generation> in effect` (each policy refuses exactly its own params' generation first, and lets other generations' probes by); a route on a reserved core host must be refused by `portcullis-edge-guard-routes`, and the same route on a free host admitted.

    **The params** (keys of `params.tmpl.yaml`; values are strings, lists space-separated, peer selectors `<namespace>:<label>=<value>`): `hubImage` (the Hub's digest), `hubServiceAccount` (`system:serviceaccount:<core namespace>:portcullis-hub`, the Hub's ServiceAccount `portcullis-hub`), `bindRoots`, `corePorts` (80, 443, the VPN port, 8000, 8081, 8443, 8444), `podCIDR`, `serviceCIDR`, `nodeAddresses` (`PORTCULLIS_KUBE_NODE_ADDRESSES`, §2, each as `/32`), `apiAddresses` (the addresses of `PORTCULLIS_KUBE_API_ENDPOINTS`, each as `/32`), the peer selectors `kubeDNS` (`kube-system:k8s-app=kube-dns`), `traefik`, `mcpGate` and `wg` (`<core namespace>:portcullis.io/component=traefik|mcp-gate|wg`), `fileMiddlewares` (the `@file` names of §5 "Traefik on Kubernetes", middlewares and the three services), `cliUsername` (the CLI's own identity, from `kubectl auth whoami` at setup), `appsNamespace`, `edgeNamespace` (`portcullis-edge`), `edgeCoreMiddlewares` (core's own Middlewares of the edge namespace, §5), `reservedHosts` (the apex and every core subdomain, from the chart's `core-routes.json`), `maxAppPriority` (the highest priority an app route may have) and `generation`. The CLI refuses to write params without a node address, an API endpoint, its own identity or the domain.

    **The CLI's exemption.** A request whose `request.userInfo.username` is `cliUsername` (Helm and `kubectl` run as it; the chart's objects carry `portcullis.io/owner: core`) passes every check except the generation probe's. No other identity is exempt.

    They refuse:

    - **pods** and **workloads** (the same rules: `portcullis-apps-pods` on `pods`, `portcullis-apps-workloads` on the pod template `spec.template.spec` of `deployments` and `jobs`), for every container, init container and ephemeral container:
        - the full PSA baseline: `privileged`, host namespaces (`hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, `hostIPC`), `hostPort`, `windowsOptions.hostProcess`, capabilities beyond the Kubernetes baseline (§3.4), a seccomp profile `Unconfined`, an AppArmor profile `Unconfined` (field or annotation), `seLinuxOptions` with a `user` or `role` or a `type` other than `container_t`, `container_init_t`, `container_kvm_t` or `container_engine_t`, a `procMount` other than `Default`, sysctls outside the baseline's safe set;
        - a `hostPath` outside the bind roots;
        - **a pod with any `hostPath` volume** (the Hub's helpers aside) unless every container, init and ephemeral included, is provably non-root (`runAsNonRoot: true` or an effective `runAsUser` above 0) with `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and an explicit effective `runAsGroup` above 0; and with no pod `runAsGroup`, `fsGroup` or supplemental group 0 (files it creates in host folders would otherwise be root's or group 0's), and unless the pod sets `supplementalGroupsPolicy: Strict` (the kubelet then adds no group from the image's `/etc/group`, which could hold 0; beta and on by default from Kubernetes 1.33, the floor). The Hub's translator sets it on every pod with a host path;
        - a `serviceAccountName` other than `default`, and a pod without `automountServiceAccountToken: false`;
        - a pod without `portcullis.io/instance`, `portcullis.io/instance: portcullis-probe` on anything but the Hub's probe pods, and a Secret, ConfigMap or PVC reference (volumes, projected sources, `envFrom`, `valueFrom`) whose name doesn't start with `<the pod's portcullis.io/instance value>--` (§11.2): the label is what owns an object, and the `--` prefix can't belong to another instance. The template-files ConfigMap is the instance's own, `<instance>--tpl-<hash10>`, so it needs no other prefix;
        - CNI annotations (`cni.projectcalico.org/*` and the like);
        - `portcullis.io/vpn-slot` other than an integer 0–46, or on a pod without an instance label;
        - **helpers:** a pod with `portcullis.io/helper` whose value isn't `fixer` or `volume`, whose image isn't `hubImage`, that carries a network label, or that isn't created by `hubServiceAccount` (`request.userInfo.username`). Only such a pod may run as root, and only it gets the capability exception: a `fixer` pod may add `DAC_READ_SEARCH` (the only fixer capability outside the baseline), a `volume` pod exactly `CHOWN`, `DAC_OVERRIDE` and `FOWNER`. No other pod gets either;
        - **probes:** a pod with `portcullis.io/probe` that isn't one of the Hub's probe pods: image `hubImage`, command `hub helper listen` or `hub helper idle` (the dialer `hub helper dial`), `portcullis.io/instance: portcullis-probe`, no volume, no capability, a non-root user and no other `portcullis.io/*` label;
    - **workloads** also refuses a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/service-account-token`, `replicas` above 1, and a helper label on a Deployment or Job (helpers are pods only). It judges two more kinds:
        - **Secrets**: an update or delete of a Secret whose old object isn't `portcullis.io/owner: hub` with an instance label, and an update that changes either label (`only the Hub's own Secrets (portcullis.io/owner=hub, an instance label) may be changed or deleted; owner and instance can't change`);
        - **PersistentVolumeClaims** (create, update and delete): a claim of another StorageClass than `portcullis-apps`, with `volumeName`, `dataSource` or `dataSourceRef`, not named `<instance>--…` after its `portcullis.io/instance` label, or without a 3-digit `portcullis.io/mode` (an optional leading 0; no setuid, setgid or sticky bit); and an update or delete of a claim whose old object isn't `portcullis.io/owner: hub` with an instance label and named `<old instance>--…`, or an update that changes either label. Two exact changes by the cluster's own controllers are exempt, matched by the request's username: the volume binder (`system:serviceaccount:kube-system:persistent-volume-binder` or `system:kube-controller-manager`) setting `spec.volumeName` once, from empty (the only way `volumeName` gets set), and the PVC protection controller (`system:serviceaccount:kube-system:pvc-protection-controller` or `system:kube-controller-manager`) removing only the finalizer `kubernetes.io/pvc-protection`, with spec, labels and annotations unchanged. Every other identity or change is judged as usual;
    - **services** (create, update and delete): an update or delete of a Service whose old object isn't `portcullis.io/owner: hub` with an instance label, or an update that changes either label; a Service without `portcullis.io/instance` or not named `<instance>--…` or `portcullis-mcp-<instance>--…`, `NodePort`, `ExternalName`, `externalIPs`, a `nodePort`, a LoadBalancer without `allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false`, a `clusterIP` / `clusterIPs` in the service network's static band (its first min(max(16, size / 16), 256) addresses, where the core Services' fixed IPs live; the API server allocates a clusterIP before admission, so a requested one can't be told from an allocated one), and a LoadBalancer on a core port;
    - **traefik** (`portcullis-apps-traefik`): every `traefik.io` object in the apps namespace (`<kind> is refused in the apps namespace: Traefik objects live in portcullis-edge`); only the CLI's own probe objects reach its later checks;
    - **edge routes** (`portcullis-edge-routes`, on every `traefik.io` and core `services` create, update and delete in the edge namespace), for every identity but `cliUsername`:
        - any kind but `IngressRoute`, `Middleware` and `Service` (so no `IngressRouteTCP` / `IngressRouteUDP`, `ServersTransport`, `TLSOption`, `TLSStore` or `TraefikService` object);
        - a Service that isn't the pinned ExternalName shape (§5): type other than `ExternalName`, a selector, a cluster IP, external IPs or load balancer fields; a name other than `<instance>--<svc>` after its own `portcullis.io/instance` label (the part after the prefix one DNS label without `--`) or an `externalName` other than exactly `<name>.<appsNamespace>.svc.cluster.local`; ports other than 1–16 entries `{name: tcp-<port>, port, protocol: TCP}` with no `nodePort` or `appProtocol` and `targetPort` (if set) = `port`;
        - an object without `portcullis.io/owner: hub` and a non-empty `portcullis.io/instance`; an update or delete of an object that isn't `owner: hub` (core's objects are the CLI's); an update that changes either label; a writer other than `hubServiceAccount`;
        - a route with `parentRefs` (Traefik's multi-layer routing would make it a child of another IngressRoute, core's included) or `ingressClassName`, or a route `syntax` other than `v3` (or unset);
        - a Middleware not named `<instance>--<name>` after its own `portcullis.io/instance` label (one DNS label after the prefix, no `--`), so no instance can take another's middleware name;
        - an IngressRoute whose `entryPoints` are unset, empty, or hold anything but `websecure` and `vpnsecure`; a `portcullis.io/reach: vpn` route off `vpnsecure`, unless every route's first middleware is `vpn-required-path@file` or `portcullis-public-guard@file` (§5 "Entrypoints");
        - a `match` other than `Host(…)` (one or more, joined by `||`, lowercase DNS names) with an optional `&& Path(…)` / `PathPrefix(…)` (joined by `||`): no `HostRegexp`, `HostSNI`, `ClientIP`, header or method matcher, no catch-all; a `Host` that is a reserved core host or a subdomain of one (`reservedHosts`); a `priority` above `maxAppPriority`; a route without `tls`;
        - a route service that is neither the instance's own edge Service (`<instance>--<svc>`, no `namespace`) nor a `kind: TraefikService` reference to `group-gate@file`, `forward-auth-ext@file` or `mcp-gate@file` (no `namespace`);
        - a middleware (on a route or in a `chain`) that is neither the instance's own (`<instance>--…` in the edge namespace, never one of `edgeCoreMiddlewares`) nor on `fileMiddlewares`;
        - `tls.options` outside the four tiers (§5: `authaware@file`, `public@file`, `protected@file`, `protected-any@file`), a `certResolver` other than `letsencrypt`, `tls.domains` (no certificate requests for other names), a `tls.secretName` or a TLS store;
        - a Middleware with other than exactly one type of the Hub's allowlist (`addPrefix`, `stripPrefix`, `stripPrefixRegex`, `replacePath`, `replacePathRegex`, `redirectRegex`, `redirectScheme`, `headers`, `compress`, `contentType`, `chain`, `rateLimit`, `inFlightReq`, `ipAllowList`, `buffering`, `retry`, `circuitBreaker`, `grpcWeb`; so never `forwardAuth`, `errors`, `plugin`, `basicAuth`, `digestAuth` or `passTLSClientCert`), a `rateLimit` / `inFlightReq` with a `redis` address, and a Middleware that sets an `X-Portcullis-*` request or response header;
    - **netpol** (create, update and delete): an update or delete of a NetworkPolicy whose old object isn't `portcullis.io/owner: hub` with an instance-shaped selector, or an update that changes its owner or instance, so the chart's `default-deny` can't be deleted or rewritten; a NetworkPolicy whose `podSelector` doesn't carry exactly one `portcullis.io/instance` value together with a `portcullis.io/net-<N>`, `portcullis.io/egress`, `portcullis.io/service` or `portcullis.io/vpn-slot` key (so no instance policy selects a helper pod), every NetworkPolicy while the params carry no `nodeAddresses` or no `apiAddresses` (fail closed), a port range (`endPort`), a rule with no `from` / `to` (all peers), an empty or `{}` `namespaceSelector` or `podSelector`, and every peer that isn't one of the shapes the Hub generates (§5 "Traefik on Kubernetes"):
        - a pod of the same instance (same `portcullis.io/instance`, ingress and egress);
        - `traefik` or `mcpGate`, as ingress only;
        - `kubeDNS`, on port 53 only;
        - `wg`, on port `9001 + n` only, from a policy whose `podSelector` has `portcullis.io/vpn-slot: "<n>"`;
        - an `ipBlock` `0.0.0.0/0` whose `except` contains `podCIDR`, `serviceCIDR`, `169.254.0.0/16`, every entry of `nodeAddresses` and every entry of `apiAddresses`;
        - an `ipBlock` that is one entry of `nodeAddresses`, on ports 80 and 443 only.

        The one exception is a policy selecting `portcullis.io/probe` whose peers are probe pods only.

    PSA on the apps namespace is `enforce: privileged`, `warn` and `audit: baseline` (built-in PSA can't allow `hostPath` under a prefix, so the policies enforce the baseline). The core namespace is PSA `restricted`.
