```json
 "tls":{"spki_sha256":["99ad5d8130ef75b24fa9a72e9ca7d0db45cee16a25405bdaa9d317a6d9dac9c6"]},
 "confirm_mass_removal":false,
 "domains":[{"name":"example.com","dmarc_start":"reject","dmarc_floor":"reject","mail":"on","dnssec":"secure"},
            {"name":"team-b.example.org","dmarc_start":"none","dmarc_floor":"none","mail":"on","dnssec":"unsigned"}],
 "accounts":[{"username":"alice","uuid":"6f1c2a9e-3b4d-4e5f-8a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b","display_name":"Alice A.","addresses":["alice@example.com","alice@team-b.example.org"],"quota_bytes":10737418240},
             {"username":"bob","uuid":"0b9d8c7a-6e5f-4a3b-9c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d","display_name":"Bob B.","addresses":["bob@example.com"],"quota_bytes":10737418240},
             {"username":"root","uuid":"3e5a7c9b-1d2f-4a6b-8c0e-2f4a6b8c0d1e","display_name":"Root","addresses":["root@example.com"],"quota_bytes":10737418240}],
 "aliases":[{"address":"sales@example.com","username":"alice"}],
 "lists":[{"address":"team@example.com","members":["alice","bob"],"posting":"members"}],
 "postmaster":["root"],
 "limits":{"recipients_per_hour":300,"recipients_per_day":1000},
 "spam":{"reject_score":15,"junk_score":5,"dnsbl":{"spamhaus":true,"spamcop":true,"barracuda":true},"allow":["example.org"],"block":["spam@example.net"]},
 "local_networks":["10.0.0.0/8"]}
```

- `version`: exactly 2. `generation`: an integer the Hub increases on every document (it saves `state.yaml` `mail.generation` before the PUT).
- `primary_domain`: the domain of every account's login and first address, one of `domains`. `mail_hostname`: `MAIL_HOSTNAME`.
- `client_ip`: `preserved` or `rewritten` (`core.env` `PORTCULLIS_MAIL_CLIENT_IP`, §2; §19.8). `submission_lan_only`: `PORTCULLIS_MAIL_SUBMISSION_LAN_ONLY` (§19.6).
- `dkim_rotate` and `former_retention`: Go durations from Settings → Mail (defaults `4320h` and `720h`; §19.9), 24h–8760h each.
- `relay`: `null` (deliver directly) or `{"host", "port", "username", "spf_include"}` (`host` a hostname, `port` 1–65535, `username` possibly empty, `spf_include` a hostname or `""`); the password is the file `relay-password` of `PORTCULLIS_MAIL_SLOT_DIR`, never in the document.
- `tls.spki_sha256`: the 1–2 SPKIs (64 lowercase hex) of the mail certificate's current and next key (§19.3); the provider's `cert` check compares what it serves with them.
- `domains[]`: every domain mail is on for, draining, or just turned off. `dmarc_start` is `reject` (no MX or SPF before Portcullis) or `none`. `dmarc_floor` (`none`, `quarantine` or `reject`) is the lowest DMARC `p=` the provider may publish: the stricter of the policy the domain's last good set published and `dmarc_start` (§19.7). `mail` is `on`, `off` or `draining` (§19.7). `dnssec` is the domain's zone state from its plan (§12.2 `dnssec.state`; for the main domain the Hub reads `GET /api/dns/main`), or `unknown`.
- `accounts[]`: the members of `mail_users` (§19.6). `username` is the LLDAP username, `uuid` the LLDAP user uuid (a person without one is left out, never sent with an empty uuid), `addresses` the primary address `<username>@<primary_domain>` first, then `<username>@<e>` for each added mail domain whose groups the person is in. `quota_bytes` ≥ 0.
- `aliases[]`: an address on a mail domain delivered to (and sendable as by) one account. `lists[]`: `<group>@<domain>`, `members` usernames that are accounts, `posting` `members` or `anyone`. `postmaster`: usernames that are accounts (the Hub sends the `lldap_admin` members who are accounts); `postmaster@` and `abuse@` of every mail domain go to them.
- `local_networks`: the Hub's Local networks (§14.7), at most 64; never "anywhere". A network inside a private or special-use block (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, `100.64/10`, `169.254/16`, `127/8`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`) may be as wide as the block; elsewhere a public IPv4 network is at most a /16 wide and a public IPv6 one at most a /32. An IPv6 network must not overlap `::ffff:0:0/96`, `::/96`, `64:ff9b::/96` or `64:ff9b:1::/48` and must lie within `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10` or `2000::/3`. Nothing is split or widened: a network outside these rules refuses the document.
- `limits`: each 1–100000. `spam`: `1 ≤ junk_score < reject_score ≤ 100`; `allow` / `block` entries are a domain or an address.
- **The provider MUST refuse** (`400`): another version; an unknown, duplicate or missing key; trailing data; an address on a domain not in `domains`; an address used twice across accounts, aliases, lists and the reserved addresses; a reserved local part (§19.6) used by an account, alias or list; a username outside LLDAP's form; a uuid that isn't a UUID; a list member or postmaster that isn't an account; a negative quota; limits, scores, durations or a relay outside the ranges above; an SPKI that isn't 64 lowercase hex.

**MailStatus** (`GET /v1/status`):

```json
{"bootstrap": true, "provider": {"name": "Stalwart", "version": "1.1.0"},
 "cert": {"not_after": "2027-02-01T00:00:00Z", "sans": ["mail.example.com"], "spki_sha256": "99ad5d8130ef75b24fa9a72e9ca7d0db45cee16a25405bdaa9d317a6d9dac9c6"},
 "dkim": [{"domain": "example.com", "algorithm": "ed25519", "selector": "v1-ed25519-20261115", "stage": "active", "since": "2026-11-15T10:00:00Z"}],
 "mtasts": [{"domain": "example.com", "mode": "testing", "since": "2026-11-15T10:00:00Z", "enforce_ready": false}],
 "dmarc": [{"domain": "example.com", "policy": "reject", "since": "2026-11-15T10:00:00Z", "proposed": null}],
 "queue": {"messages": 0, "deferred": 0},
 "restored_at": null,
 "former": [{"id": "former-6f1c2a9e-3b4d-4e5f-8a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b", "username": "alice", "since": "2026-11-10T08:00:00Z"}],
 "dns": {"example.com": "9c1f…(64 hex)", "team-b.example.org": "4b7e…(64 hex)"}}
```

`provider` repeats `GET /v1/provider`'s `name` and `version`. `cert` is the certificate the listeners serve. `dkim[].algorithm` is `ed25519` or `rsa`, `stage` `pending`, `active`, `retiring` or `retired`. `mtasts[].mode` is `testing`, `enforce`, `none` (draining) or `off`; `enforce_ready` says the `mtasts-enforce` action would be accepted now. `dmarc[].policy` is `none`, `quarantine` or `reject`, and `proposed` the next policy the promotion proposes (`quarantine` or `reject`), or `null`. `restored_at` is RFC 3339 or `null` (the last void). `former[]` are the parked accounts (§19.6), `id` the export id. `dns`: each mail domain of the accepted document (main included) → sha256 (hex) of the canonical record set `GET /v1/dns/<domain>` serves (records sorted by name, type, value, TTL); it changes whenever that set does.

### 19.6 People, addresses and mail passwords

- **Who gets a mailbox:** the members of the Hub-managed group **`mail_users`** (created by the Hub like an app's access group; rules and delegation work on it). The Hub's service account and the LLDAP `admin` user never get one.
- **Identity is the LLDAP username and uuid**, never the editable LLDAP `mail` attribute. The login is the primary address. The provider MUST key the account by uuid: a username whose uuid changed (deleted and created again) gets a fresh, empty mailbox, and the old account becomes **`former-<old uuid>@portcullis-former.internal`**.
- **Removal (MUST).** An account that leaves the document, or whose uuid changed, is never deleted at once and never bounced to: its mail passwords are destroyed first, then its login, sending and receiving are disabled, its aliases cleared, and it is renamed onto the **parking domain `portcullis-former.internal`** (never in DNS or in any `mail` set). Its old address then doesn't exist: RCPT gets `550 5.1.1`, at SMTP time (a parked account must never accept a message and bounce it later), and RCPT to any address on the parking domain is refused too. A person who comes back with the same uuid gets the account back; mail passwords are never restored. Former accounts are destroyed after `former_retention`. `./portcullis mail export <former-id>` streams one as mbox (§19.11).
- **Removal timing.** Removals (an account, an address or a list member gone since the last sent document) are sent at once and the provider MUST apply them at once; a removal that fails leaves the person removed in the provider's own state and is retried every 5 s. Additions are debounced **60 s** by the Hub. Direct LLDAP edits are caught on the evaluator's 60 s tick. A revoked mail password or a person leaving `mail_users` is refused by IMAP and SMTP within **8 s**: the Hub polls `GET /v1/state` until `applied_generation` reaches the sent one (at most 4 s) and then restarts the provider's `sessions.restart` service (§6), always: a server may keep authenticated sessions alive through the change.
- **Reserved addresses** on every mail domain: the local parts `postmaster`, `abuse`, `dmarc-reports`, `tls-reports` and `mailer-daemon`, plus every address on the parking domain. `postmaster@` and `abuse@` go to `postmaster` (§19.5); `dmarc-reports@` and `tls-reports@` are the provider's own (it reads the aggregate reports there, §19.8). Every address is unique Hub-wide across people, aliases, lists and reserved addresses: the Hub refuses a conflict with `409` naming both owners, and the provider refuses a document with one.
- **Lists:** a group made a list (§19.9) is delivered at `<group>@<domain>` to the members' primary addresses. `posting: members` (the default): port 25 refuses RCPT from outside (`550 5.7.1 only members may post`), submission admits only the list's member accounts. `anyone` accepts every sender. No archive, no subscriptions.
- **Quotas:** a group-scoped Hub setting (default 10 GiB, at most 1 TiB per row), resolved as settings are (§13.4). A person who matches several quota rows gets the **largest** of their quotas.
- **Mail passwords** are the provider's per-device credentials, created by the person only (§5.1), at most **5** active per person:
    - **What they open:** IMAPS and submission only (§19.2, P11).
    - **`allowed_ips`.** Without LAN-only, `[]` (anywhere). With `submission_lan_only`, the provider MUST restrict every mail password to the Local networks, re-applied on every accepted document so a Local-networks change reaches existing passwords; empty Local networks (loopback only, §14.7) mean `127.0.0.1/32` and `::1/128`, never an empty set. **The Hub verifies it:** after every create and every reconcile while LAN-only is on, a credential whose `allowed_ips` doesn't cover exactly the addresses of the Local networks (compared as address sets, so a provider may split a prefix) is revoked at once, and the doctor reports `mail_lan_only_unenforced` (Problem).
    - **LAN-only** (`MAIL_SUBMISSION_LAN_ONLY=true`, set only by the core CLI: `./portcullis mail enable --lan-only true` or `.env`) is enforced in two places, so neither alone is the defence: (1) `allowed_ips` (above); (2) an authentication rule on submission and IMAPS refusing a client address outside the Local networks. Both need the real client address, so under rootless Podman (`PORTCULLIS_MAIL_CLIENT_IP=rewritten`) LAN-only is refused: `./portcullis mail enable --lan-only true`, `up` and `upgrade` with `MAIL_SUBMISSION_LAN_ONLY=true` exit 1 with `LAN-only needs the real client address; rootless Podman rewrites it`. The Hub never sets it; `GET /api/mail/settings` shows the refusal (`submission_lan_only_refusal`, §19.9). If LAN-only is on while the client address is rewritten anyway, the doctor reports `mail_lan_only_unenforced`.
    - **Expiry:** none, 90 days or 1 year. **Label:** 1–64 characters on one line.
    - **Never in clear at rest** (P12): the provider stores only a hash; the plaintext exists only in the one create answer (`Cache-Control: no-store`). An account's own password is random and never disclosed: nobody signs in to the mail server interactively.
    - **Metadata** (§13.16 "Mail passwords"): `state.yaml` `mail_credentials`.

### 19.7 DNS: the `mail` set, its validation and the state machines

The provider renders each mail domain's wanted `mail` set (§12.4) on `GET /v1/dns/{domain}`, TTL 3600 unless noted. Core and the Hub write it; the provider never holds DNS credentials. `<e>` is the mail domain, `<h>` is `MAIL_HOSTNAME`.

- **Set validation.** One shared rule set: the Hub's `internal/mailprovider/dnsrules.go` and the domains service's `PUT /domains/{name}/sets/mail` (§12.2), with one vectors file (`mail_dns_vectors.json`) byte-copied between them. A record is allowed only with a name and value from this table:

    | Name | Allowed |
    |---|---|
    | `<e>` | `MX <prio> <h>.` (the target exactly `MAIL_HOSTNAME`); one TXT starting `v=spf1 ` whose terms are only `mx`, `-all` / `~all` and `include:<relay spf_include>` when the admin set one in Settings → Mail |
    | `<sel>._domainkey.<e>` (`sel` a single DNS label) | TXT starting `v=DKIM1;` |
    | `_dmarc.<e>` | TXT `v=DMARC1; …` with `p=` ≥ the domain's `dmarc_floor`, `rua` only `mailto:` addresses on `<e>`, no `ruf` |
    | `_mta-sts.<e>` | TXT `v=STSv1; id=<1–32 alnum>` |
    | `_smtp._tls.<e>` | TXT `v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:<addr on e>` |
    | `_submissions._tcp.<e>`, `_submission._tcp.<e>`, `_imaps._tcp.<e>` | `SRV <p> <w> 465/587/993 <h>.` (the port that matches the name) |
    | `_imap._tcp.<e>`, `_pop3._tcp.<e>`, `_pop3s._tcp.<e>` | `SRV 0 0 0 .` only |
    | `mta-sts.<e>`, `autoconfig.<e>`, `autodiscover.<e>` | `CNAME <h>.`, only when the Hub asked with `wildcard=false` |

    - **Never A, AAAA, CAA, NS, DS, TLSA** or any other type, and never a name outside the table: the provider can't point mail at another host, widen SPF, receive reports elsewhere, lower DMARC, or touch the CAA (`mail-cert`'s, §19.3), the TLSA and HELO SPF (core's, §19.3) or the address records.
    - **A set that fails** is dropped by the Hub, which keeps the last good one and reports `mail_records_wrong` with the reason; the domains service refuses it (`400`, the rule's text).
    - **The shape a provider renders** (the `stalwart` adapter's; any set inside the table is valid): `MX 10 <h>.`; `v=spf1 mx -all` (` include:<spf_include>` before `-all` with a relay; other TXT strings at `<e>` stay); DKIM TXT `v=DKIM1; k=ed25519; p=…` and `v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=…` (RSA-2048, written as ≤ 255-byte strings, compared as their concatenation), selectors `v1-ed25519-YYYYMMDD` / `v1-rsa-YYYYMMDD` (`-2`, … on a same-day re-rotation); `v=DMARC1; p=<policy>; adkim=s; aspf=s; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@<e>`; `_mta-sts` only while the well-known router is reachable from the internet (below); `v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@<e>`; `SRV 0 1 465|587|993 <h>.`.
- **Who writes.**
    - **Added domains:** the Hub reads `GET /v1/dns/{domain}` (with `?wildcard=false` when the domain's plan has no `*.<e>` address record) after every accepted document, whenever the domain's hash in `GET /v1/status` `dns` changes (polled every **60 s** and after every accept; a hash is recorded only after its PUT succeeded, so a failed PUT is retried), and every **6 h** as a backstop, validates it and writes it with `PUT /domains/{name}/sets/mail` (§12.2). A domain whose provider state reached `off` gets `DELETE /domains/{name}/sets/mail`.
    - **The main domain:** the CLI only (the Hub never writes it). `./portcullis dns setup --only mail` and the daily `mail rotate` read `GET /host/mail/dns/main` (`hub mail dns-main`: the validated main set plus any retiring DKIM; `409` "no mail provider is wired") and pass it into `dns-tool` as `{"sets": ["mail"], "mail": [<records>], "mail_hostname": "<MAIL_HOSTNAME>", …}` on stdin (§12.1), which adds core's TLSA and HELO SPF (§19.3). On a lego-only main domain the plan prints the records by hand (`dkim: "manual"`: one key per algorithm, no rotation, check `dkim_manual:<d>`).
    - **`MAIL_HOSTNAME`'s address:** with `PORTCULLIS_MAIL=on` (`DOMAINS_MAIL=on`), the main domain's `address` set also owns `MAIL_HOSTNAME`'s A/AAAA when it is under the main domain, whether or not a provider has sent anything (`dns.sh` always passes `mail_hostname` with the slot open): its own records stop the wildcard answering it (RFC 4592).
    - **A changed `MAIL_HOSTNAME`.** The CLI records the hostname last used in `secrets/mail/hostname`; when it differs, the old one is appended to `secrets/mail/former-hostnames`. Only those recorded former hosts are adopted by the dns tool as a former `MAIL_HOSTNAME` (its HELO SPF and TLSA removed); any other name is never touched.
    - **`mail disable` leaves** `MAIL_HOSTNAME`'s A/AAAA and its CAA pin (a known limitation): the admin may delete them by hand.
- **DKIM continuity on a switch.** For **7 days** after a switch (§19.9) the Hub keeps the old provider's DKIM TXT records (`*._domainkey.<e>`, from its last good set) in each domain's set, marked retiring (`state.yaml` `mail.retiring_dkim`), so messages signed just before the switch still verify. They are cleared per domain only after that domain's new set was written and the 7 days have passed; the doctor names a domain whose new set failed.
- **DKIM (MUST)** per domain and algorithm: `pending` (the key made, its TXT wanted) → `active` only when **both** public resolvers (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`) serve its exact TXT (a failed lookup keeps it `pending`; the previous `active` key becomes `retiring` at the same step; a failed stage change rolls back atomically) → `retired` after 7 days (the TXT is dropped) → destroyed 30 days later. Rotation every `dkim_rotate`, or at once on `dkim-rotate`. `pending` for more than 24 h is check `dkim_stuck:<d>`; the private keys never leave the provider.
- **MTA-STS (MUST)** per domain: policy `version: STSv1`, `mode`, exactly one `mx: <h>`, `max_age`; `id` changes with every policy change (the `stalwart` adapter: the first 20 hex digits of sha256(policy text) + `T<unix>`). `testing` (`max_age: 86400`) → `enforce` (`max_age: 604800`) only on `mtasts-enforce` (the doctor fix, §14.6) after 7 days of `testing` with check `cert` a definite pass and no authenticated TLS-RPT failure since `testing` began (report trust, §19.8). `enforce` goes back to `testing` only on a **known-failed local certificate check**: two consecutive definite `cert` failures at least 15 minutes apart (an unreachable listener or a timeout is unknown and changes nothing); reports never move it back. A document that says `off` without the drain goes `enforce` → `testing` for the last policy's `max_age`, then `off` (never straight off). Turning mail off for a domain makes it `draining`: only `_mta-sts` stays (a new id) and the policy says `mode: none`, for the full `max_age` of the last published policy; then the domain is `off` and the rest of the set goes (then `nomail` comes back, §12.2). The Hub learns that a drain has finished from `GET /v1/status` `mtasts[].mode` `"off"`; only then does it send `DELETE /domains/{name}/sets/mail`, report the domain `off` and drop it from the document. After a switch MTA-STS restarts at `testing` (a fresh id).
- **The Hub checks the policy.** Every 6 h the Hub fetches each mail domain's `/.well-known/mta-sts.txt` through Traefik's `websecure` entrypoint on `portcullis-proxy` (SNI and `Host` `mta-sts.<e>`; content only, the local hop's certificate chain isn't verified) and refuses a policy without exactly one `mx:` line equal to `MAIL_HOSTNAME` and `version: STSv1`: doctor `mail_records_wrong`. It is skipped while the domain's MTA-STS is `off`.
- **MTA-STS follows VPN-only mode (user ruling).** The well-known router is on `PORTCULLIS_EP_CORE` with **no public exception** (§5): in VPN mode `server` it is on `vpnsecure` only, so remote MTAs can't fetch a policy. The provider gets the same value as `PORTCULLIS_MAIL_WELLKNOWN_ENTRYPOINTS`; while it doesn't contain `websecure`, every domain's MTA-STS is `off` and no `_mta-sts` TXT is published. Mail still works: senders fall back to opportunistic TLS (and DANE, when the TLSA is published), and a policy they cached expires at its `max_age`. A draining domain then waits `max_age` from the later of the drain start and the moment the policy stopped being reachable. When `websecure` comes back, MTA-STS starts again at `testing` with a new 7-day clock. Autoconfig and autodiscover are then reachable over the VPN only.
- **DMARC (MUST):** `p=reject` from the start when the domain had no MX or SPF before Portcullis (`dmarc_start: reject`), else `p=none`. After 14 clean days (no authenticated aggregate report with a source failing both SPF and DKIM alignment) the status proposes `quarantine`, after 14 more `reject`; a proposal is applied only on `dmarc-promote` (the doctor fix), never by itself. A policy is never lowered, and never below `dmarc_floor`: **the Hub refuses a set below the floor** (above), so a switch never lowers DMARC.
- **Well-known files (MUST)** on `wellknown.port` (exact paths only, `Host` checked against the mail domains, anything else `404`): `GET /.well-known/mta-sts.txt` on `mta-sts.<e>` (`text/plain`, `Cache-Control: max-age=300`); `GET /mail/config-v1.1.xml` and `GET /.well-known/autoconfig/mail/config-v1.1.xml` on `autoconfig.<e>` (IMAP 993 SSL, SMTP 465 SSL, username `%EMAILADDRESS%`, server `<h>`); `POST /autodiscover/autodiscover.xml` on `autodiscover.<e>` (an Outlook POX answer; the request's `EMailAddress` is echoed only when it parses and is on a mail domain).

### 19.8 Checks, report trust, spam, outbound and metrics

- **Checks** (`GET /v1/checks`): every 6 h and on `?refresh=1` (one run at a time; a refresh within 60 s answers the last result). **The neutral catalog** below is fixed; any other id MUST start with `x-` (`x-[a-z0-9_]{1,40}`), and the Hub refuses an answer with any other id. `<d>` is a mail domain, `<u>` a username.

    | Id | What | Doctor kind (§14.5) |
    |---|---|---|
    | `port25` | from the provider's own delivery history only, **never a probe**: every outbound delivery of the last 24 h failed with a connect timeout or refusal across ≥ 2 distinct MX hosts and none was delivered → Problem; no delivery attempt yet → Info "no outbound delivery yet: not known" | `mail_port25_blocked` (Problem or Info) |
    | `fcrdns_v4`, `fcrdns_v6` | the PTR of each public address through the public resolvers resolves to a name that resolves back to it; when not ok, `reason` is `"missing"` (no PTR, or its name doesn't resolve) or `"mismatch"` (the PTR's name resolves elsewhere), with the hosting providers' steps. Outbound mail is IPv4 only: `fcrdns_v6` is Info at most | `mail_ptr_missing` / `mail_ptr_mismatch` by `reason`; v6 → `mail_ipv6_ptr` (Info) |
    | `blocklist` | each public address against the IP blocklists the provider uses; a residential listing says "use a relay"; a refused query is a Warning, never ok | `mail_blocklisted` |
    | `cert` | TLS on 465 / 993 and STARTTLS on 25 / 587 present `<h>`'s chain, not expired, with an SPKI in MailState's `tls.spki_sha256`. An unreachable listener or a timeout is **unknown**, never a failure; no root-store chain verification (staging certificates would always fail it) | `mail_cert_expiring` (with the CLI-reported `not_after`) |
    | `dane` | whether outbound DANE verification works: only definite verdicts count; off after **3 consecutive invalid verdicts spanning ≥ 30 min** (a Warning until then), a Problem while off, on again at the first valid verdict. Publishing our own TLSA (§19.3) doesn't depend on it | `mail_dane_off` |
    | `client_ip` | `client_ip: rewritten` → Warning | `mail_client_ip_rewritten` |
    | `dmarc_reports`, `tlsrpt_reports` | aggregate reports of the last 7 days with failures, naming the sources (report trust, below) | `mail_dmarc_failures` |
    | `records:<d>` | the provider's own view of `<d>`'s published set | `mail_records_wrong` |
    | `dkim_selftest:<d>` | each active key's public key equals the `p=` both resolvers serve | `mail_records_wrong` |
    | `dkim_stuck:<d>`, `dkim_manual:<d>` | §19.7 | `mail_dkim_stuck`, `mail_dkim_manual` |
    | `rate_held:<u>` | the account's queued messages held by the outbound limit → Warning | `mail_rate_held` |
    | `x-<name>` | provider-specific (the provider's app page lists its own) | `mail_provider_check` |

    - `title` appears only on `x-` checks (≤ 80 characters). `detail` ≤ 500 characters, at most 10 `steps` of ≤ 200 characters each, `reason` only where the table names one. The Hub clips longer text and shows it as plain text only (no links, no HTML).
    - An `x-` check's severity counts at most as Problem and it never gets a one-click fix.
- **Report trust (MUST).** DMARC and TLS-RPT aggregate reports are unauthenticated mail: anyone can send one. A report counts (to hold a progression, or to raise a doctor Problem) only when its message passed DKIM **aligned** with its From domain by the provider's own verification; reporters are told apart by the registrable domain (eTLD+1, publicsuffix) of that DKIM `d=`, never by the report's `Org`, and at least 2 independent reporters are needed before a report holds anything. Reports dated in the future or before the domain's current stage are dropped, and a report must name the domain it was sent for. Reports **never weaken** a policy: MTA-STS goes back to `testing` only on the local certificate check (§19.7), DMARC is never lowered, and failing reports only hold a progression or raise a Problem. A provider that can't authenticate reports shows them as "shown only, never acted on".
- **Spam (MUST):** the filter honours MailState `spam`: a score ≥ `reject_score` is refused at DATA with `550 5.7.1`; ≥ `junk_score` goes to Junk with `X-Spam-*` headers; the `dnsbl` switches, `allow` and `block`; remote DMARC `reject` is honoured. No external lookup beyond DNS (P18, §19.4).
- **Outbound limits (MUST):** `recipients_per_hour` and `recipients_per_day` per account hold the excess in the queue (`rate_held:<u>`), never drop it.
- **Relay (MUST):** with `relay` set, every non-local recipient goes through it (implicit TLS on port 465, else STARTTLS required), authenticated with `username` and the `relay-password` file when `username` isn't empty.
- **Rewritten client addresses (MUST, degraded mode):** with `client_ip: rewritten` (rootless Podman) SPF, iprev and the IP blocklists are off, DMARC judges on DKIM alignment only and never rejects, and the provider never bans the gateway address it sees for every client. Doctor `mail_client_ip_rewritten`.
- **Metrics.** The provider serves on `metrics.port` (Basic auth `prometheus` + `metrics-secret`): `portcullis_mail_check{check}` (0/1), `portcullis_mail_dkim_stage{domain,stage}`, `portcullis_mail_queue_messages`, `portcullis_mail_queue_deferred_ratio`; and optionally its server's own metrics on `server_metrics.port` and `.path`. Core's own `portcullis_mail_cert_expiry_seconds` comes from `mail rotate` through the textfile exporter (§19.3).
    - **Discovery.** The Hub writes `mail_slot/mail-targets.json` (file_sd), in place, on every wire, unwire and Hub start: `[]` when nothing is wired (so the generic `up == 0` alert never fires for an empty slot), else `{targets: ["mail-provider-metrics:<metrics.port>"], labels: {service: "provider"}}` and, with `server_metrics`, `{targets: ["mail-provider-server-metrics:<port>"], labels: {service: "server", __metrics_path__: "<path>"}}`.
    - **Jobs.** Prometheus jobs `mail-provider` and `mail-provider-server` keep their own entries; both use Basic auth, user `prometheus`, `password_file: /mail-slot/metrics-secret`.
    - **Alerts** (`monitoring/prometheus/alerts.yml`, names and expressions unchanged): `MailQueueHigh` (`portcullis_mail_queue_messages > 100` for 30 min, warning), `MailDeferralsHigh` (`portcullis_mail_queue_deferred_ratio > 0.2` for 1 h, warning), `MailCertExpiring` (core's textfile metric under 14 days or missing, for 10 min, warning), `MailBlocklisted` (`portcullis_mail_check{check="blocklist"} == 0` for 10 min, critical), `MailDKIMStuck` (a `dkim_stuck:*` check failing for 10 min, warning), `MailCheckFailing` (any other check failing for 1 h, warning).

### 19.9 Hub API and audit

**People routes** (§5.1): `GET /api/me/mail`, `POST /api/me/mail/passwords`, `DELETE /api/me/mail/passwords/{id}`.

**The mail provider routes** (Hub listener, proxy-secret and CSRF guards, strict JSON bodies ≤ 64 KiB). **Full administrators only** (`lldap_admin`; a delegate gets `403`), and **never from MCP or AI**: a request carrying an AI or MCP token (§15) is `403`, and there is no tool for any of them, ever.

| Route | Body | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/mail/provider` | — | The Settings → Mail header: `{"slot": "open"\|"closed", "kubernetes": <bool>, "wired": {"instance", "template", "label", "version", "wired_at", "wired_by", "mode": "void"\|"normal"\|"stopped"} \| null, "void": {"reason", "since", "error"} \| null, "held": {"reason", "since"} \| null, "candidates": [{"instance", "template", "label"}]}` (`candidates`: the installed instances of templates with a valid `mail:` block) |
| `GET /api/instances/{id}/mail-provider` | — | The instance's Mail tab: `{"wired": <bool>, "mode": "unwired"\|"void"\|"normal"\|"stopped", "provider": <GET /v1/provider> \| null, "void", "held", "refused_because": ["…"], "warning": "<the warning>", "hold_warning": "<text>"}` (`refused_because`: why wiring is refused now, `[]` when it isn't; `hold_warning` only while held). `404` for an instance whose template has no `mail:` block |
| `PUT /api/instances/{id}/mail-provider` | `{"wired", "confirm", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce", "drain"}` | Wire (`wired: true`), re-confirm a held provider (`wired: true` on the wired instance) or unwire (`wired: false`, `drain` default `true`), in the background: `202` with the op (§11.7) and the warning |
| `POST /api/mail/provider/switch` | `{"to", "confirm", "confirm_empty", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` | Switch to another installed provider instance, in the background: `202` with the op of `to` (below) |
| `POST /api/mail/provider/retry-void` | `{}` | Retry a failed void now (§19.11): `202`. While the wired provider's API secret is missing or too short (`problem` below), it first owes a void (`reason: "wire"`), which writes a fresh secret; after a core restore's hold was lifted by hand (`mail restore-hold clear`) it owes a `restore` void and is what starts the provider again. `409` "no void of the mail passwords is owed"; `409` with the hold's reason while held; `409` "a core restore of the mail provider is pending: the provider starts after `hub mail restore`" while a core restore's hold exists |

- **The warning** (exact, returned as `warning` by both GET routes, the PUT and the switch answers and `GET /host/mail/provider`, and shown by the UI and the CLI before every wiring): "This app becomes the mail server for every person and every mail domain. It gets public ports 25, 465, 587 and 993, writes the mail DNS records of every mail domain, creates and checks the mail passwords of every person in mail_users, sends mail to the internet (outbound SMTP), and can read every mailbox."
- **Wiring** (`wired: true` on an instance that isn't wired). Any installed template with a valid `mail:` block may be wired, from any source (user ruling). The guards, in this order:
    1. an AI or MCP token → `403`;
    2. not a full administrator → `403`;
    3. the fresh-auth proof (`code`, `code_verifier`, `nonce`, flat, as the Sign-in page's routes; §8 "Fresh auth", verified for the request's listener) missing, stale or invalid → `403` "a fresh sign-in is required";
    4. `confirm` isn't exactly the instance id → `400` "type the instance id to confirm";
    5. `PORTCULLIS_MAIL` isn't `on` → `409` "mail is off: run ./portcullis mail enable on the host";
    6. another instance is wired → `409` "<id> is this server's mail provider: switch instead";
    7. the runtime is Kubernetes → `409` (§19.12);
    8. the compatibility gate (§11.10) says `refused` for the listener ports → `409` with its reasons;
    9. another instance publishes 25, 465, 587 or 993 → `409` naming it;
    10. the template fails `ValidateMail` or its `api_version` is unknown → `409` with the refusal.

    Then the op `mail_wire` runs, each step saved before the next: (1) `record`: `state.yaml` `mail.provider` and `void_owed {reason: "wire"}` in one save; (2) `gate`: the API secret, the metrics secret, the relay password and the void files (§19.1); (3) `void_mode`: the void-mode override and `up`; (4) `void`: wait for `bootstrap: true` (≤ 5 min), `POST /v1/void {"reason": "wire"}` and the verification (§19.11); (5) `normal`: the normal override and `up`; (6) `document`: the first MailState; (7) `dns`: the domains' sets after the first accepted document. **Every wiring starts with a void**, so a provider that arrives with credentials from a restore, an older wiring or an imported store starts clean. Audited `mail.provider_wired` with the instance, the template, its source and commit, the block hash and the actor.

- **Template updates hold.** After every source sync the Hub recomputes the wired instance's `block_hash` (§19.1). On a change, or when the template no longer validates, it sets `mail.held {reason}` (`reason`: "the mail provider's template changed: review and confirm on its Mail tab", "the mail provider's template no longer validates: fix or update it, then confirm on its Mail tab", or "the mail provider's template source now points at another repository: unwire it and wire it again") and issues no `up`, re-render or recreate. **A hold changes no mode** (Ruling R-HH1): the running, confirmed containers keep serving in the mode they have, and keep taking every document, revocation, removal and session reset as usual; the mail routes work. **Every `up` of the wired provider is refused** while it is held or its tree on disk no longer matches the confirmed hash (Ruling R-HH3, `409` with the hold's reason): the check is in the start primitive itself, on every path (an enable, a dead container, a Hub restart's reconcile, an owed restart, the void retry, an env change, a doctor fix), so nothing of the changed tree ever starts. **Fail closed:** when the held provider can't take what the Hub must send (a document it doesn't refuse on its own, a revocation, its state), the Hub records `held.stopped` (saved before the down), stops the instance (a failed down is kept in `stop_error`, a doctor Problem, and retried), and mail stays down until the re-confirm; the routes then answer `503`. Doctor `mail_provider_refused` with the reason. An ordinary sync of unrelated templates is unaffected.
    - **Re-confirming** (`wired: true` on the held, wired instance) has every guard of wiring (an AI or MCP token, a delegate, a missing proof and a wrong typed id are refused; guards 5–10 apply as for a wiring, 6 excepted) and shows the warning plus `hold_warning`: "The template changed since you wired it. Confirming keeps every mail password and mailbox: the updated app gets them as they are." It records the new commit and block hash, clears `held`, renders the normal override and `up`. **It voids no mail password**: it is the same mailbox store. Audited `mail.provider_wired` with `reconfirm: true`. A void owed for another reason (a restore) still runs first.
- **Unwiring** (`wired: false`): guards 1 and 2 only (no proof and no typed id: it only removes powers). Audited `mail.provider_unwired`. The op `mail_unwire`:
    - **`drain: true`** (the default): every mail domain goes `draining` (§19.7), and the instance stays wired, serving the `mode: none` policies, until every domain is `off`; the Hub then finishes the unwire on its own. The Mail tab shows the wait. An unwire with `drain: false` cuts it short at any time.
    - **`drain: false`** (`--force`): every `mail` set goes now (`DELETE /domains/{name}/sets/mail`, so `nomail` comes back; the main domain's set is withdrawn by the CLI timer's next pass), and senders may bounce.
    - **Then, in order** (step `close`): every active mail password row becomes `voided` with reason `provider_changed` (audited `mail_credential.void_provider`, the count); `POST /v1/void` (best effort, at most 30 s); the API secret and `.present` are deleted, so the gate closes; the unwired override is rendered and the instance is **stopped**. Each provider call is bounded at 30 s, and the gate is closed whatever the provider answers: nothing waits forever for the provider. The instance stays installed with its data.
- **Switching** (`POST /api/mail/provider/switch`): every guard of wiring for `to` (guard 6 excepted: the old provider is the one being replaced), plus `confirm_empty` exactly `"<n> mailboxes start empty"`, `<n>` the accounts of `mail-last.json` (else `400` showing the phrase). The op `mail_switch` (on `to`'s record) runs `unwire` (the old provider's close step: no drain, the sets stay) and then the wiring steps for `to`. **Same MX:** every name stays `MAIL_HOSTNAME` and the certificate is core's, so a switch changes no MX and no TLSA: it is a cutover. The new provider's sets replace the old ones domain by domain, the old DKIM is retained 7 days (§19.7), MTA-STS restarts at `testing`, and DMARC never drops below `dmarc_floor`. People's mailboxes on the new provider start empty; the old instance is stopped with its data (the switch moves no mail). Audited `mail.provider_switched` `{from, to}`.
- **Resuming.** On start, the Hub resumes from `state.yaml`: a `void_owed` with a wired provider resumes void mode (never the normal override first, never `.present` before the verification); an interrupted `mail_wire` or `mail_switch` resumes at its first unfinished step, so a switch interrupted after the unwire never leaves both instances on the ports.
- **Stop** (§11.7): a `mail_wire` accepts Stop until its `normal` step starts; the undo closes the gate, renders the unwired override, stops the instance and clears `mail.provider` and the wiring's `void_owed`. A `mail_switch` accepts Stop only before its `unwire` step changes anything. A `mail_unwire` can't be stopped.
- **Deleting the provider.** The guarded delete (§11.4) of the wired instance is `409` "unwire it first (Settings → Mail)".

**The mail settings routes** (Hub listener, `adminOnly` unless stated, proxy-secret and CSRF guards, strict JSON bodies (unknown fields and trailing data `400`) ≤ 64 KiB):

| Route | Body | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/mail/settings` | — | `{"mail": "on"\|"off", "kubernetes": <bool>, "hostname", "primary_domain", "domains": [{"name", "enabled", "state": "on"\|"draining"\|"off", "groups"}], "spam": {"reject_score", "junk_score", "dnsbl": {"spamhaus", "spamcop", "barracuda"}, "allow", "block"}, "limits": {"recipients_per_hour", "recipients_per_day"}, "quotas": [{"group", "bytes"}], "relay": {"host", "port", "username", "spf_include", "password_set": <bool>} \| null, "dkim_rotate", "former_retention", "submission_lan_only": <bool>, "submission_lan_only_refusal": "LAN-only needs the real client address; rootless Podman rewrites it", "pending_removal": {"since", "accounts": [{"username", "uuid", "revoked"}], "confirmed"} \| null, "lists": […], "problem"?, "fresh_auth"}` (`problem`, only while the wired provider can't be managed: "Mail can't be managed: the Hub's secret for the wired mail provider is missing or too short", shown with *Retry*; `fresh_auth`: the Hub listener's fresh sign-in parameters for the proof below; `hostname` and `submission_lan_only` read-only from `core.env`; `submission_lan_only_refusal` only under `HUB_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman`; `pending_removal`: §19.5, `revoked` false while revoking that person's mail passwords failed and is retried; the relay password is never returned) |
| `PUT /api/mail/settings` | `{"primary_domain", "spam", "limits", "quotas", "relay"?, "dkim_rotate"?, "former_retention"?, "code"?, "code_verifier"?, "nonce"?}` | **A change of the relay** (its host, port, username, SPF include, or any `password`, `""` included), **of `dkim_rotate` or of `former_retention`** needs the fresh sign-in proof (`code`, `code_verifier`, `nonce`, flat, as the Sign-in page's routes; §8 "Fresh auth", a security key or YubiKey certificate, verified for the request's listener): `403` "changing the relay, DKIM rotation or former retention needs a fresh sign-in" without it, `403` "a fresh sign-in is required" for a stale or invalid one, and `403` "the relay, DKIM rotation and former retention change only in the browser, never through MCP or AI" from an AI or MCP caller. The spam settings, limits, quotas and primary domain, and a relay sent again unchanged without a password, need no proof. The primary domain is the main domain or an assignable added domain (§12.3); `1 ≤ junk < reject ≤ 100`; limits 1–100000; allow / block entries a domain or an address; quota rows an existing group and 0 < bytes ≤ 1 TiB; `relay` `null` or `{"host", "port", "username", "spf_include", "password"?}` (`password` write-only: present sets it, absent keeps it, `""` clears it; written to `hub_data/mail-relay-password` and the slot volume's `relay-password`); `dkim_rotate` and `former_retention` 24h–8760h; else `400`. Audited `mail.settings`, then a sync. Settings stay editable with nothing wired: they are sent once a provider is |
| `GET /api/mail/status` | — | `{"mail": "on"\|"off", "provider": {"instance", "label", "name", "version"} \| null, "reachable": <bool>, "status": <MailStatus> \| null, "domains": [{"name", "state"}]}` |
| `GET /api/mail/checks[?refresh=1]` | — | The provider's `GET /v1/checks` answer, as the Hub decoded and clipped it |
| `PUT /api/mail/domains/{name}` | `{"enabled": <bool>, "groups": ["…"]}` | `{name}` is the main domain or an added domain. Turning on records whether the domain had an MX or SPF before (`dmarc_start`); turning off makes it `draining` (§19.7: the MX goes after the MTA-STS `max_age`, up to 7 days). Audited `mail.domain` |
| `GET /api/directory/users/{username}/mail` | — | `{"addresses", "aliases", "passwords": [MailPasswordView]}` |
| `PUT /api/directory/users/{username}/mail` | `{"aliases": ["…"]}` | Sets the person's aliases (each on a mail domain; `409` naming the owner on a conflict). Audited `mail.alias` |
| `DELETE /api/directory/users/{username}/mail/passwords/{id}` | — | `204`: revokes one of the person's mail passwords (reason `revoked`, `revoked_by` the caller). Audited `mail_credential.revoke` |
| `PUT /api/directory/groups/{group}/mail-list` | `{"enabled": <bool>, "domain", "posting": "members"\|"anyone"}` | Makes the group a list at `<group>@<domain>`, or stops it (`409` on an address conflict). Audited `mail.list` |
| `POST /api/mail/actions/{dkim-rotate\|dmarc-promote\|mtasts-enforce}` | `{"domain"}` | The provider's action (§19.5); `202`; `409` when the provider doesn't list it in `actions`. Audited `mail.dkim_rotate`, `mail.dmarc_promote`, `mail.mtasts_enforce` |
| `POST /api/mail/confirm-removal` | `{"accounts": ["<uuid>", …], "confirm": "<pending_removal.confirm_phrase>", "code", "code_verifier", "nonce"}` | **Full administrators only** (`lldap_admin`), Hub listener, browser only (never MCP or AI: `403`), with a fresh sign-in (`403` without one or with a stale one) and the typed phrase `remove <n> mailboxes` (`remove 1 mailbox`; `GET /api/mail/settings` `pending_removal.confirm_phrase`; `400` `type "<phrase>" to confirm`, checked before the proof is spent). `accounts` must be exactly the pending set (`409` "the pending removal changed since it was shown: look again"; none: `409` "no mass removal is waiting"). `204`; the next document carries `confirm_mass_removal: true`. Audited `mail.confirm_removal` with the count and the uuids. The doctor's `mail_mass_removal_pending` fix only points here ("confirm the removal on Settings → Mail: it needs a fresh sign-in and the typed phrase"). A provider's own `mass_removal` refusal (also after a switch) becomes this pending removal; it is never dropped automatically (R-SWITCH-BASE-3). |

- **Lists in the settings.** `lists` is `[{"group": "<LLDAP group name>", "address": "<group lowercased>@<domain>", "domain": "<domain>", "posting": "members"|"anyone"}]`, sorted by `group`, `[]` when there are none (never `null`), derived from the Hub's list settings, the same ones that feed MailState's `lists` (§19.5).
- **Deleting a mail domain.** `DELETE /api/domains/{name}` (§12.3) answers `409` "turn mail off for <domain> and wait for it to finish draining first" while that domain's mail is `on` or `draining`.
- **Who.** Administrators (`lldap_admin`) hold every route. The three `/api/directory/users/{username}/mail…` routes are directory routes (both listeners): a `sign_in_help` holder who may target the person (§9.7 "Person's Sign-in routes") may `GET` (`aliases` is then `[]`) and `DELETE` a password, never `PUT`. No route creates a mail password for someone else: admins see and revoke, never create.
- **`MailPasswordView`**: `{"id", "label", "created_at", "expires_at", "last_used", "status": "active"|"voided"|"unconfirmed", "voided_reason"}` (`voided`: reset by a restore or by a provider change, `voided_reason` saying which: "reset by a restore" or "the mail server changed on <date>: create a new mail password"; `unconfirmed`: only in the admin view, for an active row while the provider can't be read: never shown as active). Both `GET /api/me/mail` and the admin view reconcile the person's rows with the provider before answering (§19.11), under a per-person mail lock shared with create and revoke (sync > person > the Hub's state lock). `id` is the Hub's row id (`m` + 16 lowercase hex, §13.16); the provider's credential ids are never exposed. Never a secret.
- **Errors.** `503` "mail isn't running right now" while `PORTCULLIS_MAIL` isn't `on`, nothing is wired, the provider is unreachable or reports `bootstrap: false`, a void is owed or the held provider was stopped (§19.9 "Template updates hold"), for every route that needs the provider; the settings routes still read and save the Hub's own state. Creating a mail password answers `503` while a void is owed, `409` "mail for <user> is still being removed: try again after the removal" while the person is pending or the provider answers `account_mismatch`, and `503` "your mailbox isn't ready yet: try again in a minute" while the mailbox isn't in the provider's applied state yet.
- **`MAIL_HOSTNAME` is reserved.** Besides the mail labels of every mail domain (§5), the Hub refuses an instance hostname equal to `MAIL_HOSTNAME` with `409` `hostname <h> is reserved for mail: it is the mail server's name`.
- **Aliases** are kept in `state.yaml` keyed by the person's uuid (`{username, addresses}`), never by username alone, and dropped when the person is deleted.
- **Audit actions** (`audit.jsonl`, §9.5): `mail.settings`, `mail.domain`, `mail.alias`, `mail.list`, `mail.dkim_rotate`, `mail.dmarc_promote`, `mail.mtasts_enforce`, `mail.confirm_removal` (the count), `mail.provider_wired` (instance, template, source, commit, block hash; `reconfirm: true` on a re-confirm), `mail.provider_unwired`, `mail.provider_switched` (`from`, `to`); `mail_credential.create` (the id and the label's length), `mail_credential.revoke`, `mail_credential.revoke_leave`, `mail_credential.void_restore` and `mail_credential.void_provider` (the count only). The host socket's actor is `host`. A mail export never passes through the Hub. Never a password, a hash, an API secret, a DKIM key or a proof.
- **MCP.** One tool, `mail_status` (§15.10). No tool creates, lists or revokes a mail password, and no tool wires, switches or unwires a provider.

### 19.10 Host control socket and the CLI

- **Host routes** (§16 "Host control socket"; actor `host`; their client is `hub mail <command>`, run by `./portcullis` inside the Hub container, which prints JSON on stdout and exits 0 on a 2xx, 1 on a refusal (the text on stderr) and 2 on a usage error):

    | Route | `hub mail …` | Does |
    |---|---|---|
    | `GET /host/mail/provider` | `provider` | `{"slot", "wired", "instance", "template", "label", "version", "void_owed", "held", "warning", "export": {"service", "argv"} \| null}` (`warning`: the warning text, always; `export`: the wired block's, for `mail export`) |
    | `POST /host/mail/install` `{"template", "source", "confirm"}` | `install` | Installs the template's default instance when no instance of it exists (else uses the existing one), then wires it as §19.9 does, with `confirm` the instance id. The host operator's typed confirmation stands in for the fresh sign-in: the CLI prints the warning and asks for the instance id; `--yes` accepts it. `202` `{"op_id", "op", "instance", "poll"}`; the client waits for it (`hub mail op`) |
    | `POST /host/mail/install/preview` `{"template", "source"}` | `install-preview` | Changes nothing: `{"instance", "creates"}`, the instance `install` would wire (whose id the typed confirmation must be) and whether it would create it (no instance of the template yet: its default instance, id = the template id). `400` "invalid template id" or "source is required"; `404` "no template <t> from source <s>" |
    | `POST /host/mail/unwire` `{"drain": <bool>}` (`drain` default `true`) | `unwire` | Unwires the provider (§19.9): `202` `{"op_id", "op", "instance", "poll"}`; `409` "no mail provider is wired" |
    | `GET /host/mail/op?instance=<i>&op_id=<o>` | `op` (stdin `{"instance", "op_id"}`, both required, unknown keys refused) | The op's record (§11.7: `op`, `op_id`, `instance`, `running`, `ok`, `error`, …); `404` "no operation recorded". The CLI polls it every `MAIL_OP_POLL` s (default 2) until `running` is `false`, at most `MAIL_OP_WAIT` s (default 1800; a core restore's provider restore `MAIL_RESTORE_WAIT`, default 21600), and succeeds only when `ok` is `true` and the record is the op it started |
    | `POST /host/mail/action` `{"name", "domain"}` | `action` | One of the provider's actions (`dkim-rotate`, `dmarc-promote`, `mtasts-enforce`) |
    | `GET /host/mail/status` | `status` | The Hub's view: the provider, the document's generation and applied generation, the checks, the void and hold state |
    | `GET /host/mail/dns/main` | `dns-main` | `{"records": […], "rules": {"relay_include", "dmarc_floor", "draining"}}`: the validated main set plus any retiring DKIM (§19.7), and the shared rules' inputs for the main domain (the relay's SPF include, the DMARC floor, whether the domain drains), which the CLI passes to `dns-tool` as `mail_rules` to check the set again; `409` "no mail provider is wired" |
    | `POST /host/mail/tls` `{"spki_sha256", "not_after"}` | `tls` | §19.3 |
    | `POST /host/mail/test` `{"to"}` | `test` | The provider's `POST /v1/actions/test`: `{"queue_id"}` |
    | `POST /host/mail/backup` | `backup` | `{"archive": "<instance>/<timestamp>.tar"}` (§19.11) |
    | `POST /host/mail/restore` `{"archive"}` | `restore` | Restores the provider instance from that archive (§19.11): `202` `{"op_id", "op", "instance", "poll"}`, waited for with `hub mail op`. The route first waits for the instance's app lock (up to 2 min, `HostLockWait`), so `hub mail restore`'s socket client allows the lock wait plus 3 min (5 min) |
    | `POST /host/mail/drain` | `drain` | `202` `{"domains": [{"name", "state"}]}`: every mail domain becomes `draining` (audited `mail.domain`) |
    | `GET /host/mail/domains` | `domains` | `200` `[{"name", "state": "on"\|"draining"\|"off"}]` |

- **The CLI:**
    - `./portcullis mail enable [--hostname H] [--lan-only true|false] [--provider stalwart|none] [--yes]` (idempotent) refuses on Kubernetes (§19.12), with a DNS provider Portcullis can't write, with `MAIL_IPV6` in `.env` (any value: `MAIL_IPV6 isn't supported yet: remove it from .env`; `up` and `upgrade` refuse it too), LAN-only under rootless Podman (§19.6), and, on rootless Podman, unless `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start` ≤ 25 (`net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start = <n>: mail publishes ports 25, 465 and 587 (sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=25, and keep it in /etc/sysctl.d/; unprivileged users may then bind 25-79)`). It opens the slot (§19.1), then, unless `--provider none`, installs and wires the provider (`hub mail install`, default `stalwart` from the default source), and prints the DNS step.
    - `mail disable [--yes] [--force]` unwires through the host socket (`drain` unless `--force`; the exact `409` "no mail provider is wired" counts as already unwired) and waits for the unwire op to end. It doesn't wait for the drain: unless `--force`, it reads `hub mail domains`, and while any domain isn't `off` it says so and returns ("Run ./portcullis mail disable again once ./portcullis mail status says every domain is off."), the slot left open. Re-run once every domain is `off` (with `--force`, at once), it withdraws the main domain's mail set, then writes `PORTCULLIS_MAIL=off`. The networks, `mail_slot` and `mail_provider_slot` stay.
    - `mail status [--json]` (and the "Mail" block of `./portcullis status`, `--json` key `mail`) shows `hub mail status` plus core's own rows: the certificate, the timer, the TLSA state, the client-address mode; it exits 1 on a problem.
    - `mail test --to <address>` (`hub mail test`: a message from the first postmaster account, signed by the primary domain's DKIM keys), `mail dkim rotate <domain>` (`hub mail action`), `mail cert`, `mail rotate [--next-key]` (§19.3), `mail schedule --systemd [--out DIR]`, `mail export <former-id> [--out FILE]` (§19.11).
    - `mail restore-hold clear [--yes]` removes a core restore's hold `hub_data/mail-restore-pending` (§19.11) after the operator typed `clear` (`--yes`: no prompt), and logs it (stdout and the system log, with the archive's name). Nothing else ever removes the file but the Hub's successful `hub mail restore`. Lifting the hold starts nothing: the provider stays stopped until an administrator's *Retry* (§19.9), which voids first, and then runs on what its volumes hold now, which may be empty.
    - **The CLI execs into no mail container** except for `mail export`.

### 19.11 Backups, restores, the void and export

- **The CLI lock.** `up`, `down`, `upgrade`, `restore`, `backup` and `mail enable|disable|rotate|cert` run one at a time (an exclusive `flock` on `<checkout>/.portcullis.lock`, held for the process's life, shared with the backup and mail timers; `--help` never locks). A second one says "Waiting for another ./portcullis command (a backup or mail timer?) to finish...", waits `PORTCULLIS_LOCK_WAIT` seconds (default 1800), then refuses.
- **Backup.** The provider's mail store lives in its instance volumes, so it is backed up by a **Hub instance backup** (§11.5), which stops the instance during the copy. `./portcullis backup` calls `POST /host/mail/backup` (`hub mail backup`): an instance backup of the wired provider with the reason `core`, waited for. It records the archive's name in the core backup's manifest and then archives `hub_data`, which contains it, so one `./portcullis backup` holds the mail store. While a void is owed or the provider is held, the instance comes back in void mode (or stays stopped), never normal. `mail_acme` and `mail_tls` stay in core's online volume archives. On Docker and Podman only.
- **Restores void every mail password before any mail port listens** (M7):
    - **an instance restore of the provider** (§11.6): the Hub owes a void (`void_owed {reason: "restore"}`) before the volumes are replaced;
    - **a core restore** (`./portcullis restore`) first stops the Hub and takes down the wired provider explicitly, before anything changes (Ruling X-H2: the Hub's wired instance and every compose project with a container mounting `portcullis_mail_provider_slot` or `portcullis_mail_tls`, volumes kept; an engine it can't list, a container outside a compose project or a failed down refuses the restore with nothing restored; the stopped projects are reported at the restore's end: "The mail provider (<projects>) was taken down for the restore: the Hub starts it again only after restoring it from the backup (above); else from its instance page."). It empties `hub_secrets` as always and `mail_provider_slot` with it, which removes the gate sentinel and the API secret; the Hub's secrets-epoch mismatch (§11.6) owes a void with the slot open. When the backup's manifest names a provider archive (`mail_provider_archive`), core always restores the provider instance from it, whether its volumes survive or not (the whole server goes back to the backup), **before** any other start: it writes `hub_data/mail-restore-pending` (`0600`, the Hub's uid, the archive's name and a newline) so the Hub holds the provider (no void's `up` can create empty volumes meanwhile), starts the Hub alone, and calls `POST /host/mail/restore` (`hub mail restore`), waited for to its op's end, which owes a void too. A Hub start that finds the wired provider running while the hold exists takes it down at once, before the host socket serves (defence in depth; the engine unreadable: down anyway), unless `hub mail restore`'s op is running; only then does the rest of the stack start. A successful restore removes the hold. A failed one keeps it, may be retried with the same archive, and makes `./portcullis restore` end with exit 1 naming `./portcullis mail restore-hold clear` (never "Restore complete"); with the slot closed on the restoring host the provider isn't restored and the restore says so;
    - **a wiring** owes a void (§19.9).
- **The void, while one is owed** (`state.yaml` `mail.void_owed`, saved before anything else, then `void-pending` and a fresh `void-session` written, then `.present` removed):
    1. The Hub never renders the normal override; it renders **void mode** (§19.1).
    2. It starts the instance, waits for `bootstrap: true` and calls `POST /v1/void {"reason"}`. The provider MUST destroy every credential of every account and record `restored_at`.
    3. **The Hub then verifies** (P8): it lists `?uuid=` for every account of `mail-last.json` and every uuid in its `mail_credentials` rows, revokes any credential it finds, and lists again. Any credential left, or any list error, is a failed void.
    4. On success it writes `.present`, deletes `void-session` and `void-pending`, and clears `void_owed`; then the normal override follows.
    5. On failure it stops the instance and keeps `void_owed`: doctor `mail_void_pending` (Problem). The Hub retries every **5 min** and on *Retry* (`POST /api/mail/provider/retry-void`). While a void is owed it refuses to create mail passwords (`503`).
- **The Hub's rows follow.** On every `GET /v1/credentials` for a person (the person's own view and the admin view reconcile before answering), at start for everyone, and whenever `GET /v1/status` `restored_at` is later than its last full reconcile (checked at start and every 60 s), an active metadata row with no matching live credential becomes `void_restore` when `restored_at` is later than the row's `created_at` (audited `mail_credential.void_restore`, the count only), else `missing` (logged); expired rows become `expired`. A row is ended only when it was created before the live list was read (one snapshot), so a credential created meanwhile is never ended, and only on the provider's word (a `204`, or its absence from the live list), never on a missing uuid. A person sees "reset by a restore".
- **Export (M5).** `./portcullis mail export <former-id> [--out FILE]` asks the Hub for the wired instance (`GET /host/mail/provider`), runs the block's `export.argv` (its `{former_id}` replaced) as an exec in `export.service` and writes stdout, an mbox, `0600` under `backups/mail-export/`. A provider without `export` says it has none (exit 1). It is the only path that reads message content: CLI only, **never through the Hub**. The provider MUST refuse a non-former id (a non-zero exit) and clean up whatever access it granted itself for the export, also on error.

### 19.12 Kubernetes

Mail isn't available on Kubernetes. Under `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=kubernetes`, `./portcullis mail enable` exits 1 with `mail isn't available on Kubernetes yet (Docker or rootless Podman only)`, the Hub refuses to wire a provider (`409`, §19.9) and shows Settings → Mail read-only. The chart has no mail slot objects: `tests/k8s_parity_deltas.yaml` lists them (`mail slot: Docker/Podman only (mail provider plan)`).
